Analog Heat: not listed
projects.version: v0.10.0 (tag 2026-11-09): ships each device's newest core (DT1 4.1, DN1 5.2.1, DT2 1.0, DN2 0.3, AR2 0.11, A4 0.5, OT 0.8, MC 0.3, MS 0.1). main since: DT1 core 4.2/4.3 and DN1 5.3 (live-note and MIDI CC events), core-dn2 0.4 (MIDI CC event, DSP post words), core-ar2 0.12 (spare table entries for +Drive mods), SDK mono machines and MIDI CCs, DT2 sharc_raw (raw section-7 loads and relocatable DSP objects); 2026-11-11 the Analog Rytm MKII Drive Loader (drive-loader-ar2 0.4: mods linked from the +Drive at boot, a MODS page, the web page's +Drive view over Web MIDI) and core-a4 renamed core-a4mk2; 2026-11-13 (main): Analog Rytm MKI 1.74 (ELE2 files, experimental, whole builds only, no core yet), core-ot 0.40 (Octatrack events and tables 0.9-0.40) and seqrows-ot 0.1
projects.tested_note: machine-pages 1.2, fxkit and the cores ran on units (shop notes); a stock Rytm MKI 1.74 repacked by its ELE2 writer was flashed, booted, played and restored over USB and DIN (DEVICES.md, I102)
projects.contains: the mod shop (catalog.json in elekloader/shop, b3d687d, 2026-11-09; moved out of the main repo on 2026-11-08): 170 mod files from 38 repos, each repo listed here as its own entry; base mods machine-pages (Digitakt), machines and fxkit (Digitone)
projects.notes: Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1).

projects.notes: 2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10).

projects.notes: Windows standalone builder (portable, no Python/Git/WSL needed) that takes the user's own official OS file, identifies it by SHA-256, writes the patched .syx; the user installs it with Elektron Transfer. The builder never connects to the instrument and never flashes. Adds two random-loop LFO waveforms on all three LFOs: DV-F (WAVE 7, free-running) and DV-T (WAVE 8, read position resets on track trigger); MODE = 2/4/8/16/32 steps; SPH = randomness (0 new values each step, 64 locks values and order, 127 keeps values but reorders, in between blends); stock WAVE 0-6 stay on stock paths. v0.2.0-beta adds a ONESHOT waveform zoom (encoder C cycles 1x, 2x, 3.75x, turning C pans; only in the combined 1.17 edition). Hardware: all three outputs validated on a physical unit for normal boot and operation, described by the author as beta evidence, not exhaustive. Open: broad MIDI / sequencer / transport / sync regression, save-reload-power-cycle persistence, long-duration stability. Unsigned .exe (SmartScreen warns). Repo: docs/INSTALLATION.md and docs/RECOVERY.md, windows-builder/, src/dv/ (host model), coldfire/ (DV, routing, trampoline, startup-allocation source), research/ (byte-backed findings), tools/midisniff.py (passive SysEx capture, does not transmit). Evidence ladder used by the author: SOURCE/STATIC, HOST, SYNTHETIC UNICORN, NATURAL EMULATED, HARDWARE. MIT, 7 commits, 4 stars. Credits: Marbles (concept only), Bezronczek's Syntakt Firmware Workbench (behavioural reference), ElekLabs digikit (research tooling, not bundled), elektron-firmware-tool (vendored). 2026-11-06: a second package, the Digitakt II Sample Editing Pack (OS 1.17, Windows builder): Universal Zoom (up to 64x), SmartSlice (automatic slice points), SampleLAB (load or record, chop, trim, audition, save copies) and CFADE (cross-fade at the SLICE loop wrap). projects.name: DN2 DT2 firmware research
projects.author: armio
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.11 (target) + Digitakt II OS 1.16 (donor); both official files supplied locally
projects.version: R027 candidate (2026-11-12): adds SEM, a seventh filter type (Oberheim-style state-variable model from Faust: low-pass, notch, high-pass, band-pass) with its response drawn on the FILTER page; browser build only; R025 stopped the right effects chain running for every voice. R022 (2026-11-06): working-project sample autosave and sampler SYN-page routing fixes; native replay passed, hardware confirmation pending; includes R020 cold-start guard and R013 FORMAT SAMPLES; an iPhone USB freeze is unresolved; R012 remains the stable target
projects.tested_note: README (2026-11-12): R012 confirmed on hardware; R027 owner-tested, not instrumented, USB audio untested since R023/R024 broke it (I74); R021/R022 fixes still pending hardware confirmation
projects.features: ["six Digitakt II sample machines: ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE", "mono and stereo samples with waveform views", "slice editing and slice grids", "recorder: record and resample, normalise, trim, save", "sample manager for the +Drive", "class-compliant multichannel USB audio", "SEM filter: low-pass to notch to high-pass, plus band-pass"]
projects.notes: Source-only recipes for Digitone II firmware with six Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE), stereo samples, sample browsing, DT2 parameter graphics and SLICES trig mode. Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment; VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Class-compliant USB audio provides 42 capture channels at 48 kHz/24 bit (MAIN, tracks 1-16, DELAY, REVERB, CHORUS, INPUT as stereo pairs) and a stereo return. R012 needs only the official DN2 1.11 and DT2 1.16 OS files; silent compatibility data replaces the private sample bank, and users load their own playable samples afterward. Native and browser builders verify exact inputs and the output: 2,563,872 bytes, SHA-256 4a2742a4...63a3a9a. The browser builds locally without uploading files; neither builder flashes the instrument. No firmware images or samples are distributed. Historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still require their original private sample bank. R011 fixed USB publication stalling after project changes by selecting its candidate destination from current DMA START while preserving ownership checks; R012 retains that fix. Owner-confirmed stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio on R012, including after project changes. Stable does not mean exhaustive validation: exact trimmed-file comparison, full Recorder-source coverage, endurance and end-to-end USB latency remain unverified. Builds on dnfw (angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore), selache, digikit and elektron-firmware-tool. AGPL-3.0-or-later. 2026-11-03: README warns new users NOT to install R012 yet. R012 mounts an existing sample filesystem but does not create one on a DN2 that never had it; symptoms are 0% Free / 0 bytes in Transfer, stalled uploads, Connection failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects; at that point an on-device formatter was still in development. R013 subsequently added FORMAT SAMPLES with erase confirmation; formatting, restart, capacity and post-format uploads were checked on the owner's unit. Owner testing of R012 had used storage prepared during development. An earlier track-2 saved-project reload report was an unsaved checkpoint; R022 addresses a separate, reproduced failure to refresh the sample table in the unsaved working-state backup. This does not establish recovery from an interrupted write or USB freeze.

projects.features: ["CMI machine: one sample played by eight voices from track 1", "forward, reverse and ping-pong loops with hold or sustain looping; LOOP and LOOP END snap to zero crossings", "RETRO dial: 16 bit 48 or 44.1 kHz, or 8 bit at 32 to 8 kHz", "stereo spread; released notes ring on and their voices switch off once silent", "TIME engine: sixteen single cycles cut from the sample, stepped or crossfaded", "waveform page with the playhead of the latest held note", "CPU meter in the title bar"]

Conflicts with Digi Poly, dt8poly, DIGISLICER, Digi EQ and Digi Matrix (same patch sites or sound slots). Kits saved with CMI load that track as ONESHOT on the stock OS. The author names Claude as coding assistant. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-12. 2026-11-12 (0.19-0.26): the meter shows the whole audio engine's peak load; on the unit it read about 85 % right after boot, and the author's instruction count in digiemu puts about 98 % of that in the stock render, so the UI gets what is left. Projects saved with 0.14-0.22's RETRO switch on open at 8 bit 8 kHz. 2026-11-14 (0.27-0.37): the envelope value 0.26 used to end voices (core export fw_amp_env) is the filter envelope and cut sounding notes on the unit; 0.30 reads the real amp envelope found by disassembly (S20). projects.name: digikit
projects.author: Em D (GitHub m-dwyer); develops in the ElekLabs organisation repo
projects.own_mods: [{"name": "PLUCK", "path": "modules/machines/pluck", "tested": "unit", "note": "Digitakt II, OS 1.17; Digitone II emulator only", "what": "Plucked-string synth machine (decay, pick position, brightness, colour), loaded at run time"}, {"name": "Frequency shifter", "path": "modules/fx/freqshift", "tested": "emulator", "what": "Shifts every frequency by the same number of Hz, as a send effect or master insert"}, {"name": "bootscreen", "tested": "unit", "note": "one Digitakt II 1.17 (finding 117); Digitone II emulator only", "what": "Loadable boot screens (.dkbs files) in place of the stock intro"}, {"name": "Overdrive curves", "path": "modules/core/adapters/overdrive", "tested": "emulator", "note": "Digitakt II 1.17, patched into the image; SHARC emulator only", "what": "OVR ROUTING becomes OVR TYPE: pre or post times eight curves (stock, TNH4, HARD, SOFT, TUBE, FOLD, FUZZ, SQR), and the top of the OVERDRIVE range drives harder"}, {"name": "Fast USB", "path": "modules/tools/usb-fast", "tested": "unit", "note": "2026-11-14: the take-over from USB AUDIO/MIDI was deleted after I80; in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode an added bulk OUT endpoint (core/usb-bulk-audio, interface 5 on EP2 OUT, replies over SysEx, optional patch set device-audio-bulk) ran on a DN2 and a DT2 on 2026-11-13; Windows stays on SysEx. Earlier: Digitone II 1.12 and Digitakt II 1.17, 2026-11-11; from USB AUDIO/MIDI mode through a take-over to USB MIDI and back (hardware handover); in the standard device patch set since 2026-11-11, on the DT2 with a fast +Drive close; the take-over from USB AUDIO/MIDI lost a Digitakt II from USB until a power cycle in cycle 5 of 20 and, with a hold and PHY fix, cycle 11 (I80), so since 2026-11-13 it is off by default: a unit in USB AUDIO/MIDI stays on SysEx, and USB MIDI mode was fully reliable", "what": "Sends samples to the unit over an added USB bulk interface instead of SysEx: an 8 MB file at 3.9 MB/s on a Digitone II against 0.68 MB/s over SysEx; falls back to SysEx when the link fails"}, {"name": "TB303", "path": "modules/machines/tb303", "devices": ["digitakt-2"], "tested": "emulator", "note": "checked against a Python model on the emulated SHARC; about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block", "what": "Run-time machine porting the Open303 bass-line synth (MIT)"}]
projects.base_os: Digitakt II target 1.17 (emulator also runs 1.16 as default file; 1.15C kept for old analysis); Digitone II target 1.12 (also runs 1.11 as default file; 1.10E kept for old analysis)
projects.tested_note: README (2026-11-10): digikit has run on a real Digitakt II (OS 1.17: runtime, PLUCK, bootscreen per finding 117); the Digitone II only in the emulator; Frequency shifter, Overdrive curves and TB303 emulator only. 2026-11-11: Fast USB (a vendor bulk interface) ran on a Digitone II (OS 1.12) and a Digitakt II (OS 1.17) after a fix found on the DN2 (I70); 2026-11-11 also from USB AUDIO/MIDI mode by a take-over, with throughput ceilings measured on both units (findings 123-124)
projects.contains: modules (README table, 2026-11-09): PLUCK (plucked-string machine), Frequency shifter (FX), bootscreen (loadable boot screens, .dkbs); 2026-11-10 also Overdrive curves (core adapter) and TB303 (run-time machine, DT2); plus the digikit runtime they load through
projects.notes: Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable.

projects.author: gdeo607

projects.features: ["shared base that the Digi2 machine mods need", "adds room for new machines, parameters and DSP voices; changes nothing on its own"]
projects.notes: Base mod for gdeo607's Digitakt II machine mods; on its own it changes nothing. It keeps irpina's core 1.0 hook bus and adds digikit's machine, parameter and DSP-inline frameworks as core services: added machine types 7-23 and parameter codes 275-338, DSP voices as relocatable objects placed in free DSP L2, a second SRC page with four saved, p-lockable controls (stored in the sound record's spare slots 77 and 78; such projects still load on the stock OS), and since 2.6 a pattern service that reads and edits trigs and locks through the firmware's own editors. Building needs an elekloader with `sharc_raw` support for the Digitakt II (a branch of gdeo607's elekloader fork, proposed upstream). Do not flash 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6: they crash the unit at boot (I67).

projects.version: v0.53 PAGES (tag, 2026-11-13): FLEX REC's page LEDs follow its own page; a switch to FLEX sets trig LEN to INF; BUF snaps buffer to buffer and BUF locks now pick the buffer a trig plays (I87); PLAY two detents a mode; FUNC + turn moves R.LEN a bar. v0.52 MUTE (tag, 2026-11-12): FLEX's MUTE SRC takes the source track out of the mix (level and sends) while FLEX still records it; the RECORDER's R.LEN counts steps at the pattern's scale. v0.51 LIGHTER (tag, 2026-11-12): Monomachine and Machinedrum machines no longer bit for bit, held to the originals' level and octave bands instead (DSP cost SID -64 %, DDRW -43 %, DENS -40 %, VO-6 -9 %, TRX-CY -33 %, TRX-MA -26 %), so more voices play before the guard drops one; FLEX settings per track, CLEAR BUF, sample TUNE plays its fine values. v0.50 LEVEL (tag, 2026-11-12): FLEX takes of a track at the track's level (v0.49's were about 7 dB low), GAIN on REC SETUP (-24..+38 dB) with a level meter, BUF fixed (v0.44-v0.49 could play the wrong buffer) and C BUF on REC SETUP, smaller fixes from a tester; the release gate runs about 20x faster on its longest steps. v0.49 FLEX (tag, 2026-11-11): FLEX, a live-buffer machine with recorder trigs, replaces BOUNCE (8 buffers; record a track, IN or MAIN); the DSP guard renders sample voices first and keeps a dropped one stopped until its next note; STRT/LEN/LOOP no longer move a sounding note. v0.48 FINE (2026-11-10): STRT/LEN/LOOP as the Digitakt II's fine controls (0.00-120.00, the DSP plays from the exact point); THRES fixed; KEYBOARD kept through grid recording; SLICE keys as on the DT2; BOUNCE's code removed (old projects load, the track silent). Next: v0.49 FLEX (a live-buffer machine replacing BOUNCE) and a guard that renders sample voices first. v0.47 TUNED (2026-11-09): Monomachine TUNE reads -64..+63 and FUNC+turn steps a semitone; TRIM preview 6 dB quieter; BOUNCE taken out of MACHINE SEL (old BOUNCE tracks still load). v0.46 KEEPER (11-09): recordings also copied to +DRIVE > RECORDED, names up to 35 characters. v0.45 ROOMIER (11-08): BOUNCE freeze fixed, +Drive library 16,384 samples, SELECT UNUSED, PING filter removed. v0.44 (11-07) withdrawn after it froze units (I65). Gate: CLEARED TO FLASH.
projects.tested_note: gated in the emulator (v0.48 adds a first gate step with ColdFire and DSP emulated together); units ran v0.44-v0.47: v0.44 froze (I65), BOUNCE recorded nothing or never played back (I66), a user's v0.47 dropped a sample voice block by block under load (I71); v0.48's fine controls and v0.49's FLEX are not verified on hardware (release notes); a user's old project silenced every track on v0.48 (I73, not reproduced); v0.50's track level is calibrated only in the emulator, which has no master path, and testers are asked to report the GAIN that matches; v0.51's lighter machines and v0.52's MUTE SRC are not verified on hardware (release notes); v0.53 fixes two faults a tester saw on a unit with v0.52 (BUF locks ignored, page LEDs stuck), gated in the emulator
projects.features: ["Digitakt II sample machines: ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE", "sample browser and recorder", "PERC: 34 Machinedrum machines (TRX, EFM, GND, P-I)", "Monomachine voices, polyphonic: SID 6581, DPRO WAVE, DDRW, DENS, VO-6", "FLEX: live-buffer machine with recorder trigs (record a track, the input or the main mix), with GAIN and a level meter", "CPU guard that keeps the unit responsive"]
projects.notes: Adds Digitakt II sample machines (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE) with sample browser and recorder, PERC (34 Machinedrum machines incl. TRX, EFM, GND, P-I), Monomachine voices (SID 6581, DPRO WAVE/DDRW/DENS, VO-6) and a CPU guard. Browser-based patcher builds from the user's own files ("nothing is uploaded") and saves only if the output sha256 matches a build that passed scripts/ship_gate.py. Hardware: README says verification is pending per version; FIRMWARE.md says nearly every v0.21-v0.33 entry was checked in emulators and "not seen on hardware yet". Main open problem: DSP time (heavy voices cut sound). Flashing a 1.12 unit takes it back to a 1.11 base, projects saved under the newer OS may not open. 1,491 commits, 8 stars, AGPL-3.0-or-later. FIRMWARE.md says built firmware is kept on the repo's `builds` branch (not main) - unlike most projects here, which only ship patchers; we link only to the repo and docs, not to builds. Withdrawn builds: v0.4-v0.7 (oversized image). v0.38 (2026-11-02): Direct Jump state kept in its own +Drive sector (0x6FF000); per-project sample lists at +Drive 0x6D0000-0x6E02FF, two checked copies each. Root cause of the silent new samples: the DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count, and live adds did not update the count. v0.39 (2026-11-03): recordings had kept only ~2 ms since v0.38 because the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as source, channel and threshold, and v0.38 sent a check command at every take's start; now only the recorder's own commands set them.

projects.name: digitone-2-modding-skill
projects.author: complex-ping
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.11 (user supplies the .syx; repo gives a SHA-256 prefix to check it)
projects.notes: Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; install with `npx skills add`) for developing Digitone II firmware mods: ColdFire MAIN OS patching in C, SHARC DSP audio code, verification in two emulators (digikit + a whole-DSP SHARC emulator), rebuild/re-sign/flash over USB. Encodes stock-firmware addresses, hook sites, the ColdFire-to-DSP frame format, free memory and "hardware rules the emulators cannot check, which each once silenced a real unit" - read on 2026-10-31 via SKILL.md and references/*.md (SKILL.md has 20 rules incl. whole 32-byte boot blocks, stock encodings only, no L2 above 0x200B0000, never read unwritten DDR, 2 MiB image / section 7 under 1 MiB, stop after two failed flashes; scripts include hwrules.py, shapecheck.py, encodecheck.py, bootblocks.py, sim.py/simc.py, cfmod.py, rpc_flash.py). Facts and rules are folded into hardware/devices/digitone-2-os111-reference.md and hardware/common/agent-workflow.md. Note: tree pages are blocked for our fetcher by robots.txt; the blob pages were readable. Examples: double_time (sequencer clock hook), track_trim (-6 dB on track 1). Needs Python 3.11+, dnfw, m68k GCC, digikit. MIT (digikit-derived files GPL-2.0), 2 commits, 10 stars. Overtone was built with it. Closest existing relative of this repo's hardware/ folder.

projects.name: digi-roll-studio
projects.author: zooloo303

projects.notes: Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete.

Not supported: chords, track-default rewriting, condition/probability/micro timing/retrig, non-destructive editing. Length encoding per README: inherit = 0xFF, explicit INF = 0x7F, finite 0x00..0x7E. 47 commits, licence not shown.

projects.name: elk-herd
projects.author: mzero
projects.notes: "Elektron device manager". Browser app in Elm for Digitakt and Digitakt II content over Web MIDI: whole-project transfer to and from device and files, reordering of patterns, sample pool and sound pool, renaming (altstrument 2026-11-03; development continues off GitHub, we do not link the new source location). Other projects call it the de-facto public documentation of Elektron's SysEx protocol (digi-roll-studio) and port its 7-bit SysEx codec and F0 00 20 3C framing (SYXGRID). BSD-2-Clause per those projects. The GitHub page is a stub: README says the project has migrated away from GitHub to an obfuscated address (not decoded by us) and that issues and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected - do not open AI-generated ones. Device support is not stated on the stub; SYXGRID says elk-herd does not support the Digitone family; the Digitakt II entry is an inference from digi-roll (which ports its protocol for DT2/DN2). 70 stars.

Each mods/<name>/patch.json lists the patch location, a hash of the expected original bytes and the new bytes; tools/build/build.py refuses the wrong OS, overlapping patches and protected sections. tools/emu is a ColdFire emulator (Unicorn + EMAC model); every mod is tested there before flashing. A git hook (tools/hooks) blocks firmware files from commits - a practice worth copying. README: seven mods running on real hardware (v0.8.0); RECOVERY.md exists. projects.name: syntakt-machine45-research

Claims: a distinct MAIN raw ID 45 and menu/metadata edits confirmed by static analysis; mapping of public ID 45 to compact selector 45 and implementation family e12 "strongly supported"; entering/leaving the machine, Sound-lock precedence and the p-lock lifecycle not verified end-to-end; arbitrary native DSP installation blocked/unproven; docs/DSP_ABI.md describes eight raw controls. Explicitly makes no claim of a hardware-working new Machine; the original private candidate is frozen. Files: MACHINE45_TECHNICAL_HANDOFF.md, EVIDENCE_INDEX.md (refers to a private 803-file census), docs/FROZEN_BASELINE.md, docs/PUBLICATION_POLICY.md. Excludes firmware images, opcode/disassembly dumps, coefficient tables, binary diffs and deployable packages. MIT. Meant to complement SyntHack OS and SY FM4 (FM4 extends machine 4; this concerns ID 45).

projects.name: DNX
projects.author: NoiseAndMatter
projects.base_os: no OS versions stated; Digitone II product id 0x15
projects.notes: Browser tools (Web MIDI, Chromium only, nothing uploaded) for Digitone and Digitone II projects: Expander (each sound-locked Digitone 1 sound gets its own track on the Digitone II), Manager (move/copy/swap/clear/rename patterns across banks with undo; Insights: polymeter, PATTERN RESET cost, voice use), Library (browse/search/rename the 2,048 +Drive presets; wavetables need Digitone II with "Waverider" firmware), Backup (whole +Drive into one .dnx with a manifest; excludes global settings), Probe (read-only identification and traffic capture) and CLI commands (project, plan, convert, copy, rearrange, rename, track, rebuild, diff, sheet; dry run by default). Write safeguards: WRITE switch must be armed, copy of current contents saved first, every write read back and compared, destinations checked against a fresh listing, never writes the loaded project, never converts a DN2 preset to DN1; close Transfer and Overbridge first (shared MIDI ports). Formats: .dnprj (DN1) and .dn2prj (DN2) projects, sound banks .syx; payloads LZ4-compressed inside a ZIP; SysEx uses 8-in-7 MSB-first. Author discloses LLM use; AGPL-3.0-or-later, TypeScript, 15 stars, created 2026-09-07. Not firmware modding. Report button opens a prefilled GitHub issue. 2026-11-10 (docs/KNOWN-ISSUES): an unpaged LIST of a 256-entry table store came back cut at about 4 KB with garbage after entry 125; listings are now paged in 64s (HYPOTHESES H23).

projects.author: algonormative
projects.notes: MCP control plane with 32 tools so a coding agent can operate a Rytm MKII (patterns, kits, scenes, songs) with validated SysEx deltas. MIT. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-02; README start read.

projects.name: DigiPrism

Four reorderable modules (colour, motion, ambience, grit) with five effects each, knob-gesture recording, a 30 s looper and MIDI CCs laid out like a commercial multi-effect pedal's chart. While active it owns the audio engine (synths silent); with core-dn1 3.4 it can instead sit after the master stage and stay on. GPL-2.0. Same author and platform as DigiSwarm.

projects.name: DigiSwarm
projects.author: irpina

Owns the audio engine while active. 0.2 tested by the author on a unit and in digiemu; not yet on a Digitone Keys. Source also in elekloader as mods/digiswarm-dn1. GPL-2.0.

projects.name: Analog Four / Keys MK1 OS 1.56 mods
projects.author: hugz202

projects.tested_note: README: the 1.56 port's placement checked in emulator sessions; no unit result stated (read 2026-11-11)

projects.notes: Build pipeline that patches the user's own A4/AK MK1 OS 1.56 file with small ColdFire routines. Mods include a scale lock, 303-style slides, kit persistence for the extra settings, a per-track digital path with drive, a digital wave/chord oscillator in place of noise, a random track generator and a resonance limit. Has its own flashing/recovery and hazards docs. The first public firmware mod for the Analog Four found. MIT.

projects.name: Cycles Engines

projects.name: Cycles Mod Standard
projects.author: durchgemacht
projects.notes: Repo was offline from 2026-11-07 (taken offline by its author together with the other public repos of the same account) and is public again (seen 2026-11-13; draft 0.8 added a knob's picture as a claim, draft 0.9 withdraws a machine's own values and adds the MACHINES switches). Draft standard for Model:Cycles mods (machine contract, extension points, per-mod manifests, clash checks over saved slots, key combos and display). Implemented in model27, tested on a unit for machines and one delay effect. Useful reading for anyone designing a mod format. MIT.

projects.name: model909
projects.author: DMDaudio
projects.base_os: Model:Cycles OS 1.13 (also Model:Samples running the Cycles OS)
projects.version: v1.0 (909 only, stable); main branch adds 808/606 voices (experimental)
projects.tested_note: README: the 808/606 branch is checked in emulation and on one Model:Samples; the 909-only branch is the stable one (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["TR-909 voices in place of the six stock machines", "TR-808 and TR-606 voices (experimental branch)", "hats and cymbals from your own WAV files"]
projects.notes: Replaces the six stock machines with circuit-modelled TR-909 voices (integer models fitted to recordings); the experimental branch adds 808 and 606 voices on SHAPE. Hats/cymbals need user-supplied WAVs. MIT.

projects.name: Octatrack modules (MIDI Scales, Loopback, Follow, Harmony)
projects.author: radiohagen
projects.features: ["MIDI scales, loopback, follow, harmony and musical units", "Euclid LFO", "percussion voice and CPU supersaw (experimental)"]
projects.notes: Source of several octabam modules (MIDI scales, loopback, follow, harmony, musical units, a Euclid LFO, an experimental percussion voice and a CPU supersaw). octabam supplies the builder and platform.

projects.name: midisc (1.40MSC)
projects.author: sambanks
projects.features: ["MIDI scene locks", "scene hold edits and crossfader morph", "part save and reload", "scene clear, copy and paste"]
projects.notes: MIDI scene locks for the Octatrack (scene hold edits, crossfader morph, part save/reload, scene copy/paste). Built with Python from the user's own OS file. Same author as octabam, which later carried MIDI SCENES. Same name as bkkbrls-del/midisc in this list; how the two relate is not stated in the README start.

projects.name: ReBirth to Octatrack
projects.author: alexandrubelc
projects.base_os: Octatrack with octabam GARDEN36 or later
projects.notes: Browser tool (Pyodide) that converts ReBirth RB-338 songs into Octatrack projects for the octabam GARDEN engines, from a template project. README in Romanian.

projects.name: Kitsmith
projects.author: Alina-sul
projects.notes: Desktop manager for the Rytm MKII that reads +Drive and projects and moves samples, kits and patterns between projects with the reference bookkeeping done for you. MIT.

projects.name: Sidecar | Expander
projects.author: trigcondition
projects.base_os: Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.73 (Rytm side is an elekloader module)
projects.version: Sidecar 0.4.4 with Rytm firmware 0.4.4 (2026-11-10): a held step's locks on the SRC view, the pads' octave keys on the SEQ and ARP pages, one NO leaves a page, the CONNECTED screen when the Rytm boots after the Sidecar; the A4 mod stays 0.12, Sidecar Mini 0.1.0
projects.features: ["a Raspberry Pi 4B or 5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer", "poly tracks on every Sidecar machine", "one SD card boots both", "Analog Four MKII support (experimental)", "Digitakt support in the emulator only"]
projects.notes: A Raspberry Pi 4B/5 on the Rytm's USB port adds digital voices, effects and a sequencer; the Rytm runs a patched OS. 0.3.2 adds experimental, emulator-only Digitakt support. The Teensy variant is frozen. GPL-2.0. On 2026-11-09, Analog Four MKII support since 0.4.0 (A4 firmware a4-v0.12, OS 1.56); 0.4.3 caps the Rytm screen redraws after users saw a sluggish Rytm at 20-40 redraws a second. 2026-11-13: a card config editor on the documentation site writes the Pi's config.txt and cmdline.txt in the browser.

projects.name: C7
projects.author: sata1000000
projects.notes: Desktop app controlling the Machinedrum and Monomachine over SysEx/MIDI (kits, sounds, patterns, songs, samples) with a DAW bridge plug-in for automation. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: OctaLib
projects.author: snugsound
projects.notes: Librarian for Octatrack projects (bank swaps and more by rewriting the project files). Unlicense.

projects.name: ModuleDrum
projects.author: K-X420
projects.notes: Chip-level Machinedrum emulation as a DAW plug-in that runs the user's own OS and DSP programs, with the sequencer and a library. Fork of Monomodule and still builds the Monomodule plug-ins. AGPL-3.0.

projects.name: Machinemodule for MPC OS
projects.author: sd88me
projects.notes: The Machinedrum's own DSP code and machine/LFO/mixer maths as a VST2 for Akai MPC/Force standalone devices (all 16 tracks in one instance). The same author ports it to Ableton Move (Schwung) and ships Monomodule for MPC OS. User supplies the OS file. AGPL-3.0.

projects.name: MachineModule (desktop)
projects.author: AcidReff
projects.notes: Windows/macOS standalone and VST3 port of sd88me's Machinedrum engine with a JUCE interface; 0.4.6 adds a native ARM JIT for voices and master effects. AGPL-3.0.

projects.name: Monomodule for Schwung
projects.author: legsmechanical
projects.notes: Port of Monomodule (chip-level Monomachine engine) to Ableton Move via Schwung, as one synth track plus the seven FX machines. GPL-3.0 per README (repo metadata says AGPL-3.0).

projects.name: mdkit
projects.author: soejrd
projects.notes: The Machinedrum's EFM, TRX and P-I voice families as standalone C99 for porting, with a web demo. Whether it was derived from the OS or modelled from recordings is not said in the README start. CC0 (LICENSE and NOTICE read 2026-11-11; the NOTICE adds that CC0 covers what the contributors can dedicate, not third-party names or materials).

projects.name: OP-XY MNMD
projects.author: mmockett
projects.version: v1.3.6 (tag, 2026-11-13): MD KIT builds into one firmware with Hexagon's Moth; v1.3.5: the synths play at one loudness, MD KIT raises its quieter machines by up to 6 dB
projects.notes: Machinedrum and Monomachine engines written from scratch (not an emulation of the chips) for the Teenage Engineering OP-XY on the Open-XY SDK. MIT. v1.3.2 (README 2026-11-12) gives each MD KIT key its own pan, level, filter, sample-rate reduction and FX sends with step locks (needs OP-XY SDK 1.10). v1.3.3/v1.3.4 (README 2026-11-13) adds a second kit, MD E12, plays the Machinedrum's sixteen E12 machines from samples the user captures from their own ROM (silent without them); both kits target SDK 1.15 for their Shift mixer.

projects.name: BSP Machinedrum
projects.author: ABarracu87
projects.notes: Uses an Arturia BeatStep Pro as a front panel for the Gearmulator Machinedrum/Monomachine plug-ins, talking to the plug-ins through their MCP servers. MIT.

projects.name: Analog Rytm MK1 OS 1.74 mods
projects.author: hugz202
projects.tested_note: README: the full image flashed and played on a Rytm MK1, OS 1.73; the 1.74 build not flashed yet (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["seven Machinedrum TX-8 and TX-9 ports as new machines", "a chorus as a third send effect", "DUCK: sidechain-style pumping from one track", "CPU probe build with live load readouts"]
projects.notes: Sister project of the A4 MK1 mods (same registry/verify method). Adds Machinedrum TX-8/TX-9 ports as new machines, a chorus as a third send, a sidechain-style duck at the voices' analog VCAs, and a CPU-load probe build. Has hazards and flashing docs. MIT.

projects.name: rytm-mods boot report
projects.author: Iced-Cream
projects.notes: Evidence for Modwerk's add-a-machine steps on the Rytm MKII - the stock file rebuilt byte for byte, a modified OS booted on a unit and recovered with stock, and elekloader's core-ar2 with every shared event observed on a unit. Hashes, addresses and photos only. GPL-2.0.

projects.name: TrackPatterns
projects.author: pgstath
projects.features: ["each of the 16 tracks plays its own pattern of the playing bank", "a track changes pattern at its own loop end (clip-style)"]
projects.notes: Each of the 16 tracks can play its own pattern of the playing bank and switch at its own loop end (a clip-style workflow). Checked in the ColdFire emulator and on the contributor's MKII; also submitted to octabam (PR 846). MIT.

projects.name: OType
projects.author: nordseele
projects.tested_note: README: developed on an Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C; not tested on the MKII (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["scripting language: scripts on the card run on the machine", "reach trigs, locks, pages, parts, scenes, tempo, patterns and banks", "load and free machines and sample slots", "save the current take as a WAV and load audio files", "live scripts on clock, note, CC and trig events"]
projects.notes: A line-oriented scripting language for the Octatrack - scripts on the card reach (almost) every editable parameter and audio files and are called on the machine. Command reference in a separate docs repo. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: OctaDraw
projects.author: nordseele
projects.notes: Browser pixel editor for the Octatrack's 128x64 screen that exports ColdFire assembly drawing the same pixels, plus PNG previews and a JSON description for wiring into a firmware module. A developer tool for UI mods. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: octa-bt-pt
projects.author: bryantysinger
projects.tested_note: README: nothing is exposed as a labelled control unless its behaviour was checked against a real unit (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["web tool that writes parameter values into your own OS 1.40C file", "effect defaults and FX1/FX2 default assignment", "AMF multiply fix", "each patch checked against the stock file's hash"]
projects.notes: Web UI that patches parameter values (effect defaults, FX1/FX2 default assignment, an AMF multiply fix) into the user's own 1.40C file - values, not code, listed in a registry. macOS build tooling. MIT.

projects.name: aCiDtRacK modules
projects.author: braikomarko-hub
projects.tested_note: README: tested on one Octatrack MKI, OS 1.40C, hours of playing (Oct 2026) (read 2026-11-11)
projects.features: ["octa303: a circuit-modelled TB-303 voice per track", "devilish: Devil Fish mods for the 303 voice", "distorx: distortion insert", "db666: compressor insert with side-chain"]
projects.notes: octabam modules - a circuit-modelled TB-303 voice per track on the ColdFire (calibrated against recordings), Devil Fish mods, an SD-1/RAT-style distortion and a dbx-160-style compressor. The README marks what is proven. MIT.

projects.name: Machinedrum USR machines (RASP, KOOK, SMSH...)
projects.author: SamplesAndSnacks
projects.features: ["three USR machines: RASP (blown trill), KOOK (kookaburra), SMSH (smashed piano)", "no sample banks needed"]
projects.notes: Custom USR machines, each a single SysEx file sent to MDX's machine manager. MIT.

projects.name: Monomachine Lab
projects.author: Jick238
projects.notes: AU/VST3 that runs one Monomachine DSP track's original DSP56300 code (15 synth and 7 FX machine dispatches, the per-track chain, kit SysEx import). Independent of Monomodule, which it points to for a fuller emulation.

projects.name: Maschine MD-MM
projects.author: sid366
projects.notes: Fork of gearmulator-md-mm with Native Instruments Maschine MK3 integration. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: MDDT (Machinedrum Data Tool)
projects.author: waftlord
projects.notes: Browser tool (WebMIDI) for Machinedrum MK1/MK2/UW data over SysEx. Apache-2.0.

projects.name: Tributary
projects.author: stampman3000-jpg
projects.version: v1.2.4 (tag, 2026-11-13): the plugin holds about 11 ms of Digitone II audio (enough for the MPC's 256-sample block); Capture waits 470 samples after the bar
projects.notes: An Overwitch rework that plays Overbridge USB audio on Akai MPC standalone tracks; heard on a Digitone II, holding ~4 ms behind the newest USB sample. Shows Overbridge streaming works outside a desktop host. GPL-3.0. 2026-11-12 (CAPTURE.md) - a Capture tab records the machine's own 48 kHz samples for 1-16 bars, locked to the MPC's bar and shifted by the 162-sample monitoring delay, into a 24-bit wav; host tests only, not yet on an MPC.

projects.name: TurboMIDI (C++)
projects.author: DatanoiseTV
projects.notes: Header-only C++ implementation of Elektron's TurboMIDI speed negotiation (up to 20x DIN MIDI speed). Since 2026-11-04 the repo no longer answers anonymously (git asks for credentials, so private or removed); still gone on 2026-11-11, so it is no longer polled.

projects.name: rytm-rs / rytm-sys
projects.author: alisomay
projects.notes: Rust abstractions over the Rytm's undocumented SysEx (bindings to a fork of bsp2's libanalogrytm). MIT.

projects.name: Analog Four sound SysEx cheatsheet
projects.author: kimasendorf
projects.notes: Tables of the A4 sound SysEx bytes, from reverse engineering.

projects.name: ot-tools-io
projects.author: jhw
projects.notes: Rust crate for reading and writing the Octatrack's binary project/bank/marker files; the same author's octapy does it in Python. GPL-3.0.

projects.name: Model:Cycles .mcpst format notes
projects.author: kg4zow
projects.notes: Reverse-engineered layout of the Model:Cycles preset files (.mcpst) with dump/compare scripts.

projects.name: Plock (Rytm pattern editor)
projects.author: plentyofnames
projects.notes: Browser pattern editor for the Analog Rytm over Web MIDI: pulls the current pattern and kit by SysEx, edits trigs, parameter locks, retrigs, micro-timing and sound locks in a step grid and sends the result back; opens and saves .syx dumps and exports MIDI. The README credits earlier community work on the format. MIT per README (no licence file in the repo).

projects.name: Digitakt Pattern Editor (JUCE)
projects.author: mk3stn3r
projects.base_os: Digitakt MKI; offline sample playback over USB audio needs OS 1.20 or later
projects.notes: Native desktop app (C++/JUCE, built for Linux, CMake also for macOS/Windows): downloads a pattern or a whole project over USB MIDI, edits the step grid and sample locks, imports MIDI files, uploads samples to the +Drive and plays patterns offline through the computer. The README says the format layer is a C++ port of elk-herd rather than a wrapper, and that it writes lanes elk-herd only decodes. BSD-2-Clause (licence file carries elk-herd's copyright). Was in ignore.yml as an empty repo; re-reviewed 2026-11-03 after altstrument listed it.

projects.name: digitakt-reorder
projects.author: daguilarc
projects.notes: Python library and job template that reorders, drops and de-duplicates the sample pool of a Digitakt project dump and remaps every kit and sample-lock reference. Works on a .syx file fetched and sent with elk-herd; no MIDI code. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep (elektron-sample-prep)
projects.author: luizvarela
projects.notes: Single-page browser sample prep: trims at zero crossings, converts to 48 kHz 16-bit WAV, works out loop lengths from BPM and steps; profiles for four devices (device list taken from the related ElekPrep Transfer app, not checked). No MIDI; files go to the unit through Transfer or Elektroid. MIT.

projects.name: ElekPrep Transfer
projects.author: unknown
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. Proprietary; author not named. Relation to luizvarela's ElekPrep not established (same name). Interesting as a second independent implementation of +Drive upload over SysEx.

projects.name: Digitone 2 Pattern Manager
projects.author: morukutsu
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app: requests Pattern+Kit dumps from a Digitone II slot over Web MIDI, keeps them in a local library and sends them back to a chosen slot; also imports project capture .syx files and replays a captured project stream. Proprietary. Shows that DN2 pattern/kit dump requests per slot work over SysEx (claim, not checked by us).

projects.name: MachineDrandom
projects.author: Kerem Ergener (per altstrument)
projects.notes: Closed-source browser app that randomises the loaded Machinedrum kit live over Web MIDI, engine by engine and parameter by parameter, and can generate rhythm patterns played as MIDI notes. Nothing is stored until the kit is saved on the unit. Proprietary.

projects.name: Say A! (MCL chromatic A tool)
projects.author: BartBral
projects.notes: Browser sample prep and transfer tool for the Machinedrum UW: shifts each sample so its root lands on an A for MegaCommand's chromatic mode, resamples, processes loops, and sends over MIDI Sample Dump or saves WAV and .syx. Licence not stated. Repo clone timed out (large); details from altstrument.

projects.name: SM (Machinedrum sample manager)
projects.author: Fyris
projects.notes: Closed-source browser sample manager for the Machinedrum UW using MIDI Sample Dump Standard over Web MIDI: 48 slots with waveform view, WAV and .syx import/export, reverse, invert, loop and name controls. Proprietary.

projects.name: Model:Cycles Web Editor
projects.author: tkawamu0622-cmd
projects.notes: Browser piano-roll editor and sequencer for the Model:Cycles over Web MIDI: parameters as CC, pattern select by program change, and recording a sequence into the unit one track at a time by playing it in over MIDI clock (no pattern SysEx). Licence not stated. Repo clone failed (transfer error); details from altstrument.

projects.name: BIAS (six-oscillator percussion machine)
projects.author: 100demons
projects.features: ["BIAS machine: six oscillators with their own envelopes", "wavefolder and a second envelope after it", "clock locked to the note"]
projects.notes: Source package for a percussion machine with six oscillators, each with its own envelope, summed, wavefolded and given a second envelope, on a clock locked to the note; written clean-room after Noise Engineering's published description of the Basimilus Iteritas Alia (no NE code or tables per its notices). Fixed-point C for the ColdFire, a table generator, a host build and an emulator test on the OS's own voice loop. A machine package for model27, with a fixed-slot tweak for Modded Cycles 2.0; also on the Cycles Engines flasher. Played on a Model:Cycles 2026-11-03 in slot 11 (README): heavy on the processor, and it does not combine with five model27 Track FX packages (15 overlap problems). Commits a compiled object (bias.o). Found via altstrument 2026-11-04.

projects.name: CTRL+ / USER CFG (Digitone mk1)

projects.features: ["the Digitone Keys' User Mode pages in the regular Digitone's TRIG rotation", "USER CFG page to assign the eight encoders", "assignments saved with the project"]
projects.notes: Adds the Digitone Keys' User Mode page (stock page 24) to the regular Digitone's TRIG page rotation, plus a USER CFG page that assigns the eight encoders; the assignment is saved with the project through core-dn1 project data. Testing status not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: CHOKE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 3.1 or later
projects.features: ["two choke groups, set per track", "a note fades out the other tracks of its group", "CHK knob on the second TRIG page, p-lockable"]
projects.notes: Two choke groups set per track from the Mod Menu and saved with the project: a note on a track fades out the voices of the group's other tracks over one 32-sample block (0.7 ms). Names no firmware address (uses ev_voice_on, ev_render_voices, fw_voice_track). Checked only in digiemu (11 voices choked, output RMS measured); not heard, not on a unit.

projects.name: PROGRAM CHANGE -> SOUND (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)

projects.name: MIDI LOOPBACK (Digitone mk1)

projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)

Names no firmware address. Checked only in digiemu with its DIN output captured; the CC path only through core_midi_receive.

projects.name: SOLO & MUTE GROUPS (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)

projects.notes: Track key + FUNC solos a track among its four; four mute groups. Checked only in digiemu (with LOOPBACK and PC SOUND in the same build), not on a unit.

projects.name: ARP MENU (Digitone mk1)
projects.author: irpina
projects.base_os: Digitone mk1 / Keys OS 1.43 and 1.44; core-dn1 5.0.1 (unreleased)
projects.features: ["a long FUNC + KEYBOARD press opens the ARP menu", "a quick press still toggles the arpeggiator"]

projects.name: Mezclando (transition mode for Digitakt II)

Built locally in a browser patch page or from source (m68k-elf GCC, Node 24, a Modwerk checkout with core-dt2 1.0). English and Spanish README. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

projects.name: elkbench (hardware tests as an MCP server)
projects.author: Iced-Cream

It enforces one owner per unit, emulator first, and a hardware run only after the person says go. Python stdlib; Windows and Linux. 2026-11-10: a flash between two fixed OS files of a unit can reuse an emulator pass of the same flash, recorded with the hashes of the emulator, the flash tool and the card, while all of them stay the same. 2026-11-11 (config example): an optional emulator headroom check waits for CPU, free RAM and a cap on running emulators before each emulator start. 2026-11-12: emulator timing (analog-emu unit or exact timing, the Sidecar's Overbridge stream on the Rytm) and a CPU gate that fails an emulator run at 95 % CPU. 2026-11-13: elklock marks a unit that stalled on its restart after a flash and refuses every device command on it until a watched power cycle (elkflash usb-cycle).

projects.author: sadnoise (femifleming)
projects.base_os: Octatrack MKII only; replaces the OS (Elektron's bootloader and Startup Menu stay untouched); the install file is built from the user's own copy of the official OS file, OS 1.40C
projects.version: v0.9.3-beta (2026-11-13; pre-releases v0.9.0-v0.9.3 all on 2026-11-13): BBD removed (old project slots load empty), engine moved into DSP core 0's private memory
projects.tested_note: docs/CHANGELOG.md (2026-11-13): every release build is marked as tested on the unit, with what was checked (effects load and play, 8/8 feature tests, a stress test, 54 delay swaps); the effect ports are verified in a DSP56300 emulator against the author's plugin models (aeria-fx test_results)
projects.features: ["replaces the Octatrack MKII's OS with its own", "weather-driven multi-effect chain of up to seven effects on the inputs", "8-track sequencer with sampler, synth and polyphonic MIDI machines", "ratchets, conditions, curved clock and a cellular automaton per track", "three LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and a flock of boids as modulators", "18-channel stems over USB"]
projects.notes: An operating system of its own for the Octatrack MKII, not a patch of Elektron's OS: a weather-driven multi-effect on inputs A-D (up to seven effects whose knobs the chosen weather moves) and an 8-track sequencer groovebox (sampler, sub, FM, noise, Karplus-Strong and polyphonic MIDI machines, p-locks, ratchets, per-track cellular automata), plus LFOs, a Lorenz attractor and boids as modulators. ColdFire part in C, effects in hand-written DSP56300 assembly. Installing it removes the stock OS until it is reinstalled from the card; both keep their saved data in the same battery-backed SRAM, so back up before switching. The build uses the Modwerk SDK's tools (not included); aeria-os/HARDWARE.md and AUDIO.md map the MKII for writing an OS from scratch, largely from octabam's and Modwerk's documents. Some effect folders (head, tap) are marked as someone else's work. Made with Claude Code (README). Found by GitHub search 2026-11-13. 2026-11-14: docs/CHANGELOG.md lists every release build and what was checked on the unit; docs/LOG.md is the request log of the 9-13 Nov build, with the hardware findings now on the Octatrack page and incidents I83-I86.

projects.name: RIFT (second Digitone II firmware)
projects.author: De-Pattern
projects.base_os: Digitone II OS 1.11 only (infrastructure from dn2mk2-firmware v0.51); the patcher also needs the user's own Digitakt II OS 1.17 and Machinedrum UW OS 1.63 files
projects.version: v0.1 FASCIA (2026-11-13): the gate printed CLEARED TO FLASH and the patcher offers it; the announcement is still a draft until the owner has tested it
projects.tested_note: v0.1 is gated in the emulator only (2026-11-13); the owner has not yet tested it on a unit; voice counts are emulator figures
projects.features: ["FASCIA: physical and spectral percussion and tuned-body engine (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies)", "32 FASCIA controls on four pages, all p-lockable and slid, most LFO destinations", "Digitakt II sample machines from the DN2 mk2 mod (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE, FLEX)", "+Drive sample library, recorder, Direct Jump and parameter slides kept from the DN2 mk2 mod", "no Machinedrum or Monomachine engines: their tracks open as FM Tone", "TZFM, ring and frequency shift, spectral morph, low-pass gate inside FASCIA"]
projects.notes: A second Digitone II firmware by the dn2mk2 author, separate from that mod: no Machinedrum or Monomachine machines, starting with one engine, FASCIA (two exciters into two coupled modal bodies, TZFM, ring and frequency shift, a spectral morph, a low-pass gate). Its first commit carries the dn2mk2 infrastructure (build framework, SHARC DSL, release gate); FASCIA's model, its float32 DSP-order contract and a bit-exact SHARC program come from dn2mk2 branches. Plan (docs/rift.md): stand FASCIA alone, measure its voice count, then integrate and release. The test bench is private. Found by find_new (new repo of a catalogued author) 2026-11-13. v0.1 (2026-11-13) removes the Machinedrum and Monomachine engines from the DSP image to fit the 2 MiB upgrade buffer. The roadmap (docs/rift-roadmap.md) plans per-track insert effects, an LPG filter type, a looping function-generator envelope and a granular machine.

projects.name: MASHUP (Digitakt)
projects.author: ClaidArremer
projects.version: 0.6.1 (2026-11-13): FUNC key repeats no longer leave the trig keys dark; called STUTTER up to 0.5
projects.tested_note: README (2026-11-13): addresses and CPU cost found and counted in digiemu; no run on a unit stated
projects.features: ["always-on buffer of the master mix", "trig keys play repeats, scrambles, half time, pitch steps, rolls and spin-backs, quantised to the 16th", "the sequencer runs on underneath, so the pattern comes back in place", "FUNC + SAMPLING switches the mode; stock keys return outside it"]
projects.notes: Performance repeats from an always-on buffer of the master mix: with MASHUP mode on (FUNC + SAMPLING) the 16 trig keys play the last few seconds back in time while the sequencer runs on underneath. elekloader mod (id mashup-dt). GPL-2.0-or-later. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14; README read.

projects.name: GESTALT (Digitakt)
projects.author: ClaidArremer
projects.version: 0.3 (2026-11-13): 512 wave tables of its own (none of WMD's)
projects.features: ["RADS: 8-bit wave-table destruction with drive, sample rate reduction and blend", "PUMP: SP-303 Vinyl Sim-style levelling compressor with ratio and release", "takes the stock compressor's master page and settings, saved with each kit"]
projects.notes: Master chain in place of the Digitakt's stock compressor: RADS, a Geiger Counter-style wave-table destruction, into the PUMP levelling compressor, on every output. Replaces PUMP for Digitakt (use one or the other). elekloader mod (id gestalt-dt). GPL-2.0-or-later. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-14; README read.
