facts.text: The Digitone II board has the same part number PCBA0109B as the Digitakt II (32 GB Kingston eMMC), so both likely run the same hardware with different OS images and header boards. `[?]` {elektronauts-dn2-pcb}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Hardware claims from forums and teardowns (not verified)
facts.text: Specs from reviews: 400 MB sample memory, 20 GB internal storage, 16 tracks (synthtopia summary); sample memory pool of dn2mk2 on the Digitone II is also 400 MB. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: SHARC part: ADSP-21569. Section 7 holds ADSP-2156x loader/application records (104 records mapped). FreeRTOS, an Audio task and a recurring block loop are traced. The hand-off from the boot kernel to that startup is not.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: The ColdFire <-> SHARC frame is the same shape as on the Digitone II: A full-duplex `0xabc`-byte DSPI2 frame carries a `0x802`-byte state payload: 16 records of `0x60` bytes, track n to SHARC unit n. ColdFire eDMA29 sends and eDMA28 receives; the SHARC uses SPI2 with completed-image double buffering. The send is driven from a level-5 interrupt that a level-6 eDMA-completion path forces in software. Link settings: SPI mode 1, 16-bit MSB-first, one `0x55e`-word window. The meaning of the SHARC-to-ColdFire return content is open. Compare the DN2's frame and reply words in [digitone-2-internals.md](digitone-2-internals.md). This is a second, independent reading of the shared design (research map T19).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Project samples reach the SHARC over a different path: ColdFire Rapid-GPIO byte/strobe/ready endpoint -> SHARC link port 0 (LP0_RX, DMA30). Samples are described by five-word resource descriptors with 4 KiB pages. This agrees with digikit finding 15 ([digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md](digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md)). The physical bridge between the two endpoints is not identified.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Audio output: two 64-word banks are selected, then sent by a two-bank circular DMA descriptor (DMA10) to SPORT4 half A. Codec and pin are not identified.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Update path: MAIN validates checksum, minimum version and the cryptographic trailer before it erases and programs the staged ELE3 slot at flash `0x80000`, then requests a reset. Which updater copy runs after reset, and whether recovery is independent of it, is marked opaque.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Architecture map from static analysis and simulation (lalzart, OS 1.15C)
facts.text: Offline modifications proven in the simulator only: a byte-exact selector reroute, and a 3-byte change that turns an output-bank negation into pass-through. Re-encoding a modified section and running it on hardware are explicitly unproven.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: The main OS's default exception handler prints `EXCEPTION ...` with the vector, format, PC and twelve stack words, then executes `halt` with interrupts masked. It never returns.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: The core watchdog is not used anywhere in the main OS, so a fault hangs the whole device until the power is cycled. Messages like the DT2's `V04 M0 P40311A64` (dt2-machine-lab) are this handler's output.

facts.section: Digitakt II / What happens on a ColdFire fault (digikit finding 37, DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12, static, checked by a second agent) `[doc]`
facts.text: digikit's runtime counts bad boots: the counter is raised at boot start and cleared only after 30 s of stable running. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: The intro is its own task, priority 7, created once by the installer before the main-OS task (DT2 `0x400d1448`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3920`) and woken by a PIT3 tick. A higher number is more urgent here, so the intro preempts the main-OS task (priority 6). A frame callback that never returns starves the main OS until power-off.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Five scene tables at `0x402a1b64`, `0x402a1b74`, `0x402a1b84`, `0x402a1b94`, `0x402a1ba4`. Each boot picks one with an LCG; the first is picked about 99.9 % of the time and has 175 frames. An entry is `{callback, frame count}`, ended by a 0.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: One pointer drives it: the current entry is at DT2 `0x43153a00`, DN2 1.12 `0x42c4cacc`, DN2 1.11 `0x42c4bacc`. Only the setup function (DT2 `0x400d1832`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d0a`) and the tick function (DT2 `0x400d18f0`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3dc8`) touch it. Each frame calls `callback(index, count, bitmap)`; count 0 ends the intro the normal way: the pointer is cleared, PIT3 stops and semaphore `0x43149550` releases the main-OS task.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Swapping the intro: a hook before the setup function's argument load (`move.l (0x24,SP),D0; movea.l D0,A0`, DT2 `0x400d183a`, DN2 1.12 `0x400d3d12`, DN2 1.11 `0x400d3bae`, the same 6 bytes on all three) can point it at an own table. In digikit's emulator the UI was then reached after 115 audio blocks instead of 5,973 (DT2) and 6,180 (DN2). Stock's frame clear is `0x40113700` (DN2 1.12 `0x40115074`, DN2 1.11 `0x40114d94`), called as `(bitmap, 0, 1)`. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Frame rate unresolved: digikit's timer model gives 30 Hz (175 frames = 5.8 s); its earlier emulator notes derived 15 Hz. Open conflict [O20](../CONFLICTS.md). Module code first runs at about frame 53-57 of the intro (emulator); almost all of that delay is stock setup.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Faults during the intro reach stock's halting handler (see the section above): digikit installs its own crash handler only from the UI loop.

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Frame layout on the panel (measured on one DT2 1.17): with y = 0 at the top, the intro bitmap holds pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, flipped vertically only. digikit's emulator shows these frames the other way up. `[hw]` ([I53](../INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel))

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: Safe mode is digikit's, not stock's: REC (key `0x13`, state byte 2 bit 2; key state array at DT2 `0x44dc8644`, DN2 `0x445a2e30`) held from power-on skips all modules. On one DT2 1.17 it worked, and a custom boot screen started about 1.8 s after the stock intro. `[hw]` ([I54](../INCIDENTS.md#i54-safe-mode-by-rec-at-power-on-tested-on-a-digitakt-ii))

facts.section: Digitakt II / The stock intro and boot screens (digikit finding 117, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12)
facts.text: With the black intro patch set, the bootstrap's logo, "B" and the OS version stay until the main OS first writes the display, then about 1-2 s of black, then the boot screen. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: ColdFire heap: a 32 MiB buddy allocator at `0x44f39c40-0x46f39c40` (16-byte minimum, power-of-two blocks), parameters at `0x402b406c`.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Allocating from the stock heap at startup (digitakt-ii-research, OS 1.16, emulator, byte-verified sites) {dt2-research-heap}: `malloc` is at `0x4011e674` (size at `4(A7)`, pointer in D0, mutex at `0x44e08654`, lazy init on first call). `free` is at `0x4011e87a`. It traps with `illegal` on a pointer outside the heap or not 16-byte aligned, the same rule as the Digitakt mk1's operator delete. The OS clears `0x40312000-0x47e28470` at reset, so static data placed there does not survive boot. A startup hook at `0x40133646` (`link.w` + `movem`) made exactly one 8 KiB allocation that stayed untouched for 20 M instructions. This is the cleanest way to own memory without a cave.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Sample pool: Logical range `0x400-0x19000400`, 400 MiB, allocations rounded to 8 KiB. The ColdFire's allocation records decide admission; no SHARC malloc is involved. In the SHARC's view the pool is a window at DSP byte address `0x8422b9c8 + (offset - 0x400)`, ending at `0x9d22b9c8`. Capicola reserves the top 8 MiB.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Recorder: the main OS fetches recorder data in chunks of at most `0x800` bytes over DSPI1 from a service whose physical owner (ColdFire, SHARC DDR or a third part) is not established. Staging buffers are at `0x4fe79340` / `0x4fe7a340`.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: SHARC side: Sample-slot table at `0x257810 + slot*0x14`: 1,025 entries, slot `0x400` is the preview. Voices at `0x2412cc + lane*0x1d8`, 32 lanes: `+0` PCM pointer, `+0x188` length, `+0x1b8` active. Link-port 0 receive staging at `0x268220` (descriptor) and `0x268240` (a tag plus 4 KiB of payload).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Memory map for samples and voices (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16, static plus emulator)
facts.text: Once published to the SHARC, PCM keeps playing after the ColdFire source is freed, as long as the stock allocation stays owned. Saving, however, needs the source, and no read-back path from sample memory was found.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: digikit's patchkit (used by digitakt-ii-research's All-in-One and dt2-machine-lab), elekloader's core-dt2 (used by digitakt2-perform) and the hand-placed builds share the flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000`. elekloader's RAM `0x47f00000-0x47f40000` lies inside digikit's `cf.expansion` `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000`. Full table of ranges and hook sites: [memory-maps.md](../common/memory-maps.md). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Three Digitakt II mod routes side by side (T21, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed a unit (dt2-machine-lab, OS 1.16): [firmware-container.md](../common/firmware-container.md), rule A46. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-capicola} ([I16](../INCIDENTS.md#i16-a-decoded-section-7-over-1-mib-crashed-the-unit))

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Reading a track's Sound parameter words needs no fixed address: get the project singleton, its ProjectSettings at project + `0x30` (static analysis only), the selected track from `view_track` (clamped 0-15), then `native_track_sound(active kit, track)` = kit + `0x6c` + `0x3c0` x track; vtable slot `0x28` of that Sound object returns the record pointer `*(sound + 0x10)` (0 when none is bound), and word i is a big-endian s16 at record + `0x14` + 2i. Anchors: settings `0x40041d18` (DT2 1.17) / `0x4003e40e` (DN2 1.12); `native_track_sound` `0x40035cca` / `0x40030e66`. The array holds 71 words on the DT2 and 101 on the DN2. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: On the DN2 a track's Sound record can sit at an odd address (kit stride `0x48b`), so read it byte by byte. A parameter code maps to its array index through the descriptor table (rows of `0x3c` bytes, index as s32 at row + 4, -1 = no word); the same index means another parameter on another machine. P-locks, sound lock, LFO and MIDI CC writes go through other paths, and a latched parameter of a run-time machine changed no word in the array (where it is stored is open). `[doc]`/`[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Track overdrive (stock): the curve clamps to +-1 and applies y*(2-|y|) three times; the blend is x + mix*(y-x) with stock ramps for drive and mix. OVR Routing is parameter `0x103` (Sound mirror index 68; 0 = pre, `0x100` = post). The per-track stage is called twice per track from the voice chain. `[doc]` {digikit-overdrive}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Run-time machines: on the DT2 they can use knob slots B C E F G H; a parameter on the seventh slot replaces LEV, whose level is then fixed at 100. The run-time module stage is limited to 64 KB; a TB-303 port costs about 8,000 SHARC instructions per 32-sample block. `[doc]` {digikit-tb303}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: ColdFire jump targets must be even: a jsr/jmp to an odd address faults with an address error on the unit while the emulator runs on; a byte-aligned mod section froze a DT2 at boot (I61). `[hw]` {elekloader-oddjump}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Sound parameters, overdrive and run-time machines (digikit, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12, 2026-11-10)
facts.text: Modwerk's DT2 base: a combined image booted on a DT2 (OS 1.17, 2026-11-08) and restored saved module kit data after a project reload. Its audio scheduler (grid callbacks and phrase replacement at the stock audio submission call `0x400d82f8`) is a proposal checked only in digikit fixtures. `[hw]` / `[emu]` {modwerk-dt2-base}

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: The firmware's own file calls can write samples: open (`0x40158902`, mode "w"), write (`0x4015866a`), reserve, hash (`0x4015b3aa`), close (`0x401588c0`), info, delete (`0x40157078`), mkdir and rename (`0x40156f6c`, which keeps the inode, size and stored hash). Each takes the recursive filesystem mutex itself and blocks, so call them from a task, never an interrupt. The sampler's recorder `0x40153c70` is a complete stock caller. `[doc]` (static)

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Open does not truncate: an existing file opens at position 0 with its old size and data; stock deletes first. Whole 32 KiB pages at multiples of `0x8000` are written straight from the buffer, the rest goes through the page cache. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: The 16-byte trailer: files carry 16 zero bytes after the data, and the stored hash covers them; the C calls do not add them (the recorder and stock's MidiRpc close do), so a writer adds them before the hash. File info reports size minus 16. `[emu]` (card read back on the emulator) Elekloader's Rytm loader meets the same 16 bytes as a header at the start of each file on the Analog Rytm MKII ([analog-rytm.md](analog-rytm.md)).

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Power cut: a cut mid-write leaves a visible file with a partial size and no hash; the mount was not seen to repair it. Delete refuses an open file (open-file bitmap at `0x46f4ded0`). Only `/factory` is RAM-backed; user files always go to the card, and a failed card write is not reported. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / +Drive file writes from mod code (digikit finding 120, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: On a unit (2026-11-11) digikit's bulk uploads through these calls left only complete files after a pulled cable, and the stock sample browser did not list the staging folder `/.dkstage`. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: In RAM: the project object is at `0x41776c9c`; 128 patterns from `0x41776cb8` (stride `0x1db8c`), 128 kits from `0x426532b8` (stride `0x5574`). Serializer `0x400df66c` (flag bits pick the parts), loader `0x400df95a`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Project and kit storage (digikit finding 121, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Bytes the serializer never writes: pattern record `0x15acc-0x15c00`, kit record `0x573e-0x5800`, file header `0x1c-0x200`. Pattern RAM `+0x1cef0..0x1db60` is not saved but is in use: pokes there hung the UI. `[doc]` (the hang `[hw]`)

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Whole-sample-clear hook on OS 1.17: the entry `0x40154634` starts with push A2, push D2, `clr.l D2` (6 bytes); a hook resumes at `0x4015463a`. INIT NEW and a full project LOAD both pass it. It is a notice, not a promise that the recorder, loaders or DMA have stopped: drain your own work before stock frees the backing. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: OS 1.16 project LOAD: the stock clear runs once per sample slot, so it marks no project boundary; the post-clear sample-batch entry does. The load-and-select callback (caller `0x40046c8e`) saves a recovery copy to internal slot 128 before its asynchronous sample batch completes; a mod that blocks that save makes LOAD report LOAD ERROR although decoding succeeded (I93). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Sample rows are shared: digikit's `core/sample-pool` reserves the top sixteen rows (H112-H127); Sketch uses H124-H127 for live buffers and H116-H123 for FREEZE, so the two declare a conflict. A user sample in those rows also blocks the reservation. Two mods that reserve sample rows need one owner. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: OS 1.16 recorder editor (static): the waveform service `0x4001266a` issues recorder command 3 for four signed extrema; encoder handling at `0x40020960`; trim endpoints at view +`0x9a0`/+`0x9a4`; the accepted-range copy is command 4 at `0x4001282e`. The native accept refuses ranges below 141 frames. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Projects, sample rows and the recorder (dt2-machine-lab Sketch, OS 1.16 and 1.17, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Stock SHARC load on OS 1.16 (emulator, mean instructions per 32-frame block of 666,667 cycles): 206,144 idle, 209,769 with 1 stereo track, 220,304 with 4, 262,231 with 16. Bounded workloads, not worst cases. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Pointer returns: the firmware returns pointers in d0, while GCC's m68k ABI reads them from a0; a C prototype returning a pointer froze the UI. Declare such routines as returning a 32-bit integer. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: Sites: encoder filter `0x40111cda`; per-frame value block `0x80005b50`; modulator call site `0x4002e90c`; LED frame `0x4003117c`, LED setter `0x400308e0`; NameView wrapper `0x40117c70`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / UI surfaces for mods (digikit finding 122, DT2 1.17)
facts.text: LED colour byte: on a unit `0x31` looked deep blue and `0x41` yellow (one observer, by eye); this disagrees with digikit's own finding 19 (CONFLICTS O25). `[hw]` `[?]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: USB mode switch: `FUN_40006c16` has the same address and bytes on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. It takes no lock and cuts a MIDI reply in flight; USB restarts after a 30-tick counter (about 1 s in the emulator; counter DT2 `0x40965a38`, DN2 `0x4058f280`). The stored USB CONFIG byte (0 MIDI, 1 Overbridge, 2 AUDIO/MIDI; DT2 `0x4099d5c4`, DN2 `0x405ce898`) is written only by the menu actions (DT2 `0x4010331a`/`30`/`48`, DN2 `0x40104dc2`/`d8`/`f0`), never by the switch, so a reboot returns to the stored mode; an Overbridge disconnect (`FUN_400f2ce0`) is the only path that re-applies it by itself. DT2 connection-state word `0x40965a40`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Take-over on units (2026-11-11): digikit's Fast USB switched both units from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM for an upload over its bulk interface and back (SysEx TAKEOVER `0x1e`, RELEASE `0x1f`); the stored mode byte stayed unchanged and USB audio was heard working afterwards. Longer loops later lost a unit from USB (I80, next section). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: +Drive internals: close hash `0x4015b1e8` under the filesystem mutex `0x46f4deb0` (recursive lock `0x400015a0`, unlock `0x400016d2`); inode get/put/write `0x4015b92a`/`0x4015b846`/`0x4015b868`; extent lookup `0x4015813c`; hash-table rebuild `0x4015b0ee` (about 300 ms per file on a unit); event post `0x4015a6aa`. Data page 0 is card sector `0x5ee180` (page p at base + p x `0x40`), the first hash page sector `0x5ee980`. Every file write reaches the card before the call returns. The eSDHC read/write is clamped to 64 KiB (DT2 `0x4012e3c4`, DN2 `0x4012ca8a`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Measured ceilings (8 MiB, 2026-11-11): DT2 +Drive file write 2.6 MB/s with 64 KiB calls, 7.8 MB/s with 256 KiB, 10.3 MB/s with 1 MiB; the firmware's close-hash re-read 4.2 MB/s; store writes DT2 about 7.2 MB/s, DN2 6.3 MB/s; raw card reads 15.3 MB/s on both; CPU hash 16-18.7 MB/s. A whole 8 MB upload: DT2 2.99-6.15 s (varies a lot between runs), DN2 1.75 s. Per file about 0.18-0.19 s fixed cost. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Fast close: digikit hashes from a card read-back and then runs the firmware's own close steps, byte-identical to the stock close, falling back to the firmware close if the read-back fails. After such uploads the stock browser listed the files, a sample loaded and played, and a project that referenced an uploaded sample reloaded and played it. Creating the staging folder `/.dkstage` cost about 420 ms and removing a file from it about 150 ms, so it now stays for the session. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: SHARC cycle counter: each image has exactly one EMUCLK reader, the block handler (DT2 `0x1c74cd`, DN2 `0x1c9d6b`), which keeps a low-word delta for reporting only; nothing branches on it. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB mode take-over and fast close (digikit findings 123-125, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
facts.text: eMMC EXT_CSD copy in RAM: DT2 1.17 `0x4fe69100`, DN2 1.12 `0x4e6f9100`; bytes are reversed within each 32-bit word because the eSDHC runs little-endian. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: The USB mode take-over is not reliable on a unit: switching a Digitakt II from USB AUDIO/MIDI to USB MIDI in RAM and back lost the unit from USB in cycle 5 of a 20-cycle loop, and in cycle 11 after digikit added a 2 s restart hold and parked the PHY's line during the stop. The host saw no disconnect, the unit no longer answered, a cable replug did not help and only a power cycle did; both failures came on TAKEOVER, never on RELEASE. digikit now keeps the take-over off by default; with USB CONFIG set to USB MIDI in the menu its fast transfer ran fully reliably (I80, rule A55). `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: External ULPI PHY: the USB controller drives an external ULPI PHY (PORTSC.PTS = ULPI, set at init `0x40006d1c`-`0x40006d2c`). The stock firmware writes no PHY register: its only ULPI_VIEWPORT (`0xFC0B0170`) use is a read of PHY register 0 every 300 calls of a periodic function (`0x40006af8`), which resets the controller (not the PHY) when the read never finishes. It never sets PORTSC.PHCD. The VBUS interrupt (`0x40005e14`, OTGSC.BSVIS) starts or stops the controller; the restart `0x40006bc6` starts it only while OTGSC.BSV is set. Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: The USB clock comes from the PHY: the stock init clears MISCCR.USBSRC (`0xEC09000E` bit 0), so the PHY's 60 MHz ULPI output clocks the controller's USB side. A PHY whose clock stops freezes USB while the rest of the unit runs on. The documented way to restart a stopped PHY clock is a viewport wake-up (WU set, RUN clear). Same code on DN2 1.12. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Stock controller reset: `0x40006ada` (same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12) stops the controller with restart type 2; after 30 ticks `0x40007104` sets USBCMD.RST and spins on it with no bound, runs the USB init `0x40006c52` and restarts if VBUS is valid. The firmware's own viewport watchdog uses this path. Each reset leaks one of the 16 shared timer slots (SB20). `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: How a failed take-over looks: after RS is set again PORTSC shows line state SE0 (`0xa0000005`; good switches show J), no SOF arrives and the host never addresses the device; after a controller reset OTGSC.BSV reads 0. Failures came on take-over and on release, with audio idle: 1 in 76 and 1 in 200 switches on two builds; parking the PHY line during the stop made it about 1 in 15. A replug never helped, a power cycle always did; a stop/hold/restart and the stock reset did not revive it. A viewport wake-up was never tried on a unit (I80). `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: USB AUDIO/MIDI port entry 5: the port table has 0x28-byte entries; entry 5 is at table + 0xC8 (DT2 `0x4029f048`): +0 connect `0x400040a6`, +4 disconnect `0x40004054`, +0xC configuration pointer, +0x10 length 0x148. The configuration has 5 interfaces (UAC2 on 0-2, MIDI on 3-4 with the EP1 bulk pair); EP2 IN is the iso feedback and EP2 OUT is unused. A bus reset clears ENDPTCTRL1-3 and every queue head, and SET_CONFIGURATION calls connect again. DN2 1.12 has the same code at other data addresses. `[doc]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: A bulk OUT endpoint fits beside live USB audio: digikit hooks the USB init entry `0x40006c52` (6-byte prologue, same on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12; it runs at boot and again in interrupt context after a controller reset), copies the configuration, appends interface 5 (vendor class, EP2 OUT bulk, 512 bytes), sets wTotalLength 0x158 and repoints entry 5; connect and disconnect touch only the receive half of ENDPTCTRL2. Replies go back over SysEx. A probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads on 2026-11-13: DN2 3.38 MB/s (6.5 MB) and 2.09 MB/s (146 MB in 200 files, audio clean), DT2 2.74 and 1.50 MB/s. macOS keeps audio and MIDI; Windows does not bind it without an MS OS 2.0 descriptor. Not yet tested: long runs, host sleep, a bus reset during a transfer. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: eMMC: both units carry an eMMC 5.1 of 23.05 GiB with identical EXT_CSD: enhanced reliable write supported but not forced, 1 MiB cache off, background operations off, optimal write size 32 KiB. Card clock 37.71 MHz (75.43 MHz divided by 2) on a 4-bit bus in high-speed timing; the eSDHC has no 8-bit mode. `[hw]` (read on the units)

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Stock card driver: data moves by eDMA channel 59 to the eSDHC data port, 16 bytes per request; every write uses CMD23 with the reliable-write bit. The block write and read split every transfer into 64 KiB commands: `cmpi.l #0x10000,D2` at offset 0x14 (entry) and 0x22 (chunk loop) of each function, same bytes on both images: DT2 1.17 read `0x4012e1b6` (sites `0x4012e1ca`, `0x4012e1d8`), write `0x4012e39c` (sites `0x4012e3b0`, `0x4012e3be`); DN2 1.12 read `0x4012c87a` (`0x4012c88e`, `0x4012c89c`), write `0x4012ca60` (`0x4012ca74`, `0x4012ca82`). The 64 KiB bounce buffer for unaligned buffers is the likely reason; the eDMA's 15-bit count allows at most 1023 blocks (511 KiB) a command, which digikit's sdhc-large uses (1022) for 16-byte aligned buffers it registers. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Raw card rates (DN2, 8 MiB, median of 3): write 11.4 / 13.3 / 15.3 MB/s and read 13.8 / 15.6 / 16.1 MB/s with 32 KiB / 64 KiB / 511 KiB commands; reliable write and the card cache change nothing within 2 %. A copy in RAM runs at 18 MB/s, USB alone at 20.9 MB/s (13.5 MB/s while the CPU copies). An upload that reads every file back is capped at about 7.2-7.8 MB/s by the card. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Cost per file: on the DN2 store the cost of an upload grows by about 0.46 ms for each file already stored (the store table is rewritten and read back at every commit), on top of about 95 ms; on the DT2 +Drive about 195 ms a file, with no growth across folders. For sample packs of hundreds of files this matters more than the transfer rate. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / USB take-over failures and card speed (digikit, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: +Drive ids at or above `0x1000000` never reach the card (DT2 1.17): the inode write-back `0x4015b868` and page write-back `0x40155c34` call the block write only for inode ids and page numbers below `0x1000000`; higher ones are copied into RAM tables (inodes at `0x47d73ed0 + n*0x80`, pages at `0x46f63ed0 + n*0x8000`, n counted from `0x1000000`). `[doc]` {digikit-f120}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Pre-send render hook proposal (Modwerk, OS 1.17, emulator)
facts.text: Modwerk's proposal guards the SHARC send-driver entry `0x1c18a6` (short-word PC), displacing one 6-byte instruction and resuming at `0x1c18a9`; the stock caller is at `0x1c3090`. Track buses start at DM `0x252df8`, 256 bytes a track, 32 floats per channel. A sidechain prototype (16 sources x 16 destinations) ran 9,060 SHARC instructions a block in digikit's emulator; with the hook off the PCM was byte-identical to stock. Not on a unit. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: The cleanest place to add a machine: each voice's mono block at `0x80001a18 + 128*v` (32 x int32, Q31). Anything written there before the per-voice processing step gets the stock filter, amp, pan, level, mute and effects for free, and resampling records it too. Bit reduction acts *inside* the stock voice synth, before that point. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Samples: table at `0x403193a0`, 16 bytes per slot `{PCM ptr, ?, length, ratio Q30}`, valid slots 0..130 (`0x82` is the audition slot); PCM is s16 mono. A voice advances its position by 32 x the pitch ratio per block. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Parameter descriptors: `0x401a9d9c + 52*id`. 44 code sites clamp ids >= 164 to 0, so new parameters must fit below 164 or every one of those sites needs a patch. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Heap: `operator new` is `0x400d4180`. Never free a firmware-owned buffer: operator delete halts on a non-heap pointer. Never write message `+0x48` (the next link). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Bound the worst case, not the average: an early granular engine froze the UI at low pitch, because fixed-length source grains became long, the pool filled up and every voice ran its worst case. The fix made grain length independent of pitch and capped overlap. `[hw]` ([I24](../INCIDENTS.md#i24-a-granular-engine-froze-the-ui-at-low-pitch))

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Render path, injection point and key tables (digigrain's platform skills, OS 1.53, Ghidra plus digiemu)
facts.text: Recorder (static reading, not yet run in an emulator; digigrain's recorder skill): the record buffer holds 1,584,000 frames (33.0 s at 48 kHz mono) as two planes written together, the top 16 bits at `0x4237DF90 + 2n` and bits 8-15 at `0x421FB410 + n`, so the reassembled sample is 24-bit. The source selector fills a mono capture block at `0x800032c4`; sources 9-16 (TRK1-8) are a straight copy of the voice block `0x80001a18 + 128*(t-1)`, so a machine that writes the voice block can be resampled for free. Sample slot `0x82` is the recorder's preview slot; a sample-table setter at `0x400763b4` fills a slot and, below `0x80`, its 255-entry slice table. `[doc]` {digigrain-skills}

facts.text: There is no spare per-pattern MIDI block on the DT1; the kit spare at kit + `0x530` and the pattern spare bytes are already used by Digi Matrix, Digi Poly and Digi EQ, so Tone+FX up to 4.1a keeps its Digitakt data in RAM, lost on power cycle or project load. `[doc]` {tonefx-pattern-storage}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Tone+FX 4.3b keeps its Digitakt settings in MIDI track 8's saved kit record at kit + `0x8ba` (the track reserved on channel 16, block magic "DGX4"), so the stock serializer saves them and they survive a pattern switch, a project load and a power cycle. Users must leave MIDI track 8 alone; another mod using that record clashes. Not yet tested on a unit. `[doc]` {tonefx-43b}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / elekloader core 4.1-4.3 and compatibility (2026-11-10)
facts.text: elekloader Digitakt cores and Tone+FX 4.3b: core 4.0 lacks the `fw_tempo` export the stutter needs and cores 4.3 and 5.0 claim its master sites (render `0x400721e6`), so the release ships its own core-4.0.1 (S21). On 1.54 the Digitakt file takes `.run` 20,352 and `.bss` 104,300 bytes. `[doc]` {tonefx-43b}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Cold boot vs LOAD PROJECT: after SAVE PROJECT, a cold boot came back with the sound records' spare bytes cleared, and a stock parameter written straight into the kit was lost too; LOAD PROJECT kept both. Mod data kept in a kit's spare bytes needs its own path through a power cycle (I77). `[hw]` (power cycle) / `[emu]` (the cause)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: The working image survives a power cycle: Digi Perform 0.1.4 copies its data into the working image, the serialized project in RAM that the Digitakt writes to the +Drive at power-off and starts from (`0x406490e8` on OS 1.54, `0x406480e8` on 1.53); the assignments then survived a power cycle on the author's unit (I77). The stock CC send queue is `0x400e0b94` (1.54) / `0x400e096c` (1.53), called from the UI task only. `[hw]` {modwerk-digiperform}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Shared hook sites read registers: CC Names' hook at `0x40030daa` reads the parameter id from d2; Digi Perform called that site as plain C with d2 unset and SRC labels read ERR (I101). `[hw]` {modwerk-digiperform}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Patch sites in use: render after the LFOs `0x40077eb2` (shared with Digi Matrix); TRIG view draw `jsr` `0x400368e0`; SRC-page routines also patched by CC Names and Digi Mono (`0x40030daa`, `0x40032d36`, `0x40032d16`) and by DigiChain/DIGISLICER (`0x4000f534`). Check these before you claim one. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Modwerk Digi Perform (OS 1.53/1.54, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Load: heavy Digi Mono machines with Overbridge streaming run near the audio budget (96 % load shown on a stock page). Digi Perform 0.1.3 takes 26,776 bytes. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The stock render already takes about 85 % of the audio interrupt: Digi CMI's meter (render entry to exit over the block period, timed with PIT0's counter `0xFC080004`, read only; 0.485 µs a tick, about 1,375 ticks a block of 667 µs) read 85 % peak right after boot. In digiemu the render (`0x40077428`-`0x400784c8`) runs about 85,000 instructions a block, 98 % of them stock's; at about 1.6-1.7 cycles an instruction that fits the 85 %. The UI gets what is left, so a few percent more load show as lag everywhere. `[hw]` (meter) / `[emu]` (instruction count)

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Voices that never switch off cost load: released voices kept looping silently and took the meter from 86 % to 94 % (I81). Switch a voice off only by the real amp envelope (below), and clear its on flag (voice + `0x28`), not only its end flag. Digi CMI 0.30 switches a voice off after the amp envelope stays below -90 dB for 64 blocks; 0.26's -72 dB rule read the filter envelope and cut sounding notes (I89, S20). `[hw]` (load) / `[emu]` (rule) {digicmi-026} {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Voice internals (digiemu): voice + `0x00` is the PCM pointer of the sample playing, + `0x10` the gain, + `0x14` the sample length, + `0x28` voice on. AMP kit slots: attack 38, hold 39, decay 40, overdrive 41, delay send 42, reverb send 43, pan 44, volume 45. digiemu does not model the PIT counters. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The real amp envelope is at `0x4199ed64 + 8*v` on OS 1.54 (8 bytes a voice: +0 phase, +4 value), updated by the render's amp stage `0x400716c0` from kit slots 38-40 (attack, hold, decay). Phase 2 attack (value rises as negated Q31), 1 hold, 0 decay (|value| / 2^31 is the level, 0 when idle). After a release it matched the output level within about 5 %. On OS 1.53 presumably `0x4199dd64`, unverified. `[emu]` (1.54) / `[?]` (1.53) {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: elekloader's `fw_amp_env` export (`0x4199ef54` on 1.54) is the filter envelope, despite its name: `0x40073304` fills it from kit slots 29-32 and 35; it fell to -135 dB while a held looping note's output stayed constant. Do not use it as a voice's level (S20). `[emu]` {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Velocity is a square law in stock: both sample players pass the clamped velocity to `0x40074c60`, which returns gain = (vel/127)^2 x (VOL/127). `[emu]` {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitakt (mk1) / Digi CMI on the unit (OS 1.54, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Count divisions in per-sample code: a `rems.l` costs about 20-35 cycles on this ColdFire but one instruction in digiemu's profile; a per-sample remainder in Digi CMI's RETRO made the UI crawl on the unit (I91). `[hw]` (lag) / `[emu]` (fix) {digicmi-037}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Proven room for added DSP code: 83,838 B over four regions (L1 block 1 17,974 B, three code regions 9,798 / 31,606 / 24,460 B). Each function is placed first-fit. Packs that fit: compressor + flanger 48 KB; with the tape echo 80 KB. All four effects together (95 KB) do not fit. L2 code runs through the I-cache like stock L2 code. `[hw]` (builds ran on the unit)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: selcc output is about 10 % larger than needed (field accesses cost 5 instructions). Digiwerk's peephole pass saves ~5-6 KB.

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Their safety lesson: stock code never puts a load into an I register directly before a 48-bit instruction that uses it (0 of ~14 cases; there is always work in between). The SHARC emulator does not model the pipeline, so the cautious pass refuses that pairing. Copy the rule: do not create instruction pairings the stock code never has. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Where DSP code may live, after the probe study (Digiwerk PB01 findings, static, 2026-10-23) {dn2-cfw-pb01}: L1 block 1 above `0x2e4f46` gives about 12 KB, not the 45 KB of the static map, because the build keeps the edge for a 32 KB DM cache. Block 3's tail is the 16 KB I-cache. `0x315f8c-0x318000` in block 2 depends on whether the PM cache there is 16 or 32 KB. Code placed there stopped the DSP on a unit (CMP2's LOW MUP stop), so builds refuse it. L2 candidates: `0x2008823c-0x200918c0` (38,532 B) and `0x200c2000-0x200fa000` (229,376 B). `0x200918c0-0x200c2000` is kept free of data by the build. Other projects use part of that range on units: [CONFLICTS O19](../CONFLICTS.md). Section 7 can grow ~150 KB before its 1 MiB limit. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Code running from L2 in dead stock FX spots stopped the DSP on a unit (Digiwerk SC01, 2026-10-21): knob turns and random idle moments, while the UI stayed fine. 74 minutes of the same recipes in the SHARC interpreter gave 0 faults, so the cause is something the interpreter doesn't model. Stable builds keep their code in proven L1/L2 regions. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-roadmap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: selcc inlining grows the stack: a static helper that selcc inlined pushed one effect's stack to 2,092 bytes; making it non-static brought it back. Check stack use after each build. `[emu]` {dn2-cfw-t53}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Bound every feedback path's output. A held three-head runaway of a tape echo reached 4.24 (18 dB over stock's delay), so Digiwerk added a soft ceiling (linear to 0.5, at most 0.7). Stock's own runaway peaks at 0.526. `[emu]` {dn2-cfw-t53}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: How far the cycle model is off on a unit (dnfw Waverider 0.3.8, DN2 1.11, USB-probe idle measure, 2026-10-29) {dn2-waverider-perf}: A change that the cycle model put at 0.6-0.7 load points for 16 voices measured 2.0 points on the unit, roughly 3x. The unit runs about 1.26x slower than the emulator assumes in general, which leaves ~2.4x unexplained (memory waits are suspected, not checked). With 16 voices of a custom wavetable machine plus a 16-note FM chord, the unit read 60-68 % with no missed frame (peak 71.8 %). Same lesson as rule A35: budget from unit measurements. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Measuring per-stage cycles on the unit (dnfw `waverider-loadmap.md`): Chosen jumps and calls go through a 12-byte stub that reads EMUCLK and adds the cycles since the previous mark to the running segment. A null segment measures the marks' own cost. Results publish through reply word 2, half a record per block. A reusable recipe for any DSP mod. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / DSP code room and load on the DN2 (Digiwerk DT01, DC01/DC02, SC01)
facts.text: Load model used: load = (1.30 x emulated instructions + 11k) / 666,667. For one build it predicted ~74 % where the unit showed ~50-60 %, so the model overestimates. `[?]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Frame: 0xa80 bytes from `0x80005e60`, sent by DSPI2 (16-bit DMA, 1,374 halfwords); the reply arrives at `0x800053a4`, every block (1,500/s). All send-FX, compressor, external-input and master parameters are one block of big-endian words at `0x9fa + 2*(k-25)` (`k` = the parameter row's mirror index; chorus is k 25-31). Compressor routing is at `0xd4` (track bits) and `0xd6`. 16 per-voice rows of `0x92` bytes start at `0xda`. A row is a voice, not a track: a track parameter goes to every row whose owner (`0xa5a + 2r`) is that track. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Audio clock: SSI0 with eDMA 48 (RX) / 50 (TX), 96,000 requests/s. One major loop is one 32-sample block, and vector 170 forces vector 191 (the frame handler). The emulator needs this clock for PLAY to run the sequencer. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Panel and MIDI: Panel MCU on UART8 at 156,250 baud, sent through eDMA 35. LED messages: `B9 i v` (LED i, palette entry v) and `B5 i r g b` (palette entry); see also [`../common/sysex-and-midi.md`](../common/sysex-and-midi.md). DIN MIDI on UART9 at 31,250 baud: out by eDMA 37 (bulk) plus direct writes for realtime bytes, in by eDMA 36. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Notes: MIDI tracks have no voice limit in the output engine; the "4 notes" are only the UI's NOT2-NOT4 rows. A pattern's note pool holds 8,192 notes, with at most 16 notes per step. The MIDI note-output length is a byte counter over a 1,024-byte buffer. Stock 1.12 plays more than 4 notes per trig from a modded project. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: DSP free memory (static): L1 block 2 is never written by the stream (128 KB), the L1 block 1 tail `0x2dd52c-0x2effff`, and L2 from `0x2008823c`. Correction: the startup turns on all three L1 caches, so `0x39c000-0x39ffff`, `0x2ec000-0x2effff` and `0x31c000-0x31ffff` are cache, not free. dnfw's proven code area is `0x2dd600-0x2e7000`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: The frame is longer than its data (elekloader core-dn2 0.3). The driver sends a 0xabc-byte frame but writes data halfwords only for the first 0xa80 bytes; for the rest it writes only command halfwords. So the tail from byte 0xa80 keeps whatever you write there before the call, and stock leaves it zero and ignores it on the DSP side. The driver's transmit queue is at `0x80002510` (one 32-bit entry per frame halfword, command half first); the frame sender calls the driver at `0x40025e9e`. The DSP reads tail word k as halfword 2k+1 above halfword 2k. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Reply word 2 (record offset 8) is free on DN2 1.12: no stock code writes or reads it. elekloader's DSP peek uses it (one halfword per block, ~3 KB/s), and so do digikit's `core/dsp-link` and the `sharc` branch's metrics core, so only one of them can be in a build. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: DSP load on a unit (DN2 1.12, elekloader's idle-task meter, Nov 2026): 666,706 cycles per block measured (the nominal figure is 666,667). Time outside FreeRTOS's idle task: about 80 % with nothing playing, 65 % with 64 notes held. Stock's own block-handler span (reply word 0) shows the same pattern (79 % and 68 %). Neither figure is headroom. Stock's audio task holds the DSP for most of each block and holds it *less* under load, so the share counts waiting. Do not read "80 % busy at idle" as "20 % left". `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: elekloader DN2 machine budget (core-dn2 0.3, experimental): each SHARC machine kind gets 64 KiB of L2 and its own guarded 4 KiB L1 stack. The callback may declare at most 2,048 stack bytes; the rest is shared with interrupts. The peek reads only L1 blocks 0-3 below their caches and L2 below the special window. On a unit, it read the machine stacks' guard words and its own code back exactly. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-adapting}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The ColdFire-to-DSP frame and the panel (Digiwerk T3.2, T3.3, T2.1, T2.4b/c; DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Emulator pitfall: digikit's Unicorn got EMAC fractional mode wrong (MACSR F/I = 1). The frame handler uses it, so values that pass through EMAC can be off in the emulator. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: SHARC: 1,038 of 1,228 DT2 functions (85 %) have a relocation-tolerant twin in DN2 (which SHARC findings hold on both units: [`../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md`](../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). What is missing is exactly the audio engine: the per-slot dispatch `0x1c642a`, the per-track loop and unpack, and the sample players. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: ColdFire UI: 884 of the DT2's 989 C++ classes exist in the DN2 with the same names, base chains and vtable sizes. So DT2 pages (records, formatters, knob lists) can be moved as data. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: The DT2 ONESHOT render (`0x1c4ecf` + `0x1c4f81`, 4 functions and 611 instructions with its callees) was extracted from the user's own DT2 file, relocated into DN2 1.11, and ran bit-identical to the DT2 for all four play modes in the emulator. dn2mk2 and armio's T1E2 later shipped full DT2 sample machines on DN2 1.11. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / How much of a Digitakt II is inside a Digitone II (dnfw `dt2-machine-port.md`, DN2 1.11 vs DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Trap for new machine types: the firmware's per-type voice setup dispatch (`0x8052db90[type]` at `0x1c91ad`) has only five entries. A new type 5 triggered from idle reads past the table and jumps to 0. Extend every per-type table, not only the render loop. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The three ColdFire <-> SHARC layers (dnfw `audio-dma.md`, `dsp-control-block.md`, lalzart cross-check)
facts.text: The audio slots are configuration, not constants: the engine indexes the TDM frame through bytes at `0x80005366-0x80005368` (enable and slot pair), set by an applier (`0x40025982`) from settings and the kit. A per-stream routing mod would change those bytes. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / The three ColdFire <-> SHARC layers (dnfw `audio-dma.md`, `dsp-control-block.md`, lalzart cross-check)
facts.text: Link alignment: a routine searches the receive half for the marker `0x007FFFFF` and, on a hit, slips the DMA by two frames by patching CITER/BITER. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Image identity
facts.text: MAIN OS = section id 3 of the ELE3 container; load address `0x40000400` on Digitone II and Digitone mk1; big-endian; 16-byte header, first instruction `46 FC 27 00` (`MOVE #$2700,SR`) at `0x40000410`. Depacked size: DN2 1.10E 3,085,696 B, DN2 1.11 about 3.19 MB (3,192,192 B per the modding skill), DN1 1.42A 2,420,912 B. CPU ColdFire V4e (octabam loads MAIN OS at the same address). Mutable state lives in SDRAM at `0x80000000`; the bootstrap (section 2) is read at load base `0x800003fc`. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.text: Landmarks (1.10E/1.11): frame ISR `0x40025e0a`; modulation module `0x400daed2-0x400db32e`, kernel `0x400db1dc`, driver `0x400db22c`, MSAC-with-load at `0x400db1f6`; string pool file offset `0x1F7000-0x202000` (load `0x401F7400`+); LFO page labels `LFO1-LFO3` only, `LFO3` at `0x40201cb0`; SETTINGS menu block `0x40200b09`; the unique cosmetic string `PERSONALIZE` at `0x40200b2e` was used as a harmless patch target in dnfw's "Gate E". `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
facts.text: The in-place loader is the hidden size limit. Section 4's loader (`0x8000357c`, stage `0x40200000`) has a stock margin of +31,182 bytes; elektron-firmware-tool's default compression level (`-l 3`) gives -39,318 and corrupts the image. Every build needs a margin >= 0 at both loader stages; elekloader's default packer produced a container too large for the receive buffer, so the DN2 build uses a dense packer (`codec/dense.py`). Stock Digitakt II 1.17 also fails the in-place path (margin -31,912). `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} ([I39](../INCIDENTS.md#i39-the-default-compression-level-corrupted-a-dn2-image))

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Hardware map and budgets (OS 1.12 unless noted)
facts.text: Elektron's own streams keep the furthest match within a 1 MiB window and the longest match at 2,048 bytes; a packer that exceeds them is refused by the build tool. Compressed streams are padded to a multiple of 4 B. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / ColdFire / MIDI side findings
facts.text: The 4-note MIDI limit is code only (NOTE/NOT2-NOT4 rows, `FUN_40055606`, a 4-byte default chord, 4-note SHAPE chords); the engine and pattern format are not limited; the note pool is 8,192 six-byte entries. Traps: the lock-clear path writes -1 to notes 1-4; the 8-bit MIDI output counter at `0x44600ca0` can wrap on large note-off bursts and leave notes stuck. The arp is kept off MIDI tracks by structure (not fully confirmed). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / +Drive and storage (digikit findings 14, 23-24, 35, 43-47)
facts.text: +Drive block records are 128 bytes; the real filesystem uses 32 KB extent-mapped pages with hierarchical directories; MmcFs has fixed-capacity project, sound and kit pools; its bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect bits, not occupancy; a panel SAVE lands in project slot 0 and does not update the MmcFs bitmaps. digikit's card module store uses sectors `0x38000-0x3E000` (blank on a real DT2 card when checked); DT2 modules can live as files in a `/digikit` folder; the USB SysEx store is version 2 with a static receive ceiling of 1.0-1.4 MB/s (about 100 instructions per byte; measured on a DN2 in 2026-11: 0.857 MB/s, see "USB transfer speed on the units"). `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The SHARC's filter accelerators, read on a DN2 (accelprobe, 2026-10-17). The ADSP-21569 has IIR0 and FIR0; the DN2 1.11 engine uses neither. Only 22 of 76 result words matched the models built from the hardware reference; the chip differs in three ways: IIR0 feeds stored word 5 of a biquad into the output: y = A0 x + s1, then s1 = (A1 x + s2) + B1 y and s2 = A2 x + B2 y, each step rounded to float32 (all 40 outputs and 4 states match). FIR0 adds its four partial sums in pairs, (acc0 + acc1) + (acc2 + acc3). In ACM mode the chip writes `0xFFFFFFFF` to a TCB's INIDX and 0 to OUTIDX after a window, the other way round from the hardware reference. Speed bounds, including setup: at most about 22 cycles per biquad-sample and 4.5 per tap-sample. ADI's application note gives the theoretical rates as 6 cycles per biquad (one MAC unit) and about 0.25 cycles per tap and sample (four MAC units), and says the coefficient and state preload dominates small jobs, which fits these bounds from jobs of 8-16 samples {adi-ee408}. The INIDX/OUTIDX write-back in ACM is not described there. digikit's models were corrected to match all 76 words. Same silicon on the DT2 ([crosscheck](../common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md)). `[hw]` {dn2-accel}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: ColdFire tasks on a unit (DN2 1.11, read with the USB probe): The context switch is at `0x40000410-0x40000458`; the ready table at `0x4664ac9c` holds one list head per priority; higher numbers run first. Prio 0 never runs; prio 1 is the real idle loop (entry `0x400cec98`, parked at `0x400cf0e2`); the MIDI task (prio 7) answers the probe. Stack high-water marks after a busy pattern and a save: the fullest is a 2,048-byte prio-10 stack at 27 %; the main application's 160 KiB stack peaked at 1.5 %. Interrupts run on the current task's stack. ColdFire CPU 58-61 % whatever plays, almost all of it the audio ISR; a pattern raises the ISR's worst frame (75-83 % in a busy one), and SAVE PROJECT takes 100 % for about a second. `[hw]` {dn2-cftasks}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / More from dnfw's notes (read 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Stock 1.11 trusts a stored song row count. The song LOAD (`0x400dea6a`) copies `count` stored 29-byte rows into 37-byte live rows without checking it. One project held 21,503 instead of at most 99 and crashed stock and modded builds alike when opened; the damage had entered between two exports. A mod that writes project data must keep every count in range, and a repair tool must use the storage-version-4 offsets (row count at record `+0x147`). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} ([I2](../INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count))

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)
facts.text: Reference disassembler: `m68k-linux-gnu-objdump` 2.42, `-m m68k:cfv4e -z`; objdump prints indexed-mode displacements in hex without `0x` and `d16(An)` displacements in decimal - confirm against raw bytes. Padding `0x0000` words appear as clusters. Bootstrap needs `--adjust-vma=0x800003fc`. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Disassembly pitfalls (agents will hit these)
facts.text: Capstone has no ColdFire mode: 98.95 % of boundaries right over `0x40001000` + 64 KB with 201 divergences (it assigns two bytes to each failed instruction and desyncs; it decodes `00 00 2f 0a` as `ori.b`, which ColdFire removed). Stock Ghidra `68000:BE:32:Coldfire` reached 99.76 % over 512 KB but lacks `movclr.l ACCy,Rx` (flow stops at words `a1c0 a3c1 a5c2 a7c3`, so decompilations of the frame ISR and modulation module may be truncated) and gets MSAC-with-load wrong (accumulator selection inverted). digikit's `68000:BE:32:ColdfireEMAC` module fixes this - re-import rather than switching language on an existing program. Auto-analysis of the 3.19 MB 1.11 MAIN OS takes about 128 s; close the Ghidra GUI before headless runs; some large switches report "Could not recover jumptable" and must be read as assembly. `[doc]` {dn2-mainos-image}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Front-panel LEDs: the LED driver `0x40132148(id, value)` remembers the last value per LED and sends only changes; `LedManager` (pointer `0x446478e0`) is the only route to it, and on each refresh (`0x4002c854`) the first write to an LED wins. The palette is uploaded in three sets (one per LED INTENSITY): index 0 off, 1 backlight white, then eight hues of 16 levels each (red 2-17, green 18-33, blue 34-49, yellow 50-65, cyan 66-81, magenta 82-97, white 98-113, orange 114-129), 130-135 special. Modes: 1 unlit, 2 steady, 3 and 4 blink. `[doc]` (read from disassembly) {dn2mk2-leds}

The TRK SETUP PLAY MODE and MONO NOTE PRIO setters are `0x4004b6d6` and `0x4004b786`. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {elekloader-machines-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 findings v0.45-v0.48 (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Coupled emulator (v0.48): dn2mk2 now runs the ColdFire image (digikit's emulator) and the SHARC image together, one audio block of 32 frames at a time: the audio interrupt once per block, the sequencer timer at its exact rate but up to one block late in phase, one ColdFire packet per block to the DSP and the DSP's status one block later. Its own audit calls this faithful in order and content, not in timing: an interrupt never lands mid-UI code, a DSP overrun is not modelled, and the default "fast" mode runs the UI's 60 Hz tick about 90x too often (the "faithful" mode gets 59 of 60 ticks a second). The unit's ColdFire spends about 56 % in the audio interrupt with the sequencer stopped. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-v048} (I66)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: The SysEx route is CPU-bound. On a Digitone II (OS 1.12, high-speed USB) the firmware's receive chain in the deferred-call task (priority 9) takes at most 0.857 MB/s of SysEx bytes even when nothing handles the message; digikit's store reaches 0.60 MB/s of payload, two requests in flight gain nothing, and its card VERIFY runs at 7.4 MB/s. Receive work and MIDI-task work do not overlap. About 53 M instructions a second are left free. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: A vendor bulk interface fits beside USB MIDI. In USB MIDI mode the port uses EP0 and EP1 only, so a patched configuration descriptor can add an interface with a bulk pair on EP2; in USB AUDIO/MIDI mode EP3 and EP2 IN are taken but EP2 OUT is free, so a bulk OUT endpoint fits there too (devices/digitakt-2.md, {digikit-f123-bulk}; earlier text: EP2 and EP3 are taken (audio and its clock feedback), and the controller has only EP0-EP3. Stock serves the configuration from a pointer in its port table, so a copy in free flash space needs no code change. `[hw]` (enumerated on macOS) {digikit-usbfast} {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Program IN endpoints for 64-byte packets. The controller's transmit buffer is 64 bytes per endpoint: two 512-byte IN packets back to back wedged it until a power cycle (I70). Stock declares bulk 512 but programs its IN queue heads for 64. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / USB transfer speed on the units (digikit, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Measured over the bulk route (64-byte IN packets): echo about 2.3 MB/s each way on a DN2 and 2.9 MB/s on a DT2; an 8 MB sample 3.86 MB/s on the DN2 (0.68 over SysEx), 0.94-1.60 MB/s with verify on the DT2 (0.11 over SysEx); for many small files the per-file overhead dominates. A cable pulled mid-file left only complete files. On the DT2 a sample loaded on a track keeps playing while its file is replaced, since it plays from sample RAM. `[hw]` {digikit-usbfast}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.49 FLEX (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: FLEX replaces BOUNCE (machine type 17, BOUNCE's, so older projects open their BOUNCE track as FLEX with no conversion code). Recorder trigs record a track, IN or MAIN into one of 8 buffers for R.LEN steps; the FLEX track plays the take. BOUNCE had two faults FLEX fixes: its engine read three sound slots the panel never wrote, so a take ignored its panel, and it waited for a +Drive pool directory that a unit with nothing ever sent to the +Drive never has, so every take was refused there. `[emu]` (gated; not verified on hardware)

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.49 FLEX (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Coupled emulator pitfall: digikit's Unicorn halved every fractional EMAC product (0.5 x 0.5 gave `0x10000000`), so the stock parameter smoother `0x400db12a` decayed every voice parameter to about 3 % and FLEX played reversed and about 52 semitones low in the emulator. dn2mk2 models the smoother; other EMAC users stay wrong until the EMAC itself is fixed (rule C10). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.49 FLEX (OS 1.11, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Open on units: an old project silenced every track until a reboot (I73); a FLEX take is much quieter than its input (takes are not normalised); BUF on the SYN page seemed to have no effect for one user (settled in v0.53: every note played the track's BUF and locks were ignored, I87). `[hw]` (user reports) {dn2mk2-v053}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The per-track chain is mono: on the SHARC runner (stock section 7), after a machine renders into its 32-float block, `0x1c8ef1` calls seven stages on that one buffer in place (`0xb8251b`, `0x1cdb56`, `0xb80c39`, `0xb8265b`, `0xb81368`, `0xb82342`, then the amp `0xb80345`), each with its own state block per track (track 0 at `0x250020`, `0x24fa20`, `0x24f320`, `0x250160`, `0x2533e0`, `0x2505a0`, `0x2547a0`). Mono becomes stereo only at the output (`0x1c244d`), which pans the block into `0x259f68 + 0x100k`. Unlike the Digitakt II's stereo voices, so stereo samples would need the chain run twice with a second set of states. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: A TRK recording takes the block after the amp, before LEVEL, pan and the sends: setting a voice's LEVEL and three FX sends to 0 in the frame leaves the recorded block unchanged (SHARC runner). dn2mk2's MUTE SRC does this from the frame ISR's first copy after its voice loop (`0x400275b0`, `jsr 0x40134490`): voice LEVEL at frame word `116 + 2v`, sends at `168 + 2s + 146v` (s = 86-88). `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Exactness costs DSP time: giving up bit-exact Monomachine and Machinedrum emulation (oversampling 4x instead of 12x for SID, 1x reads for DDRW and DENS, float instead of 24-bit products for filters) cut those machines' cost by 9-64 % while holding level within 2.5 dB and every octave band within 20 dB of the originals; the guard then allows more voices. The sound on the unit is not yet verified. `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / dn2mk2 v0.51-v0.52 and the DN2's per-track chain (OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Page LEDs: the eight page LEDs are logical ids 42-49 (two rows of four under FX and MOD). In grid recording stock lights them in mode 2: the edited page palette 33 (bright green), the pattern's other pages 10 (dim red), pages past the length 2 (near-off); outside grid recording no page is green. A mod that turns its own page without passing PAGE to stock leaves stock's green on the old page (seen on a unit with v0.52, I87). `[emu]` (palette, read from stock's code) / `[hw]` (photos) {dn2mk2-v053}. A sound's slot s sits at `sound + 20 + 2s`. `[emu]`

facts.text: DSP budget: about 666,667 cycles a frame on the DN2 (dn2mk2's handoff for a second firmware); the SHARC engine task's stack lives in the FreeRTOS heap at `0x2d08b8`-`0x2dd0b0`, so mod data starts above `0x2dd600`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Pattern change, the PTN view and the settings block (dnfw directjump, OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock prepares each step one step before it sounds. The sequencer prepares its next events at `0x400d9e10`; a cued pattern is armed by the tick routine (`0x400da406`) on tick 2 only, and the switch (`0x400da6e6`) takes its start step from the change counter `0x42c5a91c`. So a change made "now" still plays one step of the old pattern unless that step's queued events are freed. `[doc]` `[emu]`

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Pattern change, the PTN view and the settings block (dnfw directjump, OS 1.11, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock's discard at a pattern change only marks queued records; a marked record keeps its lock until its old time. Rapid cues with sixteen arpeggiated tracks emptied the lock and record pools (`0x40138992`, `0x401389dc`) on builds that only marked old events, not on one that unlinks and frees them. Stock queues an arp request (type 9) for every audio track on every step, arp on or off. `[emu]`
