The heap arena moves `+0x1000` as one block on 1.12 (descriptor `+4` holds `0x4464bbf0`, S22). `[emu]` / `[doc]` {dnfw-osport}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
facts.text: Porting: 1.11 and 1.12 MAIN images share only their first 28 bytes; about 48.7 % of 48-byte windows from 1.11 appear verbatim in 1.12 but at 535 different offset shifts - fixed-address patches do not port; locate hook points by masked byte patterns (`find`/`expect` fields) and pin every mod to its build by hash. Units already at bootstrap 0x0201 will not be upgraded again. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-release-history} {dn2-os-versions}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / OS release history (dn2-cfw `notes/dn2-release-history.md`, dnfw `docs/os-versions.md`)
facts.text: Rules for a new OS version (dnfw): compare decoded content (`dnfw diff`), never compressed bytes; use `--strings` as a filter only; read the densest change blocks first (a relink gives many small blocks, a rewrite one large one); check bootstrap and updater separately (the updater matters for recovery); re-locate every patch via `find`/`expect` and name the target build; examine unfamiliar sections (id 8) before relying on the image; mangled storage-struct names show which persisted state changed. The compression and signing scheme was unchanged in 1.11 and the codec limits were measured on 1.11. `[doc]` {dn2-os-versions}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Section 2 is 30,302 bytes; header `[u32 payload_size = 0x7656][u32 0x80010000]` (the second word is not the load base); load base `0x800003fc` incl. the 8-byte header, payload runs at `0x80000404`; status strings READY TO RECEIVE `0x80006603`, RECEIVING... `0x80006614`, UPGRADING... `0x800065e6`, "BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE" at payload offset `0x602c`. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Receive phase: start marker `0x7F` (kind 1) records the total packet count and starting sequence number; data packets `0x7E` are sequence-checked, their checksum verified over 119 bytes and 101 decoded bytes copied to the buffer; end marker (kind 2) verifies totals. The progress bar measures reception only (`received * 128 / total`). A bad sequence number or checksum sets the state to 0 and the transfer silently stops - no retransmit. Transport is one-way DIN MIDI at 31,250 baud. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Bootstrap and the recovery path (dnfw `docs/bootstrap.md`, 1.10E image)
facts.text: Write phase: the receive buffer is RAM at `0x40000000` holding `[u32 size][u32 checksum][container]`; the container check sums `(word_index ^ word)` over `size/4` words from `0x40000008`; flash is erased in 256 KB blocks from `0x80000` and the raw container is written in 512-byte chunks. No decompression happens here - the updater and MAIN OS decompress sections on the next boot (which is why the in-place loader margin matters). The page does not mention any seal/signature verification in this path. A different routine (`FUN_80011844`) flashes a single small section with a CRC (residue `0xDEBB20E3`) and 64 KB caps - not the recovery path. `[doc]` {dn2-bootstrap}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: The arp is part of the voice interrupt; its only output is the internal voice allocator `FUN_4002a6a2`, nothing on that path creates a MIDI event. Barriers: UI gating by `FUN_40031274` (isMidiTrack) at the ARP key `0x4005f9b6`, menu auto-close `0x400187ea`, LED `0x40060dde`; the step handler `FUN_400d99de` sends MIDI tracks to `FUN_400d8cbe`; live keys on a MIDI track go straight to the MIDI task via `FUN_4012bb90`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: Data: arp settings per track sound record at `kit+0x34+t*0x48b` (`+0x15f` mode, `+0x160` speed, `+0x161` range, `+0x162` note length, `+0x164` step mask, `+0x166..0x175` offsets); track MIDI mask s16 at `kit+0x5cda`; events are 0x6c bytes (alloc `FUN_40138cb6`, schedule `FUN_40138e3c`), MIDI events 0x60 bytes, MIDI task queue `0x445ff870`, free list head `0x4460f4b8` (2,048 entries), MIDI output byte count `0x44600ca0` (8-bit). The arp self-tick is a type-9 event every 90,000 units (1/60 step); one interrupt pass is ~0.67 ms. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - internals collected from the research repos (OS 1.10E / 1.11 / 1.12) / Arpeggiator vs MIDI tracks (dn2-cfw `notes/T2.2-arp-midi-v2.md`, OS 1.12, static analysis only)
facts.text: Hazards for any MIDI-generating mod: the event allocator `FUN_4012a6e8` does not check for an empty free list (test `0x4460f4b8` first); MIDI events take the untransposed note (the task transposes); source byte `[0xd]` 1 = sequencer (subject to mute/solo), 2 = live; length `0x7f` (INF) hangs notes in the MIDI task; the 8-bit output count wraps above 255 bytes per message; latency ~one pass plus DIN serialisation (~0.96 ms per 3-byte note); vector 191 (voice interrupt) is not modelled by the emulator by default. Design options range from UI-only (~0 bytes) to sequenced trigs with p-locks (~850 bytes). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-arp}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / SHARC address map of the boot stream (digikit `docs/SHARC-ADDRESS-MAP.md`, from dn2_firmware_explore, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: `load = exec * 2 + 0x28000000`. Code addresses count 16-bit parcels (VISA), and the entry `0x001c12e2` lands exactly on a loaded region; all 591 of 591 `0x1c`-space jump targets fit. The `0xb8` space (1,025 targets) needs the other mapping (L2 code at `0x20000000`, see the firmware map). `[doc]` {digikit-sharcmap}

facts.text: Regions (DN2 1.11, section 7 836,956 B): L2 `0x20000000-0x2001e880` code (125 KB), `0x2001e888-0x2008823c` data; L1 `0x282403f0-0x2826f000` and `0x282c0000-0x282dd52c` rodata, `0x283825c4-0x2839bffc` code (105 KB); DDR `0x80000018-0x8052fbe0` 5.4 MB, almost all fill. About 240 KB of the 837 KB section is code. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / SHARC address map of the boot stream (digikit `docs/SHARC-ADDRESS-MAP.md`, from dn2_firmware_explore, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: The blob keeps FreeRTOS `__FILE__` strings (`lib\freertos-sharc\tasks.c`, `queue.c`, `port.c` for SHARC_215xx, `heap_4.c`, ...) and the task name "Audio Task", so code can be named from upstream FreeRTOS sources. These addresses never appear as plain 32-bit words; a word scan finds nothing. You need a SHARC disassembler. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / A. Adding machines (elekloader machines-dn2, OS 1.12 only)

Other addresses: owner map for note-on `0x40288306 + 0x14*v`, value-class accessor `0x400c257c`, CC/NRPN lookups `0x400dc978` / `0x400dca5a`, FLTR knob lookups `0x4006efcc` / `0x4006f004`. facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: One mod can run code on the DSP at the master output; a build contains either selectable machines or one master-output mod, not both. DSP = ADSP-21569, SHARC+ VISA instructions; silicon stepping not observed. The writer replaces one stock instruction (the profile's single hook) with a call into a bridge; the bridge occupies a fixed range; mod code sits in L2 starting at PC16 `0xbc8000`; mod data uses byte addresses. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Section 7: 602,076 bytes stored, 836,956 decoded, 95 boot records forming two boot images; later loads overwrite earlier ones in order; the writer keeps record order and bytes except for the one hook and bookkeeping for added records. With no SHARC mod, section 7 stays stock. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Regions (half-open, loader byte addresses): bridge and state `[0x282dd600,0x282dda00)`, bridge pitch table and padding `[0x282dda00,0x282dde00)`, mod (L2) `[0x20090000,0x20098000)`, replaced stock instruction `[0x2838489a,0x283848a0)`, excluded from new code/data `[0x200fa000,0x20100000)`. The mod's 32 KiB splits 16 KiB code + 16 KiB data in the examples; the last 64 bytes of code are a NOP guard (16,320 bytes of instructions). Stack is separate: bridge declares 116 bytes, a mod may declare up to 428 (544 total). `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Addressing: L1 loader address = core byte address + `0x28000000`; PC16 addresses count two-byte parcels (the stock hook at PC16 `0x1c244d` is loader byte `0x2838489a`); the stock data pointer `0x268438` maps to loader byte `0x28268438`; the last stock byte loaded into L2 is `0x2008823c`. An address that exists, or that maps onto another, is not thereby free. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Machine callbacks run on their own stacks (elekloader machines-dn2): synth `0x2de000-0x2df000`, filter `0x2df000-0x2e0000`, 4 KiB each in L1. A callback may declare at most 2,048 bytes; the rest is for interrupts, because an interrupt taken during the call, and a FreeRTOS context switch's 516-byte register save (partly through the PM bus), push onto the running stack. A guard word at each stack's base is checked before and after every call; once broken, the machine is no longer called and its slots play silence. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2-voice}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Writing B7 also loads I7. To switch stacks, write B7 first, then I7 and L7 = 0 (linear), with interrupts off for those instructions, and restore stock's I7, B7 and L7 afterwards. `[doc]` {elekloader-machines-dn2-voice}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Stock constants to keep: M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0, M14 = 1 and both stacks in stock's circular configuration; the master-output bridge saves R0-R8, PX, I4, I5, I12, L4, L5 and the ASTAT/STKY pairs, and everything else is the mod's to preserve (MODE1, MODE2, IMASK, cache configuration, the hardware PC, loop and status stacks). The same constants appear in the DT2/DN2 voice code ([`../common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](../common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md)). `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-abi}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: A 64-byte NOP guard ends every code segment of a mod: the VISA alignment buffer and fetches in flight can run past the last instruction (SHARC+ programming reference 1.5, sections 4-5, 4-6). elekloader states it as a conservative rule, not a proof. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-abi}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Size limits, each checked separately: section 7 stored `0x100000`, decoded `0xfffff`, update including its 8-byte preamble `0x200000`, flash up to `0x380000` with the container starting at `0x80000`. The section 7 limits come from the stock sender's staging buffers; the update limit is a cautious figure measured over USB, not a proven buffer size. None concern mod RAM or stack. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Tests in the suite: SHA-256 of the OS 1.12 SysEx and of section 7 (stored and decoded) pinned in the Python and TypeScript profiles; boot record structure; a no-change write reproduces the stock file; the stock sender's 828 bytes at `0x400cf4b0` hashed against a published analysis; the writer checks packing, the seal, flash bounds and that the main OS unpacks in place safely. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / B. Linking DSP code (elekloader sharc-dn2, OS 1.12)
facts.text: Evidence ladder in that doc: static analysis found no direct access, data reference or resolved pointer range touching the mod's 32 KiB (2,979 pointer rows resolved, 192 unknown, of 25,878 indirect accesses - not a complete proof); an emulator canary kept unmodified stock intact over 44 checkpoints and 5,136 DSP blocks and detected a deliberate corruption (cannot see same-value writes, reads, or writes undone before the next checkpoint, nothing about the real cache); C and assembly builds gave identical 99,904-frame captures; on hardware (USB, one unit) sine variants ran, an L2 variant ran ten minutes over notes 36-84 (392 note/release pairs), pattern/page/send/project-load checks were limited. Not established: program safety, DAC behaviour, heavy-project stress, real cache and interrupt behaviour, total DSP load, cycle margin. `[hw]` {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: Samples travel over USB as SysEx (`dn2samples.py`: hello, send, save, load, forget, lib-send/list/delete/info; Elektron Transfer must be closed). They are written first to a mirror in ColdFire RAM, then fed to the DSP over a TDM "fast link" at about 0.7 MB/s (about 124 words per packet, 1,500 packets/s). Frames are sent first and the directory last so no slot points at missing audio; each 64 KB chunk loaded into the DSP is checked with a VERIFY sum and resent on failure. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: +Drive regions: pool image from sector `0x600000` (3 GiB) with a header sector (`DN2P` in v0.15, `DN2Q` in v0.16) holding length and checksum - the stock storage code does not use anything above 2,224 MiB; library from sector `0x700000` to the end of the device (~20 GB) with a superblock (`DN2L`), an index of 2,048 64-byte entries and up to 64 folders; each library sample is checked with adler-32 before its index entry is written. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: A DSP command handler that reads fields of every command can be set by the wrong one (dn2mk2 v0.39, 2026-11-03): the DSP recorder took words 2-4 of every new link command as its source, channel and threshold. When v0.38 started sending a check command at each take's start, every recording kept 96 frames of its source and then the empty input. Fix: only the recorder's own commands (ARM, NOW, STOP, MONITOR, ARM_PLAY) set those fields. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v039}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: The DSP plays a pool slot only below the directory's count (dn2mk2 v0.38, 2026-11-02). Since v0.33 a live add or a recording went into the first empty slot, which is past the count in a pool without gaps, and only a whole-directory load (power-on, project load) carried the count; so new samples stayed silent until a restart. Fix: update the count with every live entry. Per-project sample lists now sit at +Drive `0x6D0000-0x6E02FF` (two checked copies each), Direct Jump's state at `0x6FF000`. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v038}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: DSP RAM pool: base at DSP address `0x84000000` in the 512 MB DDR; directory magic `SMP1` (count + 128 entries of address, frames, rate, spare) then the frames. A power-on RAM check (`CMD_PROBE`) fills and reads back 256 KB blocks at 143 MB and 256 MB+; if it fails or gets no answer within 4 s the pool stays at 128 MB. Pool sizes by version: 5 MB (v0.14-v0.15), 128 MB (v0.16: 96 MB samples + 32 MB recordings), 400 MB (v0.22+: 0..96 MB and 128..400 MB samples, 32 MB between for recordings, no more than ~5.5 min of recordings). Up to 122 user slots (SAMP 1..122), 124..127 for the recorder. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: Formats: inputs 8/16/24/32-bit PCM or 32-bit float at any rate, mono or stereo; stored as int16 frames in the pool (the doc is inconsistent - an older section says float32); each sample plays at its own rate; recordings 48 kHz int16, peaks between 64 and 32,700 are normalised to 32,700. Slices (max 64): from cue points, `grid:N`, onsets or none; stored with the sample (format word bits 8..15 = count) or, for slices made on the instrument, in a 768-byte area in the last 128 KB of the recordings area (bit 16 marks it). `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / C. dn2mk2 sampler and +Drive layout (OS 1.11; most numbers are version-specific, v0.13-v0.31)
facts.text: Power-on: the RAM check runs first; the pool loads whole in 64 KB chunks; from v0.31 the samples used by the current kit load first and the waveform shows LOADING n%; about 30 s for 20 MB. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-sampler}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)
facts.text: Needs Python 3.12, `uv`, WSL; stock Unicorn has a destructive SR read that corrupts condition flags; install `unicorn==2.1.4 capstone==5.0.7` and the patched Unicorn script. After installing a hook in a harness call `uc.ctl_flush_tb()`, otherwise stale translated blocks keep running. CRLF checkouts break shell scripts under WSL. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)
facts.text: Models enough to boot the control processor, render the panel and take input; storage is not served (eSDHC/eMMC identification only, CMD18 returns zeros). Boot ladder snapshots at 60M/120M/200M/280M/400M instructions; on 1.11 only the 400M rung draws frames. DMA timer 3 at 30 Hz and PIT2 are required or the main task blocks forever. Cold boot plays no notes, turns no encoders, loads no project - emulator zeros cannot refute a crash diagnosis. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / D. dn2mk2 emulator notes (digikit via patched Unicorn)
facts.text: 1.11 section sizes: bootstrap 30,302 bytes (dest `0x02010000`), updater 32,768, blob 836,956, section 8 159,948, meta 15; main application task priority 6, entry `0x4002e688` (on 1.10E). Panel: 55 buttons and 10 encoders; code = channel*8 + bit + 1 for buttons, channel + 1 for encoders; channel 6 is non-linear (code 0x00 is shared by (6,2) and (6,3)); the wire carries a whole-channel state mask and the firmware XORs it against the last state to detect edges; 1024-byte framebuffers flushed by `panel_diff`. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-emulator}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: DSP time overruns cut all audio until power cycle. Every voice that does not rest costs time. Dynamic voice allocation spawns voices faster than old ones die away, so eight tracks can need far more than eight voices; locking each track to one voice avoids it. A guard (v0.27) silences voices that do not fit and a CPU indicator shows when it fires. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: A removed table silenced everything: AMD read a sine table that a later version had removed, so it read uninitialised DSP memory; fixed with a unit test that every table is loaded (v0.30.1/v0.31). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: A guard that wipes with the wrong register (R0 used as loop counter wrote counts instead of zeros) left voices that went non-finite silent until power-on (v0.33 report; fix planned). Non-finite values (inf/NaN) from engine parameter sweeps (e.g. VO-6 at some CONS/CLEN values) are the likely root; the output guard hides them. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: Voices read their sound by voice number as if it were the track (Monomachine engines; ~2 of 16 voices sounded). Same family as the skill's "voices are not tracks" rule ([`digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](digitone-2-os111-reference.md)). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: Stock behaviour users expect to be mirrored: FUNC+turn jumps values to set positions (NOTE by octaves, LFO DEPTH to -128/0/127.98, SPEED to fixed steps; slices count from C1, not C0). Stock mute only drops a muted track's *new* trigs on the ColdFire, so custom voices get no note but sounding notes end via note-off through the stock AMP. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: After an install MD and Monomachine tracks went silent until the track was cleared (intermittent, suspected stale voice-slot state or state carried from an older version's project) - always test an old project after an install. A YES on the OS-update prompt could open the app's own pop-up instead of the update question (keys must be routed to stock questions). `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports} ([I21](../INCIDENTS.md#i21-md-and-monomachine-tracks-went-silent-after-an-install))

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: Custom pages must hand YES/NO back to stock's own questions. With a custom machine page open, the OS's "update?" question (OS sent over USB) and the stock sound preview (TRIG + YES) opened the mod's pop-up or lock menu instead, so the update could not be accepted. Fix: when a stock question or pop-up is up (found in the screen's view list), its keys go to stock. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: DDR holds garbage, including NaN, until written. Delay lines in DDR are zeroed at power-on. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-dsptime}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: A deadline that follows the stock tail (dn2mk2 v0.32): instead of a fixed 0.6 of the frame, each frame measures how long stock's work after the custom voices takes, holds its peak (easing over ~3 s), and sets the limit to min(0.6 P, max(P - tail - P/8, P/4)). Without a reading it stays at 0.6 P. Voices left out are counted, and the newest note always plays. `[emu]` (stress-tested at 3x slower clock) {dn2mk2-dsptime}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: Cost estimate per voice (dn2mk2 v0.33, SHARC runner): instructions + 4 x L2 accesses + 10 x DDR accesses, against 666,667 cycles. The dearest voice (a DigiPRO double-draw) estimates at ~16 % of the frame; most Machinedrum voices at 3-5 %. Moving voice state from DDR to L2 `0x200A0000-0x200A8000` (a range other mods proved on units) was their largest expected saving. The unit's meter is the measure; the estimate only ranks. `[emu]` {dn2mk2-dspcost}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / E. Field incidents reported by dn2mk2 users (lessons for any DSP/voice work)
facts.text: Process: dn2mk2 forked dnfw at commit `8c40698` (2026-10-01), enforces the safety preflight inside `dnfw mods apply`, tightened its DSP limit to the uploader's actual check, runs `scripts/ship_gate.py` on the exact file of every build, and its `CLAUDE.md` requires the ship gate on every build. Versions v0.4-v0.7 were withdrawn for exceeding the 2 MiB USB limit; v0.17 turned PERC into the Machinedrum (25 machines), v0.18 added the Digitakt II sample engine, v0.19 SLICE. `[doc]` {dn2mk2-changes} {dn2mk2-firmware-md}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Which traps are armed: startup enables only ILOPI (illegal opcode, bit 4) and PARI (L1 parity, bit 3) besides the RTOS timer and software interrupts. FP-exception interrupts (FIXI, FLTOI, FLTUI, FLTII) are not enabled: a NaN in TRUNC/FIX sets only a sticky flag. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: EMUI, PARI and ILOPI record an error code and return address (DN2 1.11 at DM `0x26ef88-0x26ef94`: `0x507` EMUI, `0x502` PARI, `0x501` ILOPI), then jump to `idle; jump .` inside the handler, forever. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: How to tell a stop from the sound `[hw]` (inferred from the handler, matching every failed build): Silence (or a buzz from replayed pages) means a trap. The core sits in a high-priority handler, so the audio service can no longer run. A stuck tone (the output DMA replaying its last two pages, ~750 Hz) means a task-level stall, such as an endless loop, while the audio interrupt still runs. In both cases the ColdFire and UI keep running.

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: ILOPI is what toolchains miss: an encoding that selas emits and every decoder accepts, but the chip rejects. Examples are negative shift immediates and selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` (Type 5a), which put the wrong source code for every register from PC up, so `R0 = EMUCLK` became `R0 = LCNTR`. Use the compressed forms. `[hw]` {dn2-stall} ([I27](../INCIDENTS.md#i27-an-encoding-every-decoder-accepts-raised-ilopi-on-the-chip))

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: L1 block 2 is not free just because the image leaves it empty: the PM data cache lives in L1 block 2 (and the I-cache in block 3), sized at boot by `SHL1C_CFG`. Code ending exactly at the last written word lets the sequencer prefetch never-written L1, which can raise a parity trap. Keep written memory after your last instruction. `[hw]` {dn2-dspstop}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: DSP DDR on the DN2: 512 MB, and `0x80531000-0xa0000000` (~507 MB) is free. This was measured on the instrument by filling that range with a pattern at boot and scanning it during heavy playback, pattern/kit changes, FX extremes and a save; nothing wrote there. Stock uses the first ~5.2 MB. `[hw]` {dn2-ddr}

facts.section: Digitone II - machine registration, SHARC mod link, sampler/+Drive layout and field incidents / Reading a DSP stop, and what the silicon enforces (dnfw, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: DN2 stock load from the idle task: ~63-65 % flat, whatever plays. The frame handler's own count (word 0) is ~416k cycles, and a held voice adds only ~8k: the engine renders every voice every frame. Bursts of +40-49 % of a frame come every 15-30 s (more with note starts), also on stock WaveTone. No frame was missed. `[hw]` {dn2-sharcload}

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
facts.text: LOOP-ISA: last 11 instructions of a hardware loop (all of a short loop) must be legacy 48-bit ISA - stock 1.11 obeys it in all 286 loops ([rule A45](../AGENT-RULES.md)). LOOP-END: nested loops must not share an end address. LOOP-LCE: no `IF NOT LCE` in the last 11 instructions of a counter loop. LOOP-CALL: no CALL in the last 5 instructions of a loop. BRANCH-12: at least 12 valid 48-bit instructions' worth of code after every branch. BRANCH-WIN: no two branches in one 48-bit (3 short-word) window. DAG-SAME: no same-DAG DAG-register store and no post-modify same-DAG DAG-register load ("the root cause of silent units"; stock real code has zero of either). PRM references 4-14, 4-41, 4-42, 4-44. The checker reports only violations not present in a stock baseline. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / The static checks, exactly (from `hwrules.py`, `encodecheck.py`, `shapecheck.py`)
facts.text: Encoding census: for every instruction you add, its shape (registers and constants blanked) is looked up in stock real code; bits that are constant in every stock instance must match - catches encodings a decoder accepts but stock never emits (the negative-shift sign-bit case). Shape census: lists instruction shapes stock never uses - not an error, but each must be justified from the PRM. The skill's assembler decodes every emitted instruction and compares it with the intended text, and its 48-bit packer schedules loop bodies so they stay hwrules-safe. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)
facts.text: Framing: `F0 00 20 3C 10 00 <8-in-7 encoded body> F7`; body = sequence (2 bytes, big-endian), `00 00`, opcode, payload; the reply opcode = request OR 0x80. Opcodes seen: `0x01` ping (device name and opcode list), `0x04` screenshot, `0x50` OsUpgradeStart (u32 size big-endian, "sysex", auto-commit byte), `0x51` OsUpgradeWrite (2 KB blocks with CRC32), `0x52` OsUpgradeEnd (1 commit / 0 cancel). OS 1.11's RPC handlers read every u32 big-endian. Upstream documentation: dnfw `docs/midi-rpc.md` (derived from Elektroid). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)
facts.text: Upload pitfall `[hw]`: with auto-commit the OS posts "upload complete" to the upgrade view as the last block is parsed; on the first upload after a boot that view is not open yet, the event is lost and the unit sits on "OS UPGRADE / Receiving". The skill therefore sends Start without auto-commit, all blocks, waits a few seconds, then End(1) - the End handler checks every byte arrived and posts the event itself; the stock OS then validates the container and asks UPGRADE OS NOW? (press YES). Keep USB silent while it writes flash (~90 s), then ping until it answers; one upload, no retries. Raw OS SysEx sent over USB to the running OS is ignored. Python + mido can hang at exit in CoreMIDI. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts} {dn2-skill-setup} ([I4](../INCIDENTS.md#i4-auto-commit-upload-loses-its-complete-event-on-the-first-upload-after-boot))

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Talking to the running unit over USB (MIDI RPC, as used by Transfer/Elektroid and the skill)
facts.text: This explains the "stall on Receiving/PREPARING" reports in Overtone 1.0 and elsewhere ([`../common/recovery.md`](../common/recovery.md)).

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
facts.text: C/asm is compiled with m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os` (no libc) and linked at `0x46800000` (free on 1.11) by `dnfw.patch.cbuild`; dnfw's 138-byte startup loader copies the appended `DNFW` area there at boot and calls your init; every hook site is checked against the stock bytes before it is overwritten - a wrong address fails the build; `context()` asserts bytes a hook relies on without writing them; section 3 is recompressed and the container re-signed. API shape: `jsr(addr, stub, stock=...)` (6 bytes), `jmp(addr, stub, displaced=N)` (the stub replays the displaced bytes), `patch(addr, old, new, why)`. `[hw]` Same toolchain as summarised in [`digitone-2-os111-reference.md`](digitone-2-os111-reference.md).

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
facts.text: Flash space is the binding limit (2 MiB upgrade buffer): dnfw's packer is greedy with a one-step lazy look-ahead over a 32-deep match chain; a 192-deep chain packs MAIN OS 0.8 % and section 7 0.5 % smaller within the same format and window (depth 1024 packs worse); pure-Python aPLib costs ~20-50 s per section in CPython, ~3 s in PyPy; a content-keyed cache skips unchanged sections. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-scripts}

facts.section: Digitone II OS 1.11 - function and data map (from the digitone-2-modding-skill sources) / Build pipeline (`cfmod.py`, `dspblocks.py`, `zcache.py`)
facts.text: Examples: `double_time` hooks `move.l 0x402a0dec,%d0` (6 bytes) at `0x40027ac0` with `jsr dt_stub`, keeps the live d1/a0/a1 via `lea -12(%sp),%sp; movem.l ...,(%sp)`, and caps the doubled step under one 96 ppqn subtick per block (112,000 units); `track_trim` adds an L2 code block, a CALL hook and an fxdsl kernel (-6 dB on track 1, A/B ratio 0.5000).

It runs UI, sequencer, parameters, p-locks, LFOs and builds the 2688-byte frame sent to the DSP for every audio block. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
facts.text: ColdFire: `0x46700000..0x46900000` unused by stock (as the skill states; wrong at its bottom end, settled in [CONFLICTS S17](../CONFLICTS.md)); cfmod links at `0x46800000`, dnfw uses `0x467c8000..0x467fffff` (the skill's figure; dnfw's chunks actually span `0x46708000-0x46f00000`, see [who uses this RAM](../common/memory-maps.md)). More RAM above is plausible but must be verified (fill, reboot, read). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
facts.text: SHARC L2 (contested between projects: [CONFLICTS O19](../CONFLICTS.md)): usable `0x20088400..0x200B0000`; stock loads L2 code only up to `0x2008823c`. Not above `0x200B0000` (stock data points to `0x200C0008` and `0x200C1F84`; `0x200FA000..0x200FDFFF` is non-cacheable DMA buffers; L2 is shared with the boot ROM and one block there stopped a unit from starting). New boot blocks: code at `0x20090000` (sw `0xBC8000`), data at `0x20098000` onward - hardware-proven. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-sharc}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
facts.text: SHARC DDR (512 MB): stock references go up to `0x8052FBE0`; `0x80800000` and above read back untouched on hardware. Large tables can live in DDR blocks (sw `0x800000` on, byte `0x80A00000` on) but every fetch is slow. The delay's L/R rings are masked to 2^18 samples; their upper halves are free if delay time is capped. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-sharc}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Free memory
facts.text: Power-on DDR is garbage (`0xFFFFFFFF`, a NaN, is common). A NaN that reaches a feedback state (send FX, say) silences the unit until restart. The emulator zero-fills DDR and hides this: fill new DDR with `0xFFFFFFFF` in tests. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} ([I8](../INCIDENTS.md#i8-power-on-ddr-holds-garbage-often-a-nan))

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
facts.text: Side channels: the DMA moves 1374 halfwords; the 30 halfwords after the 2688-byte frame (data halves of TX entries 1344..1373) are never rewritten by the stock driver and reach the DSP - write packets there from a hook just before the driver call (header word + checksum, round-robin if larger). Return: reply word 0 = the DSP's cycle count for the block (a load meter), +0x16 = master compressor gain reduction, `+0xa9c..+0xabc` (ColdFire `0x80005e40`, 16 u16) is unused by stock and free as a DSP -> ColdFire channel. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
facts.text: Timing: the DSP renders on the codec clock and does not wait for the ColdFire. A frame that arrives after render started is dropped and the previous frame repeats, including its note-on masks ("the trig lights, no sound"). This is what happens when the ColdFire audio ISR overruns. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire-to-DSP frame (per voice, big-endian halfwords; the DSP swaps halves of each 32-bit word)
facts.text: Voices are not tracks. The DSP renders 16 voices; the ColdFire allocates them per note and copies the track's sound into the voice record; unison uses several voices per note. Note path, lock applier, LFO evaluator and per-voice mirror blocks all work per voice - map voice -> track everywhere. The skill calls this the #1 bug source. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware} {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: Hooks are `jsr stub` / `jmp stub` over N displaced bytes; the build asserts the displaced bytes match stock. Arguments on the stack, result in d0 (GCC ColdFire convention); d0, d1, a0, a1 are scratch. A hook in the middle of a function must preserve d0, d1, a0, a1 for the code after it; a hook replacing a function's entry must preserve the callee's exit d0, d1, a0, a1 and copy every stack argument. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: `movem` accepts only `(An)` or `d16(An)`: push with `lea -12(%sp),%sp; movem.l %d1/%a0-%a1,(%sp)`; recount `sp@(n)` after every push. Every symbol a hook references must be an entry or `--gc-sections` drops it. No libc: zero-initialised locals become `memset` calls and the link fails - use static const data or field-by-field stores. Appended asm after `.bss` lands in zeroed memory and the boot dies in the exception reporter. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: Compiler: m68k GCC `-mcpu=5475 -Os`; build system `dnfw.patch.cbuild` with `cfmod.Mod` as startup loader. cfmod's loader cave: 138 bytes at `0x4028da6e` (copies the appended area to its load address at boot and calls your init); proven asm cave: 170 bytes at `0x4028ea02`; never use the ~64 KB of zeros near `0x402e2000` (the `.data` initializer). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: Audio ISR budget `[hw]`: period ~0.67 ms per block; stock already uses ~64 % during playback; code at `0x46xxxxxx` costs roughly 4x more cycles per instruction than stock (DDR + cache misses) while SRAM at `0x8000xxxx` is cheap. Keep ISR C short, non-blocking, allocation-free; defer per-note work; count DDR accesses, not instructions. A laggy UI usually means ISR work is too heavy. `[hw]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: Slot bounds: every stock value, lock and LFO routine bounds `slot <= 100`; slots 0, 65 and 100 are holes; a sound stores 101 u16 values at `sound + 0x14 + 2*slot`. A new slot means hooking every one of those routines. Your own p-lock record headers need an ID no stock slot uses, and copy/paste/recount/clear routines must skip them. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / ColdFire hook rules
facts.text: Pitfalls: a new parameter record needs a guard record after the last entry (the drawer reads one past); enum formatters print ERR past their table; every per-sound side table needs a reset hook (sound reset and kit creation reuse memory); sound save rewrites LFO DEST words in slots 4, 12 and 20; skipping the stock redraw request can add ~1 s UI latency on hardware (the emulator does not show it); never draw the stock screen and then patch it (panel can receive a frame mid-draw); a new machine type means re-entering every per-type accessor bounded by `type <= 4`. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-coldfire}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
facts.text: SHARC (`sim.py`/`simc.py`, ~200 blocks/s with the C core, ~7 on PyPy, ~1 on CPython): logic and arithmetic in the real frame, stock-vs-mod A/B, memory footprint, the PRM rules it encodes. Cannot cover timing, caches, stalls, interrupts, DMA, branch predictor, ECC, boot-ROM loading, power-on memory contents; "instruction counts under-predict the unit's load". One-time boot ~4 min (`dn2setup.py --boot`). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
facts.text: ColdFire (digikit + `fastemu.py` + `cfkit.py`, 10-30 M instr/s): main OS in Unicorn with HLEs for flash, SD, panel, screen; boots to the main screen (~1 min first time, cached). Divergences: idle skip fires widget timers far more often (redraws look smoother than the unit's ~1/s); encoders register in bursts (single detents do nothing, use `turn_to` with 11-detent messages); holds need >= 12 M instructions; keys right after encoder bursts may drop; Python hooks do not fire under the fast stepper; panel TX ring is never drained; no DTCN2 timer; plain Unicorn halves fractional EMAC results (use digiemu's patched Unicorn); test from several start offsets - a real bug fails at every offset. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Emulator coverage (skill's view)
facts.text: Measuring on hardware: a screenshot RPC (`dn2rpc.c shot`) lets a mod publish a debug page; DSP load = reply word 0; ColdFire ISR time = DTCN2 stamps at hook entry and before the RTE (`0x40027bbe`). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-emulators}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Flashing notes from the skill's setup
facts.text: Flash with `scripts/rpc_flash.py IMAGE.syx` over USB or Elektron Transfer and confirm on the unit. Keep USB quiet for ~90 s during the flash write. The first upload after boot is lost with auto-commit; kill stale flasher processes before rerunning. Python + mido can hang at exit on CoreMIDI. Avoid flashing or measuring during heavy local jobs (USB MIDI timing). Raw SysEx over USB to the running OS is ignored (only the update protocol works). Recovery: FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, DIN MIDI, ~12-15 min. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-setup}

facts.section: Digitone II (OS 1.11) - engineering reference from the digitone-2-modding-skill / Flashing notes from the skill's setup
facts.text: Toolchain: `gcc-m68k-linux-gnu` / `binutils-m68k-linux-gnu` with `-mcpu=5475` on Linux/WSL; on macOS build GCC 13 and binutils 2.42 from source; PyPy 3.10+, `cffi`, `mido`, `python-rtmidi`; dnfw from angellinares/dn2_firmware_explore; digikit (the skill clones m-dwyer/digikit and applies `scripts/digikit-local.patch`). The stock-file check: SHA-256 starts `2af43e65` and ends `72e0` (the full value is `dn2paths.STOCK_SHA256`; elsewhere in this repo: `2af43e65e3d8390b41c9f66222620f8cce027d73ed87db00c80b440f628472e0`). `[doc]` {dn2-skill-setup}

facts.section: Digitone II / From the official manual (OS 1.12; first part only - the MIDI appendix C was not reachable)

TRIG modes: TRACKS, VELOCITIES (TRIG 1-15 = velocity 8..120 in steps of 8, TRIG 16 = 127), RETRIGS (1/1 ... 1/64). `[doc]` {dn2-manual}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: The OS keeps its C++ RTTI, enough to name most code: on 1.12, 12,350 functions and 1,624 types (752 classes, 872 lambdas), 741 with vtables; about a third of all instructions sit in a function that RTTI names. A function that loads a vtable is a constructor or destructor; a `std::function` lambda's typeinfo names its enclosing method with the signature. The DSP has no application RTTI. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: 1.11 to 1.12: sections 2, 4, 7 and 8 are byte-identical (the DSP did not change); section 3 is relinked (+4 KB, BSS +0x1000, DMA alias +0x8000). Overtone ships on 1.12 by translating every 1.11 patch address through a code map built from anchors of 10 matching instructions. `[doc]` {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Cache map (OS 1.11 and 1.12): the bootstrap leaves the data cache off (CACR `0x000cc100`), but the main OS start-up at `0x40000554` writes CACR `0xa50ce100` and ACR0 `0x4007e020`: `0x40000000-0x47ffffff` is cached copyback, everything else uncached, including the SSI DMA buffers at `0x4e6e7100`. Reading those buffers byte by byte from a mod is slow enough to stall the sequencer: Digiwerk's first multichannel USB build (UM01) packed the SSI slots with byte-wise uncached reads and lagged until unusable; reading each of the 14 slots once as a 32-bit word (UM02) ran on the unit with busy sequences and no lag. Checking only the bootstrap's CACR gave a wrong "cache off" conclusion first, corrected the same day. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-handoff} {dn2-cfw-usb} ([I10](../INCIDENTS.md#i10-byte-wise-reads-of-uncached-dma-buffers-stalled-the-sequencer))

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: DSP works per block; the stock handler can be interpreted offline (sharcvm); new effects are portable C, compiled with selache/selcc and spliced into the DSP section. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Board PCBA0109B, read from photographs of the parts (dnfw `docs/hardware.md`, 2026-09-12) {dn2-hw}. The same board number as the Digitakt II is reported. CPU: ColdFire MCF5441SCMJ250 (MCF5441x, 250 MHz). Not the V4e that older notes inherited from the Octatrack. RAM: NANYA NT5TU128M8HE-AC, 128 MB DDR2. Flash: Winbond W25Q128JV (16 MB SPI NOR, by the ColdFire). Storage: Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 (32 GB eMMC). DSP: ADSP-21569 (KBCZ10) with its own Kingston DDR3 beside it. Codec: AKM AK4621EF, 20 MHz crystal by the SHARC. There is no flash chip by the DSP: the ColdFire boots the SHARC (section 7 is its boot stream). `[hw]` (photos)

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Flash-part mismatch worth knowing: the bootstrap's DYB sector protection (`0xE1`) is applied only on a Spansion S25FL (`0x01 2018`), and digikit's DT2 reading names that part. On a unit with the Winbond part, that lock has no effect (Digiwerk T1.5/T1.4). Do not count on hardware write protection of the bootstrap. `[?]` {dn2-hw} {dn2-cfw-t15}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Third-party claim about the family (not measured): Digitone mk1: two MCF54415 plus a Spartan XC3S50A. Digitakt mk1: one MCF54415. Digitakt II: one MCF54415-class part plus the ADSP-21569. Syntakt: two MCF54415, XC3S50A and XC3S200A (the latter driving the analog side). digikit's Syntakt 1.42 reading (an FPGA section, a second ColdFire program) fits. `[?]` {dn2-hw}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Cross-device transplant (armio's R012, DN2 1.11): the Digitakt II 1.16 sample machines and their UI (ONESHOT, WERP, STRETCH, REPITCH, GRID, SLICE, stereo samples, sample browsing) run on a Digitone II. Donor routines are extracted from the official DT2 file and relocated at build time. `[doc]` {armio-r012} The same build makes USB AUDIO class-compliant with 42 capture channels (48 kHz/24 bit, 21 stereo pairs) and a stereo return. Digiwerk's USB01 note sketched this. `[doc]` {armio-r012} R013 (2026-11-05) adds the missing sample-storage setup: SYSTEM > FORMAT SAMPLES creates a sample filesystem in an area the stock OS does not expose as sample storage, and erases that area (including other mods' data there). Formatting, restart, Transfer capacity (about 20 GB on the tested DN2) and uploads afterwards passed on the unit. `[hw]` {armio-samples}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: Two independent 42-channel USB audio builds now exist for the DN2, on different OS versions: armio's (1.11, above) and Digiwerk 0.3.0 (1.12, USB MULTI/MIDI as a fourth USB CONFIG choice; UAC 2.0, 48 kHz/24 bit; inputs 1-32 the 16 tracks, 33-34 main, 35-40 delay/reverb/chorus returns, 41-42 the inputs; used with a Mac and with AUM on an iPhone). Digiwerk's USB addition changes only the main OS, leaving each build's DSP section unchanged. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-030} {dn2-cfw-usb} Historical size estimate (UM03): the USB addition's code and BSS added about 2.6 KB to the existing 1 MB mod region. `0x47e00000-0x47e075a4` describes the combined used span, not the USB addition alone; this is not a size measurement of the later UM04 implementation shipped in 0.3.0. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-um03} Recorder adds recording/resampling, source selection, normalization, trimming, audition, saving to +Drive and optional track assignment. VOICE cycles Voice Setup, Sample Manager and Recorder. Exact trimmed-file comparison and full Recorder-source coverage remain unverified. `[doc]` {armio-recorder} R012 requires only the two official OS files. Native and browser builds verify the final SHA-256; the browser builds locally without uploads. No sample bank or factory library is required; historical exact T1E2/R003/R008/R011 builds still need their original private bank. `[doc]` {armio-r012} {armio-browser} R012 stable is owner-confirmed for stock audio, samples, Recorder and USB audio, including after project changes. This is not exhaustive workflow or endurance validation. `[hw]` {armio-r012}

facts.section: Digitone II / Architecture
facts.text: USB audio repeating old audio after a project change (armio, R007-R011; fixed 2026-11-03): USB audio froze or repeated while headphones and UI kept working; accepted publications stopped, rejected ones rose by 16,392 in about 10.9 s, and USB transfers kept running. Cause: the render-time TX selector follows RX completion and is not a TX ownership grant, but the build had bound the retained queue head to a destination derived from that older phase. R011 picks the candidate from the current DMA START and leaves the ownership guards to decide; the owner confirmed playback after project changes, and R012 is the stable build. Endurance and end-to-end USB latency are unmeasured. `[hw]` {armio-usb} {armio-r011} ([I13](../INCIDENTS.md#i13-usb-audio-repeated-old-audio-after-a-project-change))

facts.section: Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)
facts.text: Incremental working-state updates are a separate persistence path from whole-project saves. In armio's port, sample load/unload updates a separate identity companion and sends the native ProjectSettings notification. Its queued worker `0x400469E2` calls settings serializer `0x400DF57A` at `0x400469FE`; it does not pass through whole-project serializer `0x400E1494`. The extension had been attached only to the latter, so the native settings mirror advanced while the added sample mirror stayed stale. The alternating boot snapshots at sectors `0x40000` / `0x48000` are separate from explicitly saved project slots (see the existing [storage map](../common/memory-maps.md)). R020 replay reproduced a new identity absent from the prepared backup and from a fresh emulated boot. R022 updates the working companion at the narrow settings-worker callsite under the existing project mutex, checking destination, owner, readiness and matching UIDs; explicit saved companions remain untouched. Unchanged identities skip the 16 KiB copy/CRC. Load, unload, fresh-boot restore and failure guards passed native replay; physical shutdown and freeze recovery are unverified. These extension defects are not evidence of a stock DN2 autosave bug. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I52](../INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot))

facts.section: Digitone II / Sampler port lifecycle findings (DN2 OS 1.11, 2026-11-06)
facts.text: A Machine change can leave a port's old SYN view attached even when the Sound has changed. Native selection reselects the view when audio/MIDI classification changes; stock synth to a ported sampler remains an audio track. Generic Project, ActiveTrack and Sound notifications redraw but do not replace the view. R020 replay reproduced knob D reaching the stock handler after switching to all six samplers. R021, included in R022, reconciles the exposed SYN view through the existing factory and native selector on the next UI poll, deferring during modal ownership, selected-trig edits, construction and expired ownership. Ten transitions and nine guards passed. Earlier tests explicitly selected SYN before turning D and therefore repaired the state they were meant to test. Hardware confirmation is pending. `[emu]` {armio-r022} ([I51](../INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines))

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table
facts.text: Overtone: LFO 3's storage holds ARP 2, so a sound that used LFO 3 loses it; ENV3/LFO3 no longer exist in Overtone. `[doc]` {overtone}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Each parameter is one 60-byte row. Table base `0x401f83a4`, stock 321 rows. Offsets: `+0x00` group (set/page family), `+0x04` k (the slot that holds the value in its set), `+0x08..0x14` min/max/default/bipolar, `+0x18` MIDI CC, `+0x1c` NRPN, `+0x20` Overbridge id, `+0x28..0x38` names/formatter/suffix. A separate RAM display table holds glyph, lock flags and randomiser data. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Row ids are not saved; projects store values by slot k through fixed k-to-stored-id tables. Slot maps and CC/NRPN maps are rebuilt from the table at each boot (`0x400dc634`); page records are built at boot from code constants (`0x400c2c4e`). Moving the table does not change project storage; new rows do, via their k and display flags. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Grown table at `0x47D00000`, room for 384 rows (`0x180`), copied at boot by `pg_boot` (called from `0x40000568`). New row ids `0x141`-`0x17f` (63 ids); the same-length-edit ceiling is `0x1e0` (480 rows). 56 address operands in 53 functions had to be redirected; 57 row-count compares changed (`#0x141`->`#0x180`, `#0x140`->`#0x17f`; five look similar and stay). The display-table reader at `0x400c257c` has its first 10 bytes turned into a jump plus two nops. The MIDI input cache (33 constants in five functions) grows by 12,852 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: The grown table ran on a unit (Digiwerk GT00/GT01, OS 1.12, 2026-10-13): boot, cold start, +Drive project save and load were all reported fine, and GT01 added 17 hidden rows for the 3-band compressor that later shipped (CMP3). In the emulator, not one instruction read the stock table after the boot copy. Since projects store values by slot k, and stock saves FX k 25-69 only, values in new slots k 70+ need their own storage (the 3-band compressor uses 28 FX-record words that stock never writes or reads). Whether such a project opens cleanly on a stock OS has not been reported. `[hw]` {dn2-cfw-t65}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: New rows carry Overbridge ids of `0x400` and up. Each is sent to the plugin as soon as its value changes; what the plugin does with an id it doesn't know is not known. `[emu]` {dn2-cfw-t65}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Map builders hold 101 entries each, so k must stay in range (0..100 for sound/FX/MIDI, 0..25 for trig). Stock saves FX k 25-69 only; FX k 70+ and sound k 65 and 100 are not saved. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Rules for a new row: use a free k in the set's table, one row per k (the last row written wins and can silently replace a stock knob); value 0 must keep classic behaviour (existing projects store 0 in slots stock has no row for); send-FX rows set `flags_set = 8` so they are never lockable; synth rows use free saved k values (FM Tone 34, 49; WaveTone 50-64; FM Drum 55-64; Swarmer 33-64); no randomiser; MIDI: no CC already in the set's map, none in 32-63, none taken by the CC parser (1, 2, 6, 64, 66, 94, 98, 99, 110, 120, 121, 123), NRPN 398 at most; Overbridge id outside stock's 0..387 (e.g. `0x400`+n, untested with the plugin). `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: P-lock trap: a row is lockable when display flag bits 0 and 3 are clear; locks are stored as (track, k), so an FX row with k 70 could create a lock on a sound's slot 70, which stock would play back. A bad row can write past map tables, replace a stock knob, or leave stray p-locks that persist after returning to stock. A project saved on a grown build and loaded on stock 1.12 is untested on hardware. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Parameter table / Parameter table details (OS 1.12; dn2-cfw `docs/parameter-table-growth.md`)
facts.text: Checks used: brick checker 12/12 for GT00/GT01 ("a pass is not proof for code changes"), `scripts/t65_build.py check_rows` for FX rows, `pg_boot` only skips ids outside `0x141`-`0x17f` (it does not check k, flags, CCs or Overbridge ids), an emulator run of 7,100 MIDI messages giving the same 991 parameter sets as baseline. Never flash `param-test-dn2` or `fx-page2-dn2`. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-param-table}

facts.section: Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)
facts.text: A stock DN2 has no sample filesystem, and a mod that mounts one must also create it (armio R012, 2026-11-03). R012 mounted an existing sample filesystem but did not create one on a unit that never had it; on such a unit Transfer showed 0% Free / 0 bytes, uploads stalled and connections failed. The author says stock FORMAT +DRIVE, EMPTY RESET and FACTORY RESET do not create it and can erase projects. The bug was found by new users; the author's own unit had storage prepared during development, which is why owner testing missed it. A test on a freshly flashed stock unit is the only check that catches this. `[doc]` {armio-samples} ([I12](../INCIDENTS.md#i12-a-sample-machine-mod-could-not-create-the-storage-it-needed))

facts.section: Digitone II / Sample memory (dn2mk2)
facts.text: Stock eMMC TRIM can fail with TRIM ERROR on a busy card (OS 1.11). A unit running dn2mk2 v0.39 stopped with TRIM ERROR at two different sector ranges while erasing mod data. dn2mk2's reading of the stock code: TRIM `0x4012c4b2` fails only when CMD35/36/38 get no answer (command timeout); after CMD38 the busy wait arms the DAT0 edge interrupt (`0x4012c53e`) before testing DAT0 (`0x4012c544`), so a short TRIM whose card finishes in between leaves a stale semaphore post (`0x4461b6c0`), the next TRIM on a really busy card returns at once, and the call after it gets no answer. The driver has no timeout. v0.40's fix: read the eSDHC present-state register `PRSSTAT` `0xfc0cc024` before every TRIM and verify read and call only when the card is idle; retry a failed call five times (TRIM is idempotent); report ERASE PAUSED and continue on request. The error is `[hw]`; the race is a static reading of stock code, not seen on the bus. Anything that issues TRIMs through the stock driver on a DN2 (and, not checked, a DT2 with the same driver) should do the same. `[hw]` {dn2mk2-v040} ([I1](../INCIDENTS.md#i1-stock-emmc-trim-fails-with-trim-error-on-a-busy-card))

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
facts.text: The Digitone mk1 is a Digitakt mk1 plus six keys, a second ColdFire and an FPGA. taktone runs Digitakt 1.53/1.54 main OS builds on Digitone hardware by replacing only section 3 and adapting the panel, LEDs, codec start-up, autosave GPIO and shutdown copy. Four 1.53-based builds were reported working on hardware. `[hw]` Both main CPUs set up 128 MiB DDR at `0x40000000-0x48000000` (cached and uncached aliases are the same RAM). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
facts.text: How the main CPU drives the second ColdFire (board interface, from taktone-extended, which ran its own engine on it): Reset: PB6 held low. Releasing it starts a serial boot. Upload: the main CPU is DSPI2 slave (eDMA 29, vector 149) and the secondary supplies the clock. Section 6 (a 1,504-byte loader stream; dnfw's section table lists it as 1,492 bytes and "unidentified") loads section 7, which runs at secondary `0x40000400` from entry `0x40000B92`. Shared SRAM: FlexBus, main at `0x10000000`, secondary at `0x00000000`. Native use is below offset `0x7a0`: a 928-byte parameter packet at `0x000-0x39f`, then eight mono voices of 32 signed 32-bit samples at `0x3a0-0x79f`. Handshake: the secondary writes `HO`/`HA`; the main writes 1 to +2 before `B0` to +0. The stock secondary then writes `A5A5` at +4. Render request: a PA4 edge triggers the secondary's DTIM0 capture (vector 96). The secondary signals back through EPORT4 (vector 68). One block of pipeline: ~0.667 ms. Clear stale shared words at start, because they can survive a main reset. Never wait in the audio IRQ for late output, and bound the start-up polling. `[hw]`

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
facts.text: The FPGA bitstream is in section 7: decompressed from `0x400077A0` to `0x40009000`, 54,664 bytes, sent as 16-bit words over the secondary's DSPI1. This is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX's and Analog Four MKII's FPGA sections, a strong lead for research map T12. Stock FPGA polling can stall forever, so keep a main-side timeout. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications)
facts.text: Two SysEx addressings: the startup menu's OS UPGRADE receiver always expects Digitone-addressed SysEx (device `0x0d`). A running Digitakt-based application expects Digitakt addressing (`0x0a`). So recovery to stock Digitone always goes through the startup menu over DIN. `[hw]` (first install confirmed over USB)

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
facts.text: Split the work: keep sequencer, locks, LFOs, menu and storage on the main CPU; render on the secondary from a complete control snapshot. Compile secondary code for `-mcpu=54418 -msoft-float`, freestanding.

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
facts.text: Shared protocol (taktone's, versioned): a ready tag, committed/completed sequence words, eight 28-byte controls and an XOR checksum; outputs as eight 32-frame int32 mono blocks at `0x3a0`; only aligned longword writes with readback: no byte writes to shared RAM, and any mismatch disables submission; one packet outstanding, never block the audio callback, and shut down after 64 consecutive misses.

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
facts.text: Hook points on the main CPU (Digitakt 1.53 application): triggers are captured at `0x40077F8E`, before stock source processing consumes them; voice PCM is substituted at `0x40077FBA`, before filter, AMP and mix. On the secondary, init is patched at `0x40000B7A` and the stock engine init at `0x40000B80` is skipped.

facts.section: Digitone (mk1) / Digitone Keys / The board and the second ColdFire (taktone, DN1 1.43 with DT1 1.53/1.54 applications) / Writing your own engine for the second ColdFire (taktone-extended's contract)
facts.text: Memory: taktone shrinks the native buddy heap from 16 to 8 MiB to reserve `0x4319D6B0-0x4399D6B0` for its runtime, with guard words at both ends. The sample pool (`0x43BAF5F0-0x47BAF640`) and the audio-input ring (`0x47C00000-0x48000000`) stay untouched. This is the same heap-reservation idea as SyntHack's modarea on the Syntakt. `[hw]` (Sophie on the secondary ran on units) / `[doc]` (addresses)
