facts.text: joelanders/gearmulator-md-mm source (`source/elektron/md/mdLib`: memory map, types, board scheduler comments). Key {gearmulator-md-mm}. Projects: [../../catalog/machinedrum.md](../../catalog/machinedrum.md), [../../catalog/monomachine.md](../../catalog/monomachine.md). The short version: an early-2000s three-chip design (an old ColdFire plus two Motorola DSP56303s). It is nothing like the DT2/DN2: no SHARC, no FreeRTOS budget model, and no USB. Its flash updater lives in a boot sector that the OS itself can rewrite.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
facts.text: CPU: ColdFire MCF5206E. It runs the OS (UI, sequencer, MIDI, kits, parameter conversion, flash, DSP control). Older notes say MCF5307; the board model and the MAME driver both identify an MCF5206E. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
facts.text: DSP2 ("producer"), a DSP56303: renders the 16 machine voices, one 32-sample mono block per track per audio block. It holds the machine code, the stock sample data and the sample RAM. Custom machines run here.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
facts.text: DSP1 ("mixer"), a DSP56303: track effects, mix, master delay/reverb/EQ/dynamics, and the six-output codec. Custom-machine work leaves it untouched.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
facts.text: Links: ColdFire to each DSP over the HI08 host port. The DSP-side handler takes an address and a count and DMAs the words into Y memory; this is how parameters reach a voice. DSP2 to DSP1 over ESSI0 (one block per track); codec on ESSI1. MIDI on ColdFire UART1; front panel on UART2. The old idea that the ColdFire plays voices through a DSP SCI port is wrong. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum silicon
facts.text: Timing: 44.1 kHz, 32-sample blocks. DSP1 at 101.6064 MHz = 73,728 cycles per block. DSP2 at 98.784 MHz = 71,680 cycles per block. Its program never sets the PLL, so the boot stub's setting stays. The emulator clocks it at DSP1's rate and so overstates the budget. The two budgets cannot be pooled. `[hw]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
facts.text: The whole producer pass (16 renders plus dispatch, updates, interrupts and DMA waits) must fit in 71,680 cycles. A severe overrun on hardware first crackled, then lit every LED and left the engine silent. `[hw]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
facts.text: Per-track floor of ~3,290 cycles (measured on hardware): each track's 32-word block travels to DSP1 over ESSI0 at ~100 cycles a word, double-buffered. Track k's transfer runs during track k+1's render, so a track costs `max(render + ~40, ~3,290)`. Time saved below the floor is lost, not banked. Making a cheap machine cheaper gains nothing. `[hw]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
facts.text: Planning numbers (emulator): an idle track 3,438 cycles; stock TRX/EFM/E12/P-I voices ~2,000-3,200. `[emu]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Machinedrum budget facts (DSP2)
facts.text: External-memory wait states (the emulator ignores them; measured on hardware): ~1 wait state in areas 0-2, ~5 in area 3 (`0x1C0000+`). A machine with many external accesses costs several thousand cycles more on hardware than in the emulator. `[hw]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
facts.text: In emulated cycles, a busy kit costs 38,789 per block (54 % of 71,680), and the most expensive stock kit, 16 ROM machines, up to 67,309 (94 %). `[emu]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
facts.text: Kitbasher measured that pipeline interlocks alone add a median 26 % on hardware, so the dearest stock kits sit close to the limit. Treat these numbers as a floor.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / How full DSP2 is with stock kits (MModule research 04, OS 1.63, emulator)
facts.text: MModule found `$020000-$0FFFFF` of the emulated DSP's shared P/X/Y never written by the 1.63 program (found by poisoning memory and playing all 104 machines). That is emulator memory: check what a real unit decodes there before relying on it (compare the `P:0x400` lesson below). `[emu]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
facts.text: Flash appears at both `0x0` and `0x10000000` in the emulator. On hardware, after the OS remaps CS0 nothing decodes the low window: images with low-window flash pointers boot in the emulator and hang on the unit. Link and point through `0x10000000`, and scan images for low pointers. `[hw]` ([I38](../INCIDENTS.md#i38-low-window-flash-pointers-boot-in-the-emulator-and-hang-on-the-unit))

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
facts.text: `P:0x400-0x4FF` on DSP2 is not internal memory on hardware (the cache is on, so internal P ends at `0x3FF`). Early prototypes put code there. `[hw]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
facts.text: No pipeline interlocks, no wait states and no instruction-cache timing in the emulator. Bit-exact tests can't see any of them.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Emulator vs unit (Gearmulator's Machinedrum board model)
facts.text: A coarse CPU/DSP time slice (125 µs) produced false "missed blocks" that look exactly like overruns. Use a 30 µs quantum before blaming your code. `[emu]` Rule A23 ("success is no proof") applies with force here.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: ColdFire ISA: `movem.l d0-d1,-(sp)` is a 68000/68020 form ColdFire lacks. Emulators run a 68020 core, and the first trigger of every new machine froze the unit. Kitbasher allows only ISA_A for the MCF5206e (no MAC in added code) and decodes the final image from every entry point (rule A42).

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: Boot-time memory: Ordinary stores to flash relocation sites hung the unit at the boot screen; the emulator ignored them. Boot writes from `0x2bd000` up froze a MKII +Drive UW at the logo, while the same image without them booted. Use only hardware-proven RAM ranges. Boot code must not push registers before the OS has set up a stack.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: The host port to the DSPs holds about two words; the emulator buffers thousands. A sender whose poll timed out left DSP1's handler armed, so the next stock send was shifted by two words. A loader interleaving its writes with the OS's put a thousand words at a wrong address. Send exactly as stock does (interrupts masked) and own the port for the whole transfer.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: The per-step trigger loop is hot: a hook doing a table lookup and register save on every call froze the audio with 12-16 tracks triggering (CPU! lit). It was found only by a hardware bisect. Cache, then exit early.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: Never remove stock DSP pacing. Replacing a 480-cycle DSP1 pad contributed to that freeze. Letting DSP2 skip ahead on silent tracks starved the ColdFire's stream and lost triggers.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: No long `rep` on a DSP path: `rep #$600` (clearing 1,536 words) overran the CPU on the first P-I bass-drum trigger. Changing it to `rep #1` proved the cause; two stores per `do` pass fixed it. This is the same rule as on the Octatrack.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: The stock DSP1 watchdog: DSP1 counts blocks that DSP2 delivered late. On the third in a row it stops the output DMA and spins, silent until a power cycle. Half a percent over budget for three blocks is enough.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: DSP correctness traps: Nested `do` loops sharing an end address left state on the real hardware stack, and DSP2 hung. An inherited modulo register wrapped a 384-word clear into 32 words. DSP2 external RAM holds power-on garbage (the emulator reads zero), so init must clear everything it reads, and every block must write all 32 samples.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: Machine ids 124-127 fall inside the OS's "control machine" range tests.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: Pin data assumptions: after a firmware update, wavetable models went silent because older UW sample sets were shorter than the new build expected. Declare minimum lengths.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / What crashed, froze or corrupted real Machinedrums (Kitbasher's FIRMWARE-SAFETY, mostly a MKII +Drive UW)
facts.text: What the emulator does not show, in numbers: DSP56300 pipeline interlocks add a median ~26 % (12-47 % per model). Instruction-cache misses and wait states: 16 copies of one model fit in the emulator and stalled on the unit. The emulator's default 441-sample slicing invents host-port spins of ~13,000 cycles. Use 64- or 8-sample slices, and don't "fix" spins it invents.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
facts.text: `move #16,a` loads a fraction (`a1 = $100000`), not 16. Write integers into data-ALU registers in the long form `#>16`. Address registers and the ALU immediates (`cmp`, `add`, `sub`) take integers.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
facts.text: Moving an accumulator to memory saturates: `move b,a` limits, `tfr b,a` doesn't. After `and #mask,a` take `a1` explicitly.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / DSP56300 pitfalls (from building custom machines)
facts.text: The reference assembler (mborgerson/dsp56300) accepts overlapping `ORG`s silently, so validate its output before packing: one contiguous segment, inside its bank, no warnings, entry points inside. A DO loop's end label goes on the instruction after the last loop instruction. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: The OS `.syx` carries flash from `0x4000` up (stock 1.63: 939,744 bytes), in 2+7+7-packed 64-byte packets with a checksum and two terminators. It never carries the 16 KiB boot sector.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: The boot-ROM updater stages the whole image in RAM and checks it before the first erase, so an interrupted or corrupt transfer changes nothing. `[doc]` (code reading)

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: It refuses a version not newer than "140", and halts on one flash part ID.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: An exporter must include everything up to the last non-`0xFF` byte below `0x100000`. Custom code near `0xFE000-0xFFFFF` sits after the blob chain, and stopping at the last blob boots with pointers into erased flash. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: The trap: the OS rewrites the boot sector. On every boot, MainOS checks the magic word at flash `0x3FFE`. If it isn't `0x224B`, MainOS erases the boot sector and rewrites it from a copy embedded in MainOS. A modified OS that alters that check or that copy can destroy the updater on its first boot; after that only an external flash programmer helps. Same pattern as the A4 MK1, so rule A38 applies. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / OS update and recovery (Machinedrum)
facts.text: Recovery otherwise: enter the boot ROM's upgrade mode and send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI (the unit has no USB). Rule A36. `[doc]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: Monomodule runs the Monomachine's own sound engine in an emulated DSP56300 and matches the hardware sample for sample. So the sound engine is DSP56300 code taken from the OS file (OS 1.32B, `Elektron_SFX6-60_OS1.32B.syx`). `[doc]` {monomodule}

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: Board, as Gearmulator models it (joelanders' gearmulator-md-mm, which boots the unmodified MnM OS 1.32B on the same board model as the Machinedrum, `[emu]` {gearmulator-md-mm}): the same ColdFire MCF5206E (modelled at 40 MHz) and two DSP56300-family DSPs; the same address map: flash at `0x10000000` (8 MiB OS images for both machines), main RAM `0x200000-0x2fffff`, each DSP's HI08 host port at `0x500000` / `0x600000`, internal SRAM at `0x1000000`; the SFX-60 MKII keeps user DigiPRO waveforms in a 2 MiB flash window at `0x10200000`.

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: What differs from the MD in that model: the ColdFire services the DSP host port through the hardware receive latch rather than the MD's HREQ-to-IRQ4 wire; the two DSPs are coupled by their own link handshake. These are emulator-level facts. Nothing in our sources has measured a unit's clocks. `[emu]`

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: Custom OS saved-data hazard: em's firmware reclaims song slots for extended data (MnM: slots 13-24; MD: 13-32). Songs left in those slots are corrupted on boot, so back them up first. The same can happen with any mod that changes saved-data layouts (compare section E of AGENT-RULES). `[doc]` {ems-fw}

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: em's firmware carries features from jmamma's MDX (new machines, tunings, LFO shapes, MIDI fixes) with credit. `[doc]` {ems-fw}

facts.section: Machinedrum (SPS-1 UW) and Monomachine (SFX-6/60) / Monomachine (thin)
facts.text: Screen dump (ems-monomachine-firmware 26B09): the request `F0 00 20 3C 03 00 64 F7` returns 16 SysEx chunks of 7-bit-packed data, 64 bytes each once decoded: the native LCD bitmap, 128x64, 1 bit, column-major, bottom to top, MSB first. Whether stock 1.32B answers it is not stated. The firmware is now compressed, so boot is slower. `[doc]` {ems-mnm-changelog}

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
facts.text: CPU: ColdFire MCF54415CMJ250 (chip marking read 2026-09-30): MCF5441x, V4 core with EMAC, 250 MHz, no separate DSP. All audio is ColdFire assembly. It is the same CPU family as Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1, Rytm and A4; the Octatrack is the exception. The MCF54418 reference manual applies. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
facts.text: Audio: 6 tracks, rendered per 32-sample block (0.67 ms) in the audio interrupt. The stock OS already takes about 77 % of each block, even when stopped, because all tracks and effects are computed every block. Peaks reach 99 % with heavy added engines. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
facts.text: EMAC runs with MACSR = `0xa0` (signed fractional), and Unicorn gets it wrong (the same pitfall as Syntakt, Octatrack and DN2). The project ships its own EMAC model. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
facts.text: Container: ELE3, text header plus section table (16-byte aligned), with a trailer of zero padding, 4 zero bytes and an HMAC-SHA256 at a 16-byte-aligned offset. The key is re-derived from the image itself, so checksums and HMAC can be recomputed. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
facts.text: The startup menu lives in flash that OS updates never write. Hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE, "READY TO RECEIVE". It listens to MIDI IN only, never USB.

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
facts.text: Model:Cycles' MIDI IN is a 3.5 mm TRS jack (type A and B both work). A mono TS cable does not work. Use the supplied DIN adapter if your interface has DIN.

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
facts.text: Takes 5-10 minutes; the unit restarts by itself.

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
facts.text: If it stays on "RECEIVING..." a packet was lost: power cycle and send slower (Modded Cycles' flasher pace 1.4 by default, 2.0 when it fails). `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: Free space is scarce. The project's main source of code room is freed sprite masks: Groups of byte-identical `0xFF` bitmap masks are each referenced by one 32-bit constant. Redirecting that constant to a kept copy renders identically and frees the others. 10 groups, 164 freeable masks, 104-1,024 bytes each. Never write into a kept copy. A registry tool tracks which mod owns which mask.

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: Other `0xFF` caves are refused when stock code points into them.

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: Large code is appended to the image and copied to SDRAM at boot by one shared boot hook (Syntakt engines and MACRO at `0x43000000`, Model-TG at `0x46700000`). A new payload joins the chain rather than adding its own hook. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: Settings that must survive a save go into proven-unused bytes of the pattern, project or sound structures (examples: pattern-track byte +512, sound slots 18/27/30/31), declared in a registry so that two mods cannot claim the same bytes. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: Syntakt engines run on a Model:Cycles: Modded Cycles reads them from a Syntakt 1.41/1.42 file at build time and places them as a payload. The Syntakt's CPU #2 and the Cycles' CPU are the same core family. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
facts.text: The same OS can be installed on a Model:Samples; the project marks this route experimental. Returning from the Cycles OS on a Samples needs a MIDI interface. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
facts.text: Every stock voice is rendered every block, playing or not: about 7,600 instructions each, so six idle voices cost ~45,800 per block. Stock audio takes ~77 % of the CPU at rest, measured on a unit with a diagnostic load counter (the same figure as in Modded-Cycles' notes). Skipping silent voices cut 77 % of the voice-loop instructions in the emulator; the unit test is still open. `[hw]` / `[emu]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
facts.text: Ported Syntakt engines cost about the same instructions as stock voices (-7 % to +43 %), yet three or more made the unit slow and glitchy. The likely cause is their much larger memory footprint (cache misses), which the emulator does not time. Another case of rule A34. `[hw]` (symptoms) / `[?]` (cause)

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
facts.text: Units report peaks of 101-108 % of the block budget, with clicks, while the average sits around 73-77 %. Peaks, not averages, decide. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
facts.text: Stock voices start accumulating into ACC0 without clearing it, so they rely on an empty accumulator at entry. Leave ACC0 at 0 (as on the Syntakt). `[emu]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
facts.text: USB multitrack glitches (reported on Reddit after 15-20 minutes): Cause: the OS sends each block to USB right after rendering it, and the 6-channel mod's queue tolerated only 0.2 ms of jitter. With variable engine load (muted tracks, effects off) frames went missing. Fix: send at a fixed time at the start of the next interrupt, align the queue at start-up, and use a 9-slot ring instead of 8. Zero defects in the simulator afterwards. General rule for USB streaming mods: decouple the send time from a variable render time. `[emu]` (cause read in the OS, fix simulated)

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: Thresholds seen on units: the sound crackles when a block nears 100 % of its time; a single block at 91 % did *not* crackle; the UI was still fluid at ~86 % sustained load and slows above that. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: Mistake 1: reacting to one heavy block. Peaks are isolated: a step where several tracks start (the sequencer takes up to ~7 % of a block), or caches the UI flushed between blocks (+4.6 points). By the time the governor sees such a block, it is already over; cutting a voice can't rescue it and is audible. The fix reacts only to a peak that lasts two blocks, or to sustained load. On a unit: "works well", 6 tracks with effects at 89 % peak / 78 % average, no crackle. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: Mistake 2: an integer moving average that never moves. `slow += (load - slow) >> 8` with load and average in whole percent rounds every step to 0, or to -1 below the average. The "sustained load" rule therefore never fired on a unit. The emulator test hid it because it pre-set the average. Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units (e.g. load << 8), and test them from a cold start. `[emu]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: Mistake 3: stealing the quietest voice before the mixer. That ignores track volume, sends and mute, so a naturally quiet but loud-mixed track (hi-hat, a long tail) always went first, and a muted but still computed track was never preferred. Pick by audibility after the mixer, and prefer muted tracks. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: EMAC wrappers are not free: wrapping the reverb kernels in helpers that saved ACC3 and MACSR around every product cost +20-48 % instructions. Save the EMAC state once per block. `[emu]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
facts.text: Finding the worst block on the unit (note 217, results pending): Seven markers in the audio interrupt read the DMA timer (`0xFC07000C`), and the stages of the worst block are kept for display. One block is 90,112 timer ticks. The same method as digihealth (Digitakt mk1) and dnfw's loadmap (DN2): measure before optimising. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: CC lookup (Model:Cycles): the CC-to-descriptor table is built at `0x4005a8ce`; CC 16-23 are looked up only in the row of the track's machine, so a shared descriptor on CC 20-23 is never reached, while CC 75-78 reach shared descriptors on all six tracks (`[emu]`, interpreter). CC values are not scaled: the handler `0x4000b568` writes value x 256 and the setter `0x4000b274` clamps to the descriptor's range. Edits send their CC through `0x4000b942`, which reads the stock table at `0x4010dce0`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Stock MIDI map (Model:Cycles): CCs that reach a track descriptor: 3, 7, 10, 12-19, 65-67, 70, 80, 93 (Solo, by code reading), 102-110; on the FX channel 3, 14, 15, 85-88, 102-110. Stock NRPNs: 1:26-1:30, 1:32-1:39, 3:0, 1:100-1:103. Free next to 74/71: CC 72, 73, 75-79. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Model:Samples knob CCs from its descriptor table at `0x40109048`: Pitch 16, Loop 17, Flip 18, Start 19, Length 20, Cutoff 74, Reso 71, Decay 80. `[doc]` (code reading, not run)

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: No CC goes out for a knob until TRACK SETUP MOUT is on for that track (with ENCS at I+E); stock behaviour, not a bug. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Voice internals (Model:Cycles): amp envelope `0x400a9252`, decay table `0x4011d84c` (DECAY 127 is about 15 s to -60 dB); the VCA `0x400a9430` clears the level in a trig's block, which clicks on a retrig; PUNCH `0x400a967a` (with PUNCH off a TONE track's output is x1/8); the voice loop `0x400a7d4a` keeps trig and release flags for one block only, runs the EMAC with MACSR `0xa0` and leaves acc0 uncleared; per-track velocity gain at `0x40fe4c90 + 2*track`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Cost per 32-frame block in Unicorn (instructions, not cycles): TONE 5,291, PERC 6,079, METAL 6,431, KICK 7,429, SNARE 7,158, CHORD 8,300; model27's SOLID (an eight-mode struck-body machine on the EMAC) 3,588 for one ringing voice, 51,589 for six tracks of sustained noise. `[emu]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: On a unit (2026-11-11): SOLID with every other model27 card ran on a Model:Cycles; six SOLID tracks, each with a Track FX, and POTS on the delay send averaged about 60 % CPU with peaks up to 75 %. Track FX answered CC 75/76 and NRPN 1:22/1:23. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)
facts.text: Where SOLID sits: at `0x43000000` when it is the only added machine (13,216 bytes of code, 2,832 of variables), or as machine 7 at `0x43009680` beside SAMPLE; this is the same SDRAM payload area the Syntakt engines and MACRO use ([RAM-TENANCY.md](../RAM-TENANCY.md)). It takes 80 bytes of the shared freed mask at `0x4016cae8`, now 1,016 of 1,024 bytes used. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / The +Drive sample store (model27's sample uploader, OS 1.13)
facts.text: A sample in use is locked. Once a track uses a sample, the Model:Cycles refuses to delete it; a restart unlocks it only if no track uses it anymore (tried on a Model:Cycles with one SAMPLE track, 2026-11-10). An uploader should delete what it can and name the locked files rather than stop. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / The +Drive sample store (model27's sample uploader, OS 1.13)
facts.text: Uploads become 48 kHz mono samples; Chromium decodes neither AIFF nor 64-bit float WAV, so model27's page converts those itself before handing them on. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Pads and TRIG keys: the pads play and end notes through `0x4001d05e(view, track, note, velocity, speed)` and `0x4001d0fc(view, track, note)`, called only by the pads' handler `0x4001d180`; the TRIG keys in keyboard mode use `0x40019e7a` (on) and `0x40019c84` (off). Each of the note-on routines begins with `lea -16(sp),sp ; moveq #5,dN`, a clean 6-byte hook site. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Note ranks: the audio side's event loop keeps, per track, the rank and note that hold it (`0x40fe4c9c + 4t`, `0x40fe4cb4 + 4t`); sequencer notes are rank 1, notes played live rank 2, a note of lower rank is dropped, and a note-off frees the track only with the same rank and note. That is why a held pad or TRIG key pauses the track's own trigs on every stock machine. `[doc]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Preset preview: the PRESET browser's cursor preview `0x400a63ac` reads the entry as a preset (`jsr 0x400a3052` at `0x400a6426`) into one of two 100-byte buffers and marks it (`*0x40fb5a04`); a live note on the active track carries the mark and the audio side copies its 66 parameter bytes into `0x800015ae + 66t`. A sample file fails the preset reader's size check (48-160 bytes). model27's SAMPLE 0.16 hooks `0x400a6426` to preview +Drive samples; flashed and checked on a Model:Cycles 2026-11-12. `[hw]`

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: Knob writes and preview notes: the parameter write `0x40059534(value, track, k)` writes straight into the voice's targets `0x800015ae + 66t + 2k`, so a turned knob reaches a note that already plays. A preview note, though, takes its 66 bytes from the OS's own preview buffer (`0x40058a0a`), into which the OS copies the browser's sound (two buffers take turns), so the next preview note plays the knobs as they were when the cursor arrived (I88). model27's SAMPLE 0.17 writes the track's sound (k 0..32, except the key, k 25..27) into that buffer on each tick; flashed on a Model:Cycles 2026-11-13, knob changes are heard on the next preview note. `[doc]` (read in OS 1.13) / `[hw]` {model27-sample017}

facts.section: Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
facts.text: The OS sine `0x8000eee4` (257 Q31 samples in SRAM, copied from the image at boot) is the default wave of every voice operator: the voice reset `0x400a7ab8` (at boot and at each machine change) points all four operators' wave pointers (voice + 168 + 120j) at it. Only KICK (`0x8000eae0` on one operator), METAL (`0x8000f2e8` on two), PERC (`0x4012024c`, in DDR, on one) and CHORD (its own frames) set other waves; SNARE and TONE play only the sine. The waves `0x8000eae0`, the sine and `0x8000f2e8` sit back to back, 1,028 bytes each, after CHORD's last SRAM frame. A mod that rewrites the sine changes every machine. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: CPU: ColdFire MCF5445x (board photos read MCF54454VR266 or MCF5445AVR266), 32-bit big-endian. The firmware stores 264 MHz; internal bus 132 MHz (UARTs, PIT, DSPI), FlexBus 66 MHz, 24 MHz crystal. 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000`; NOR flash on CS0, 8 MB decode. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: Audio DSP: Freescale Symphony DSP56721, two DSP5636x cores in one chip, 200 MHz each, with no external memory. Each core has its own P memory. A 64 K-word shared window at `$030000` is reachable by both cores; P, X and Y alias there. Tracks 1-4 run on core 1 and tracks 5-8 on core 0 ("inverted from old assumptions"). Each track's FX1 and FX2 run on its own core. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: Storage: CompactFlash (FAT16/32) through an ATA stack (PIO task-file registers at `0x90000000`).

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Silicon
facts.text: The kernel is a proprietary preemptive microkernel (banner "ElektronOctatrack DPS-1"), not FreeRTOS.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: 4,532 cycles per sample per core at 44.1 kHz (199.9 MHz measured). The older 4,160 / 183 MHz is retracted.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: About 3,120 cycles/sample are usable for DSP work; stock takes ~1,410.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Planning number: ~500 cycles on top of the current reverb with 4 FX1 FILTERs, ~900 with 2. One FX1 FILTER costs 192 cycles/sample. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Stock FX2 costs per sample (one MKII, 1.40C), dearest first: DJ EQ ~340, LO-FI ~310, SPRING ~300, CHORUS ~295, FILTER ~285, DARK ~255, PLATE ~250, PHASER ~240, EQUALIZER ~190, FLANGER ~145, COMB ~125, COMPRESSOR ~100, SPATIALIZER ~80, DELAY ~0. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: Words are not cycles: `move x0,a` 2 cycles, a one-word displaced `move x:(r7+$15),a` ~4, a two-word displaced ~6. Static word counts are a floor; only a burn sweep measures the ceiling. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: ColdFire access costs (one unit, 132 MHz, inside the frame interrupt, stock cache settings): register/SRAM/cache hit ~2.9 ns, uncached SDRAM store 36 ns, load 69 ns, cache miss ~80 ns, `cpushl` 46-80 ns. SRAM is 12-28x cheaper than SDRAM, and caching a transmit buffer does not help. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Cycle budget (measured with a burn probe on units)
facts.text: USB costs: one recording buffer is about 6 points of the ColdFire's frame share, USB streaming about 12. Six buffers plus streaming drop frames. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
facts.text: Every track runs `FX1 -> FX2 -> gain`. FX1 has 3,072 words of Y, FX2 16,384, which is why reverbs and delay are FX2-only.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / FX slots
facts.text: Both menus share one DSP dispatch table indexed by the raw id. A module on a stock effect's id replaces that effect in both slots, and removing an effect from a menu frees no space. The reclaimable pool is FX1's ten effects, 3,384 words. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Elektron ships the same OS as `.bin` and `.syx` (the MKI and MKII files are byte-identical for 1.40C). `.bin` = ELUP header + seed + XOR-feedback-obfuscated `[len] + ELEK(aPLib(MAIN OS))` + checksum. `.syx` = SysEx-packed ELEK container. The MAIN OS is 1,112,560 B. No cryptographic signature in any layer. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Validation on update returns: -1 IO, -2 not a valid OS, -3 length (more than 1 MB + 12 B), -4 checksum, -5 MK1 not allowed (version code below "0156"), -6 cannot downgrade (below "0178"). octabam images keep code 0178. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: The card path: OS UPGRADE lists `/*.BIN` on the CF, validates, programs NOR from `0x4000` and verifies it word by word. Stock then shows "PLEASE REBOOT!" and never resets the unit itself.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Recovery: hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE (not TRIG 4 as on the small boxes), send the stock `.syx` over DIN MIDI. `TRIG 2` (EMPTY RESET) clears battery-backed RAM and settings, not the card. Pace about 7,460 messages at DIN rate. Filter MIDI clock on that port and merge nothing else into it: a MIDI-hub preset caused a CHECKSUM ERROR. If the unit loses sync, send again slower (60-300 ms between messages). The unit may update its bootstrap after the flash. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: How stock writes NOR (1.40C, Modwerk's reading, `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-traps}): OS UPGRADE reads the whole card file into RAM, then erases and programs NOR from there (sector erase `0x40020628`, 256-byte page program `0x400206f4`, the 37 sector starts listed at `0x400a95c0`). The layout is 8 KB boot sectors from `0x4000`, then 64 KB sectors up to `0x1f0000`. Both routines poll the chip themselves and mask interrupts only around the command bytes, so a mod can call them from a task without breaking the frame interrupt. The bootloader below `0x4000` is never written. It depacks NOR from `0x4012` without checking anything, so an image that doesn't boot is recoverable over DIN MIDI only. The startup menu's MIDI UPGRADE checks the received file, not NOR. `[hw]` (testers' units)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: Don't verify a running image against its own RAM: once running, stock rewrites bytes inside its bootloader copy (`0x400e201e-0x400e2108`) and reuses the RAM after the image. Compare against digests taken before stock started. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / OS format, update and recovery
facts.text: After flashing a build that changes an effect's parameter layout, old projects need their stored values stamped. A select value outside its count stalls the sequencer on first play. `[hw]` ([I28](../INCIDENTS.md#i28-a-select-value-outside-its-count-stalled-the-sequencer))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: The free ROM is small: zero runs in `0x400c0000-0x400d8000` total ~8.4 KB, shared by every mod. The zero region above `0x400d8000` is the PROJECT subsystem's RAM. A menu table placed in a 15 KB zero run at `0x401087e4` crashed a unit. ([I48](../INCIDENTS.md#i48-a-menu-table-in-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit)) Larger code goes to a loader-copied area: octabam's loader is a stub at `0x4010fdf0`, right after the OS image, reached from the boot site. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: DSP code that does not fit a core's P memory (ends `P:0x1fff`) runs from the shared window `P:0x30000-0x3ffff`. This was proven on a unit (PEXT probe, 2026-10-25). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Memory and code placement
facts.text: DSP scratch: r7 scratch `$00-$83` is the per-instance block, and `$84+` hangs the unit. Stock effects scratch `X:0x20-0xff`, and the hardware dispatcher passes the audio block at X:0. `[hw]` ([I29](../INCIDENTS.md#i29-dsp-scratch-at-84-and-up-hung-the-unit))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: `dsp_asm` silently mis-encodes: `tfr a,b` as `rnd b`, and any `mpy` operand order it does not know as `mpysu`. `lua (rN+d),rM` takes d in -64..63 and silently wraps larger values. Labels resolve by prefix, so a new label may not have an existing label as its prefix.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: DSP56300 semantics: A logical op on an accumulator leaves the extension byte stale, so the next store saturates to full scale. `move a,b` limits; `tfr a,b` moves all 56 bits. A Tcc pair sharing one compare breaks with any arithmetic in between. `asr #n,a,a` shifts into a0, and Z is set only when all 56 bits are zero. Reading a0 exposes the fractional left shift that a1 hides.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: No `rep` in an effect's init or proc (it cannot be interrupted, and the host-command handlers need to run). No dense X work in a DMA's 8K block.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: Instruction-form rule, as on the SHARC: a DSP form ships only if a stock payload runs it or a hardware probe approved it.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: Stock Unicorn halves every ColdFire fractional-mode multiply and adds where `msac` subtracts (the firmware runs EMAC with MACSR = 0x20), and its MAC-with-load decode has three defects. MACSR S/U is bit 6, and in fractional mode it selects 16-bit rounding. These are the same EMAC pitfalls as on the Syntakt and DN2 (rule G-series, `common/toolchain-and-emulators.md`). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / DSP56300 assembler and emulator traps (from octabam's trap register; each cost real work)
facts.text: The emulator (`ot_emu`) charges one step per instruction, with no cache or memory timing. A change can be cycle-identical in the port and several percent worse on the unit.

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: No EP0 reply or OUT data stage may be a whole multiple of 64 bytes. A reply of 64/128/192/256 bytes left a stale zero-length packet, and the next request returned 0 bytes (once, the unit froze). Stock leaves zero-length termination on in the EP0 OUT queue head, so a 128- or 192-byte OUT stage never completed. Send one byte less, or clear ZLT when priming. `[hw]` Rule A39. ([I5](../INCIDENTS.md#i5-ep0-data-stages-of-a-multiple-of-64-bytes-stall-or-freeze-stock-usb-driver))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: About one EP0 OUT stage in 50-100 goes unanswered on a MKII: completed inside the ISR after stock's poll, or stopped part-way. Modwerk runs a 60 Hz tick that finishes a completed stage, or stalls EP0 after 0.5 s so the host resubmits. `[hw]` ([I6](../INCIDENTS.md#i6-about-one-ep0-out-stage-in-50-100-goes-unanswered))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: DMA reads RAM, not the copyback cache. A value the CPU stores rarely stayed stale for minutes in USB replies, while values stored every frame looked live. Copy a reply through the uncached alias and send it from there. `[hw]` (Same idea as A28 on the SHARC.) ([I35](../INCIDENTS.md#i35-usb-replies-stayed-stale-for-minutes))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: A soft reset leaves the USB controller and PHY as they were: one RAM boot in about six came back with no USB until a power cycle. Stop the controller (USBCMD.RS = 0) and wait ~50 ms before resetting; that gave 20 of 20 good boots. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I7](../INCIDENTS.md#i7-a-soft-reset-leaves-the-usb-controller-running))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / USB device side (both octabam and Modwerk, measured on units)
facts.text: Never post key events into stock's queues directly (two crashes minutes later). Feed the panel parser its own bytes instead. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-traps} ([I30](../INCIDENTS.md#i30-key-events-posted-into-stocks-queues-crashed-the-unit-minutes-later))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: The Modwerk base with nothing installed shows ~42-47 % CPU. That is mostly stock's own tasks; there is no clean stock baseline yet. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: An FM synth module costs ~8 points just by being installed, plus ~5 while a track plays it. Small effects cost 0.5 points or less on the ColdFire, but their DSP cost lands on their core (BBD on T6: core T5-8 went from ~44 % to 54 %). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Uncached module code is expensive: Analog BD on one track cost ~20 points. 93 % of each call was a write lease whose owner check read the module header through the uncached alias (~0.6 µs a read). With one lease per frame it dropped to ~10 points. Lesson: take locks only where a call writes, at most once a frame, and keep uncached reads out of hot paths. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: UI-task edits can cost milliseconds: a 64-step MIDI rewrite took 3.9 ms per knob turn, mostly stock's lock-index rebuild. Updating only the own track's bits brought it to 0.5 ms. Audio frames stayed ~406-417 µs apart throughout, because it all ran on the UI task. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: The DSP peak meter shows the busiest single frame of a 1,024-frame window. A self-test or sync leaves it at ~99.7 % while the mean is flat and the audio fine. Judge overload by the longest frame of a real load, not the peak. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Frame budget from the field (Modwerk beta, 2026-11-08): audio frames are 363 µs apart (16 samples), and the DSPs starve once a gap passes about 515 µs. A unit left stopped and connected for about 23 hours with 6 modules showed 42 % CPU and a longest gap of 423 µs, with no freeze. `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Settled: the silence after USB DISK MODE was Modwerk's, not stock's (finding 72, 2026-11-10): stock pauses the DSP while USB DISK MODE is open; Modwerk's base took that pause for a stalled DSP, and its recovery kept the audio stopped until a power cycle. Fixed in the base; on the owner's MKII (1.40C) PROJ > USB DISK MODE, about 10 s, NO, PLAY now plays. Not tested: the walk on a flashed base, a file copy in that mode, an OS upgrade from the card. A mod that watches for DSP stalls must tell stock's own pauses from a stall (rule C12: it was never reproduced on a stock unit). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / ColdFire load (Modwerk's meter on a MKII, Oct 2026)
facts.text: Field stalls with modules (Modwerk beta, 8-10 Nov): stalls still come within about a minute of installs or restores, before any module code is placed (finding 71), and on a heavy self-test Part (FILTER and DELAY on every track plus FLANGER and PHASER) 1 run in 21 stalled on the live base, 0 in 5 on the lighter Part; only a power cycle recovered. The base's longest fully masked span measured about 14 µs, far under the roughly 200 µs that stops core 0, so masked ColdFire code is unlikely but not ruled out for the stall itself. One field crash record: vector 3 inside a module's ColdFire code. A unit with 6 modules stayed up 70 hours (longest frame gap 424 µs). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-beta-1110} {modwerk-ot-unit-1110}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: An effect's `init` must preserve r1: the FX1 dispatcher keeps the effect id there and calls `proc` through it. An init that moved r1 jumped to the reset vector and killed the core at project load. octabam's build refuses an init that writes r1/n1/m1. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A persistent slot that `init` does not clear holds the previous effect's leftovers. The emulator boots with zeroed RAM and cannot show it. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Resident window code must sit in `0x33da3..0x37eff`: payload B's boot loop clears `Y:0x37f00..0x3ffff`, and DARK REV writes up to `0x33da2`. `[emu]` (both cores faulted at boot in the port)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A DSP frame counter past `$7fffff` saturates in `move a,nN`, which stopped a frame engine after 50.7 minutes. Mask counters to 23 bits. `[hw]` ([I32](../INCIDENTS.md#i32-a-dsp-frame-counter-saturated-after-507-minutes))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Core 1's load-meter counter is at `X:$2840` on Modwerk USB bases; module state there gave a jittery pitch. `[hw]` ([I33](../INCIDENTS.md#i33-module-state-on-a-load-meter-counter-gave-a-jittery-pitch))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: Cold starts: an early-startup change passed emulator boots and quick power cycles but stalled at the logo after several minutes powered off. Keeping the activation helper resident in the OS image fixed it; the mechanism is unknown. Qualify startup changes after a long power-off (rule A40). `[hw]` ([I34](../INCIDENTS.md#i34-a-startup-change-stalled-at-the-logo-after-a-long-power-off))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / More DSP and boot traps (measured on units)
facts.text: A write-watch on cached addresses is blind to a clear through the uncached alias. A "free 8.8 MB" region turned out to be the stock delay rings. Before trusting a null result, ask what the instrument cannot see (rule A31). `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: A core's crash threshold, found on hardware in KYOTI's own cost model: stock's heaviest effects plus the sidechain compressor model at ~3,516 cycles per sample. The core crashed somewhere between ~3,760 and ~3,830. With DJ EQ in both slots on T5-T8, one extra REPITCH voice (~240) was clean; adding a second (RPS9 ~77 or RPSP ~240) crashed. KYOTI's bar: a feature must not break any configuration that is clean on stock. So beside stock's heaviest effects a core has room for about one heavy voice. Note that these "modelled cycles" are KYOTI's estimate, not octabam's measured 4,532 cycles per sample. Compare figures only within one model. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: The DSP shared window in work RAM is volatile: at boot, `0x401086f4` is copied to `0x80000000` (`0x3e88` bytes) and the rest is zero-filled up to `0x80004000`. Nothing of yours survives there across a boot. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: One image for MKI and MKII: the OS probes `0x46c8d18c` and shows 15 (MKI) or 16 (MKII) PERSONALIZE items. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / From KYOTI (Zac-Kyoti/octatrack-kyoti-fw, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: KYOTI keeps a merged, confidence-tagged 1.40C address map (`reference/kb/memory-map.md`) that cross-references octabam. It is a good second reading. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: When the emulator cannot run the code you need to see (here, the EMAC-heavy frame builder), log from the unit itself. OctaMax added two detours that call the firmware's own file primitives (open `0x40016864`, write `0x400166b8`, close `0x4001677c`, sprintf `0x40013a08`) and write `/HOTDBG.TXT` to the CF card. Pull the card and read it. It works on hardware, and it showed that values seeded in the emulator had been guessed wrong (a voice type byte of 1, not 4). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: The DSP never plays on its own: every frame the ColdFire builds a per-voice packet in shared RAM (double buffer at `0x80000000`, selector `0x800000e0`) and pokes the DSP. A voice that stops being fed goes silent without any "stop". `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: Recorder buffers live in a paged RAM pool (base `0x40a955e0`, ~89 MB) that survives a project change; the voices are torn down and rebuilt by the load. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: Restoring state every frame is safe only for CPU-side bookkeeping. Overwriting data the DSP reads corrupted the audio. `[hw]` ([I31](../INCIDENTS.md#i31-restoring-dsp-read-state-every-frame-corrupted-the-audio))

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Debugging on the unit by writing a log to the CF card (OctaMax, MKII, OS 1.40C)
facts.text: An Octatrack emulator built on QEMU (ColdFire MCF54455) plus dsp56300, octemu by markandrus, targets firmware development including USB MIDI and audio; PassOS uses its 20-channel USB audio work. `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: The parameter-page descriptor table is live data, zeros included. It is 31 entries of `0x192` bytes at `0x400d2e52-0x400d5f00`, and a zero entry means "the default". Never place code or data there unless the entry is proven unreachable. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: The canary test (from octalab) before anything ships in a new region: 1. Fill the range with a pattern, or a 32-bit counter so that partial overwrites show. 2. Use the unit for a full session: load, record, change patterns, save, power-cycle, load again. 3. Read the range back and compare. octamax lost tables to a heap tail and probe counters to a region restored on every load. See rule A43. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: Scratch RAM `0x80006a40+` is not safe under live audio: a magic word at `0x80006a60` was overwritten by the next key press on a real MKI while recording; the emulator, which runs no DSP/audio path, kept it forever. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Where code and data may go: KYOTI's cave ledger (OS 1.40C, `reference/kb/caves.md`)
facts.text: Past the image's ceiling, two routes: append a runtime after the OS image (octabam's loader stub; proven on an MKI); put a position-independent payload with a relocation table on the CF card and load it at run time. octemu does this for USB audio (four UAC2 descriptors, iso servicing and a 36 KB ring against ~408 B of slack). `[doc]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: AMP envelope: the DSP's AMP envelope restarts from zero at every trig START, so with any ATK above 0 a sound that plays across trigs drops out and fades back in, a click on every note. A ColdFire machine holds the DSP at ATK 0 / HOLD INF / REL INF and shapes AMP itself, as SYNTH MACHINE does. Measured laws (Tim Hastie): ATK is a linear ramp of 3.85 ms x 2^(ATK/8.53), at least 16 frames; REL is exponential with tau 0.295 ms x 2^(REL/8.53). `[hw]` {octabam-wavecf} (I58)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Crossfader: stock maps the crossfader through one table of 128 Q15 values at `0x400bcd90`; the panel handler `0x40061e40` and the MIDI CC 48 handler `0x400626ba` rebuild the per-track weights at `0x80003c60` from it. Replacing the table changes scene locks, XVOL and the morph alike; MIDI SCENES mixes linearly on its own. `[hw]` {octabam-xfcurve}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Demand loading: the loader copies a whole effect block (MODULATION, 1,561 words, an estimated ~31k of the 72,512 cycles in a frame) inside one DSP frame hook; the DSP-busy meter reads 99.7 % in that window `[hw]`. The frame interrupt has two waits with no time limit (the loader's wait before each host word, and stock's spin at `0x4000ab26` until the DSP takes the frame's `0x8c` host command); if the DSP stops taking host words, the ColdFire can spin forever `[?]` {octabam-dl} (I57, H22).

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: CF write throughput (STEM REC, MKII): write time per KB grows with the number of files written at once: 54-92 us/KB for one file, 423 us/KB for eleven (212 after writing whole 32 KB clusters only). Samples streamed by Static machines from the same card slow writes further (252 -> 387 us/KB for ten files); eleven 24-bit files need 2.9 MB/s. `[hw]` {octabam-stemrec}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Test host: octabam's hardware tools run on Linux and on WSL2 with usbipd; MIDI, transport and the load meter work there, but USB-audio capture over usbip delivered only about a quarter of the frames. `[hw]` {octabam-hwtest}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Key bus (Modwerk): the key bus moved from Y `$800-$9FF` to Y `$7E00-$7FFF` on each core, the tail of the first internal FX2 slot, which frees Y `$7F0-$9FF` for a DSP machine's voice. An FX2 effect that fills the whole 16,384-word buffer is then refused on T1/T5; Mini Verb, E-Verb (15,870 words) and BBD still fit. A keyed duck lands within one 5 ms window of the kick, on the same core and across cores; in the DSP simulator the cross-core key arrives exactly two blocks late. Four RINGMOD SC plus four BBD while playing: CPU 85.1 %, core peaks 66/74.5 %. `[hw]` (MKI 2026-10-30, MKII 2026-11-10), memory survey `[emu]` {modwerk-ot-keybus}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Module cost (Modwerk survey): module DSP code runs at 1.4-1.7 cycles per instruction against about 1 for stock, and installed but unused modules add frame-interrupt time (23.3 % -> 28.2 % stopped with 26 installed). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-options}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Internal SRAM has no free holes: `0x80000000-0x80008000` is the program's `.data`/`.bss`, filled at boot from the image tail; `0x80006964-0x80007574` is the work buffer of the stock audio-analysis task, which writes up to 768 words from `0x80006974`. This explains the KYOTI scratch-word loss at `0x80006a60`. OCTAMAX keeps patch state in DDR at `0x40af0000-0x40af0600`, inside a reserve stock never references, cleared by its boot stub. `[hw]` {octamax-notes} (I59; boot-fill extent disputed, CONFLICTS O23)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Sequencer state: current bank/pattern at `0x800065bd/be`, the cued pair at `0x800065bf/c0` ("nothing cued" when both pairs are equal); cueing the playing pattern cancels in stock, and a switch to the same pattern is a restart with no Part reload. Active bank `0x80000002`, active Part `0x80000003` (disputed, O23); whole-Part apply `0x40009094`. `[hw]` {octamax-notes}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Step timing (KYOTI): the sequencer schedules each step one step ahead, so a Part change sent to the engine in the landing tick sounds a step early; a per-track apply must wait one of the track's steps `[hw]`. The whole-Part apply posts a kernel message and belongs on the UI task; a storage job's done-callback runs on the UI task, which ticks at 1/60 s `[emu]`. Copies with interrupts masked click (I60). {kyoti-reload}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam and octamax findings (2026-11-10)
facts.text: Sample pool: paged in 6 KB pages (MEMORY shows 85.5 MB); KYOTI V1.7 takes 11 pages on DRAM units, octabam reserves 10 MiB when any module runs from DRAM, 18 MiB with STEM REC. `[doc]` {kyoti-build}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Audio-interrupt budget (CX OSC on a MKII): with nothing playing the ColdFire idles at 44.7 % with a mean audio interrupt of 125 us (max 212 us); four CX OSC tracks: 21.8 % idle, 272 us; six: about 12 %, 309 us mean but a 376 us maximum past the 363 us frame; seven: 0 % idle and MAIN clipped. The module now refuses a seventh instance. `[hw]` {octabam-cxosc}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Stock icon blit (`0x400128a8`, a 13-row column word with mask `0xfff80000`): bit 31 is the bottom row and bit 19 the top, so a left shift moves the picture down. Five flashes went into one pixel before this was written down. `[hw]` {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: FLEX slices (DRUMMER, OS 1.40C): in slice mode the voice start `0x4000f450(track, slot, flags)` plays slice `min(STRT >> 1, count - 1)`; the slice table is 64 entries of 12 bytes from +312 of the FLEX slot record `0x100b14f0 + 0x448*slot` (octabam's own STORAGE note said 20 bytes; the code multiplies by 12). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Adding and moving trigs: the sequencer builds each step about 912 samples after the step counter changes, one step ahead; a detour right after the builder (`0x400a2d82`) can add a trig on an empty step or rewrite its micro-timing (one unit is 1/24 of a step). Locks staged for an added trig are ignored, and its lock block holds zeros at boot unless the mod fills it (all 32 lane values of the track went to 0 until DRUMMER wrote `0xff` there). `[emu]` {octabam-drummer} DRUMMER ran on the author's MKII from these sites; two bugs found after the first unit test are I72. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / octabam findings (2026-11-11)
facts.text: Scene locks sit at Part `+0x662 + (scene*8 + track)*32`, one byte per parameter, `0xff` for none. Retrig time RTIM is exponential: half a step at 79, doubling every 12. `[emu]` {octabam-drummer}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Boot keys (OS 1.40C): FUNC held from power-on opens Elektron's startup menu; PROJ held at power-on is ignored by the bootloader and the unit starts normally. Modwerk therefore moved its "skip modules" gesture from FUNC to PROJ on the MKII (the MKI keeps FUNC). `[hw]` {modwerk-ot-base}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Scene keys take the encoders: pressing a scene key writes stock's scene-lock knob handler `0x40053498` into every encoder slot of the table at `0x46c7dede + 20*enc` (writer `0x40031406`, dispatch `0x40031944`), so a page editor's hook sees no turn while a scene is held. `[emu]`, seen by a user {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Stock calls clobber scratch registers: the CC sender `0x4009eec8` saves only d2-d7/a2-a5; any `jsr` into stock can change d0, d1, a0 and a1. `[emu]`, seen by a user {octabam-traps}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Render after stock's trig work: in SYNTIZ, a render in the same frame after stock's trig handling cost up to 2.25x a first render (33.6 % vs 14.9 % of a frame); stock's own work reached 84 % of a frame at pattern transitions. Modwerk refuses a RAM boot or trial while the sequencer plays. `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: An installed module that never plays can cost margin: on an MKII, FM Synth 0.1.2 installed beside SYNTIZ gave light crackle and one sample track less of headroom; removing it cured both (one A/B, cause unknown). `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Removing a module in use left the loader stuck in recovery until a power cycle (I75, rule A54); a base update over USB once reported Done and did not stick (I76). `[hw]` {modwerk-syntiz}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: USB base: Modwerk's Octatrack base is open to everyone since 2026-11-11; the first install still goes through the CF card, a module set holds at most 20 modules, and USB Audio is off (USB MIDI only) unless the set has the USB Audio module. `[doc]` {modwerk-ot-base}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Analog BD 0.1.7 (909 model): tables and voices in DSP X `$2841-$3200`, next to the core-1 load counter at X:`$2840`; glue plus engines take 1,003 P words per core. On an MKII a voice on T5 (core 2) was refused even alone with every core-2 effect slot off, and the DSP `meter` command did not answer on that base. `[hw]` {modwerk-analogbd}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: A recorder started on the first PLAY after power-on (MIDI mode, T1 idle), probably from a quantized REC start left staged at `0x800018be`/`0x800018de` (QREC branch of REC_POST `0x40005178`); a double STOP before PLAY avoided it (I78). `[hw]`, cause `[?]` {octabam-freeloop}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: The stock DELAY's coefficient table `0x400d1ce0-0x400d2cdf` is not free space: its upper half is zero in the stock OS and looks unused, but DELAY reads it. Code that card builds placed there dulled DELAY repeats; Modwerk's checks now refuse any package or base site that writes into it. `[doc]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: CPU-rendered machines need a budget like DSP effects: on the owner's MKII, three FM Synth tracks beside a busy eight-track pattern froze the unit (I79). Modwerk's base now prices machines (first estimates: 45 % of the CPU for added machines, 12 % for one that names no price), refuses a pick over the limit (CPU FULL) and drops a voice instead of freezing. Seen on development builds; the release base was not run on a unit. `[hw]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: Modwerk dropped its card firmware builder (2026-11-12): Octatrack modules now reach a unit only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (`MODWERK0.SET`) on the CF card. `[doc]` {modwerk-1112}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Modwerk and octabam findings (2026-11-12)
facts.text: FREE LOOP and RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT can share the UI tick: both detour the UI task's 1/60 s tick `0x40056c28` (the toast countdown's read), which made them a listed conflict. octabam's HOOKS now chains the site (FREE LOOP first, then RELOAD_FROM_PROJECT); the chain passed four cases under Unicorn, not flashed yet. `[emu]` {octabam-hooks}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Frame grid: the DSP raises the frame interrupt once a frame (362.8 µs) and the ColdFire answers with the next frame; the handler's entry is `0x4000aad0`. At START and at a program change one frame interrupt runs 475-585 µs on every image measured, so the next one enters late. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Late-entry window: measured on an MKII, an entry 128-149 µs late is followed by one back-to-back frame interrupt and the unit runs on; 155-223 µs late, one frame is skipped and it runs on; the two stalls logged entered 149 and 155 µs late, after which the DSP took no more frames (sequencer held at step 1, panel and USB alive, power cycle needed). A USB audio capture adds 25-30 µs to the START frame. octabam's FRAME GUARD waits out entries 110-190 µs late until 190 µs; the DSP-side mechanism is inferred (I82, rule A56). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Open: on a test image with 60 µs added to every frame interrupt and a 20-channel capture (the frame interrupt at 91 % of the ColdFire), 7 of 16 STARTs froze the whole unit 8.2 s later, at the pattern's wrap; not seen on shipping images. `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / Frame-interrupt timing and MIDI scenes (octabam, 2026-11-13)
facts.text: Scene lock view (stock): the audio pages draw scene locks from a view byte `0x460d1694` (1 scene A, 2 scene B), set only by the hold-and-turn paths and the scene press handlers `0x40054c80` (A) and `0x40054c5c` (B), which return at once in MIDI mode; the MIDI key's handler (`0x40055548`-`0x40055676`, tail `jmp 0x4007e998` at `0x40055670`) does not set it. So a scene held while switching from the MIDI to the audio tracks shows no locks on stock; octabam's MIDI SCENES hooks the tail to fix that. `[emu]` {octabam-msc}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Audio codec: the converter on one MKII board was read as a Cirrus Logic CS42432 (marking read off the board). `[hw]` (one unit)

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Stock does not set up the codec over SPI; its only SPI traffic is the real-time clock (stock's code traced, every hardware write logged in octabam's emulator). `[emu]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: The analog outputs stayed silent under an own DSP program that copied every DSP register write stock makes; inputs worked. Bisecting put the switch-on in a ~40 ms slice of stock's start-up where its frame exchange with the DSP begins, and the outputs came alive once the engine used a DMA-driven audio ring restarted by a DMA interrupt, as stock does. `[hw]` What actually un-mutes them is `[?]`: the CHANGELOG names the codec's DAC mute, the log the DMA ring. {aeria-changelog}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: DSP memory per core: a probe on core 0 measured 48K words of private Y and 36K words of private X (core 1 assumed the same). `[hw]`

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Running code from the shared window costs about 2x, and the two cores slow each other there. Moving AERIA's engine into core 0's private P memory cut its worst case from ~700 to ~370 instructions a sample and a sequencer stress test from 89 % to 50 % of core 0. `[hw]` {aeria-changelog}

facts.section: Octatrack (MKI, MKII) - OS 1.40C / AERIA OS findings (own OS on the MKII, 2026-11-09..13)
facts.text: Shared-window memory is not zeroed at a cold boot, unlike in the emulator; core 1 ran a garbage effect from an uninitialised slot table and crashed (I84). Clear any table there before use. `[hw]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Recovery (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`)
facts.text: Mod data written for defaults slows project load and save (Synfact, OS 1.41): a user saw a project load slowly when switched to from another project and save more slowly than usual; a reboot straight into it loaded normally. The export was valid. The ARP mod wrote and sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; leaving default carriers absent cut the emulated serialization from 24.8 M to 4.8 M instructions (81 % fewer). The slowness is a user report; the cost is `[emu]`, the wall-clock gain not yet measured. `[doc]` {synfact-lifecycle} ([I50](../INCIDENTS.md#i50-mod-data-written-for-default-settings-slowed-project-load-and-save))

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
facts.text: Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff}

facts.section: Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)

facts.section: Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
facts.text: Boot unpack limit: the bootstrap loads compressed section 3 at `0x40200000` and unpacks it to `0x40000400`. The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]`
