facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Hardware lesson `[hw]`: SyntHack up to v0.8.0 kept mod code at `0x46000000`. Projects with SP TWINSHOT samples then crashed at boot. Since v0.8.1 the mod code (compressed, appended to section 3 at `0x40348000`) is unpacked into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. ([I20](../INCIDENTS.md#i20-mod-code-at-a-free-address-crashed-projects-with-certain-samples))

facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Conflict to watch `[?]`: SY FM4 (OS 1.40A) copies its code to `0x47000000`, which it describes as "above the BSS end, below the stack, addressed by nothing". That is the region SyntHack found to be overwritten by sample loading on 1.41. Treat any use of RAM above the BSS as unsafe until it is tested with sample-heavy projects.

facts.section: Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
facts.text: Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: CPU #1 load: ~89 % at rest (sequencer stopped), measured on the device with DTIM0 (`0xFC07000C`) at interrupt entry and exit. The UI gets the rest, so a few thousand instructions per block make the UI lag. `[hw]` SY FM4 reports its main-CPU render at 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (stock 85.0k). That is a different span of the same interrupt. `[?]`

facts.section: Syntakt / Audio path
facts.text: Digital filter and amp run on CPU #2; the cutoff is computed on CPU #1. Analog voices and the FX track drive a hardware envelope generator with 20-bit rate codes. Measured curves: the digital biquad f0 = 4.918 Hz x e^(0.0655 x FREQ); the analog filter f = 14.645 Hz x e^(0.0574 x FREQ). Tempo is at `0x402D7010` (BPM x 120). `[hw]` (analog curves measured)

facts.text: Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images.

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: CPU #2 configures its own FPGA: a packed bitstream at `0x40041060` is unpacked to `0x40042000` (54,664 bytes) at init. That is the same size as the Analog Heat +FX FPGA section, so it may be the same part `[?]`. Keep away from it (rule A22).

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB".

facts.section: Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
facts.text: Above the BSS, `0x4404f980-0x48000000` (63.7 MB) is not referenced by any section-7 instruction and is used for SynCrackd's state. Leave the top megabyte for the stack (its depth is not measured). This is CPU #2's RAM, not the main CPU's region that sample loading overwrites (CONFLICTS O2). `[hw]` (alpha, one unit)

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS).

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time.

facts.text: Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: UI internals: parameter descriptors at `0x4022D59C + 52*id`; page objects at `0x41B9F3C8` (44 B, 8 slots); per-parameter `std::function` objects at `0x41B9FA24 + 84*id` (+20 text, +36 icon, +68 style). Page 25 ("OB8") is a free Digitakt leftover. Rewrite a `std::function` only from UI code, never from the audio interrupt.

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Audio mods: Hook the mix function; keep the OS's EMAC `msac` sign convention (the result is -Σ g·x). Do nothing when there is nothing to do. Compute at 24 kHz where the sound allows it. Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. Keep a cost-per-block regression test (count instructions with `UC_HOOK_CODE` after `ctl_flush_tb()`).

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. So mod code is appended to section 3 compressed (SHLZ, at `0x40348000 + offset`). At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. The earlier home above the BSS (`0x46000000`) was overwritten whenever samples loaded (SyntHack issue 4), which settles conflict O2. `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Kit and project storage that round-trips through stock code (SyntHack kitstore/projstore): Kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track blocks go into 6 file bytes that stock's writer zeroes and its reader ignores. 256 bytes go into the project settings block (`+0x227..+0x3FF` is zeroed by the writer and ignored by the reader), behind an `SH` marker. Tests run the real writer and reader with and without the hooks. Zero must mean "default", because stock-saved files load as zero. `[emu]` {synthack-mods}

facts.section: Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
facts.text: Controlling the analog side digitally (SyntHack master-comp): a feed-forward compressor detects on ADC 6/7 (the FX-track bus before its VCAs) and applies gain through those VCAs' control voltages (CV 35/36), once per block (~1.5 kHz). Its UI uses the Digitakt MIDI-track "CC Select" ids 262-268, which the Syntakt never uses. Cost: ~100 instructions per block when off, ~600 when on. Checked on the device (v0.9). `[hw]` {synthack-mods}

facts.text: Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware). facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
facts.text: digikit's run-time limits (its own, not the firmware's): 8 modules, 4 FX slots, 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2) DSP area in 64-byte granules, 64 KiB per module file. The firmware would allow about 900 / 450 KiB. Every limit was filled in the emulator and the next module was refused with a clean error. `[emu]` {digikit-f57}

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Call: `CALL (linked, delayed)` (Type 25a). Prologue `I7 = MODIFY(I7, -N)`, saves to `DM(I6 - n)`. Return `I12 = DM(I6, M7); JUMP (M14, I12) (DB)` with `RFRAME` in the delay slot.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Arguments R4, R8, R12, then the stack (`DM(I6, M6)`). Result in R0 (F0; R0:R1 for 64-bit). Render kernels return nothing and write through pointers.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Callee-saved: R3, R5-R7, R9-R11, R13-R15, I0-I3, I5, M1-M3, B3.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Constant registers that voice code never writes: M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0, M14 = 1, M15 = -1. Indirect jumps use DAG2 (`JUMP (M13, I12)` relies on M13 = 0).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: The exception is the float divide `0x1c06ba` (plain CALL, R4/R8 in, F0 out). `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: Parameters: the ColdFire smooths them (one-pole) before the frame. The DSP converts s16 to float once per block (scale 1/32512) and ramps per sample by (new - old)/32 inside a block (/64 in DN2 FM operators).

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 4. SHARC calling convention of the stock code (selcc emits the same)
facts.text: DT2 sample machines and DN2 FM TONE render 64 samples at 96 kHz and decimate to 32 with a half-band filter.

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
facts.text: At H2/H3 SIMD is off and no DO loop is active. The stock FX state lives in DDR: chorus `0x80459388`, delay `0x8005912c` (rings of 524,288 floats, max 8 s), reverb `0x80000018`. FX rings wrap by index arithmetic; FX units never write B or L registers, but the voice renderer does and restores them. Static FX cost: chorus 7.1k, delay 6.0k, reverb 17.2k instructions per block. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 5. The DT2 audio chain per block (planar floats, 32 L then 32 R; voice blocks mono)
facts.text: The stock machines share almost no code (each machine is one large function). Only the post-voice chain and a few maths helpers are shared between DT2 and DN2. `[doc]`

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Clock and block: 1 GHz, 32 samples per block, 666,667 cycles nominal. Measured median per block: DT2 666,582, DN2 666,784 (digikit); DN2 666,706 (elekloader's idle-task meter); the owner's idle counter on a DT2 agrees. {digikit-f103} {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Core behaviour: 59 value items (saturation with MODE1.ALUSAT, the short and multifunction compute forms, float rounding) and all cycle snippets equal, including the L2 conflict loads (2,769 vs 2,803 cycles for 4,096 loads); the 6,694 RECIPS/RSQRTS seed results are equal. So the cycle budget of rule A35 and the float rules in [`../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md`](../devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md) section 6 hold on both. {digikit-f103} {digikit-f102}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Core registers set by the boot code: IMASK, MODE2, SHDBG_REVID, cache configuration (`SHL1C_CFG`) read the same on both. The traps armed (illegal opcode, L1 parity) are therefore the same. {digikit-f103}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Never store a DAG register through its own DAG (rule A33): hung a DT2 (Plaits port, digikit's "rung C"); the DN2 skill names the same pattern "the root cause of silent units" on its unit. {dt2-plaits} {dn2-skill-sharc}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Hardware loop ends in 48-bit ISA (rule A45): a DT2 froze at boot from a compressed loop end; stock DN2 1.11 obeys the rule in all 286 loops and the DN2 skill enforces it. {digikit-f91} {dn2-skill-scripts}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Decoded section 7 under 1 MiB (rule A46): the same 828-byte staging routine on DT2 1.16/1.17 and DN2 1.11/1.12; the overrun crashed a DT2. {digikit-f06} {dt2-lab-capicola}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: NaN or Inf in stock FX feedback silences everything until reboot: on a DT2 from an LFO at large depth on TUNE (digikit) and in the owner's builds; on a DN2 from never-written DDR, which powers on as garbage such as `0xFFFFFFFF` (the DN2 skill). Same failure, two triggers: guard every value you feed into a feedback path, and fill new DDR in emulator tests with `0xFFFFFFFF`. {digikit-f51} {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: Shared stock DSP code, by the bytes: the DT2's six wavetable render stages are in the DN2 image too. Three are byte-identical; in the other three every differing byte is a PC-relative call offset (same target) or one table-pointer literal. All call the same reciprocal helper at sw `0x1c06ba` in both images (RECIPS plus Newton steps, the helper behind A35's divide cost). A fix or measurement on one of these stages carries over. `[doc]` {digikit-f11}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. Shown on both units `[hw]`
facts.text: The unused frame tail carries DSP code on both (+23 instructions per block on DT2, +26 on DN2). `[doc]` {digikit-findings}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: SIMD loads and stores into L2 byte space hang the DSP (DT2, Plaits port; rule A33's second half). No DN2 report either way. {dt2-plaits}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: Instruction-cache misses are the largest stall class (33 % on the DT2 Plaits models), and L2 data lines 16 KiB apart thrash the 16 KiB cache. digikit's DN2 cycle snippets match, so plan DN2 kernels the same way. {dt2-plaits} {digikit-f103}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: ILOPI catches encodings the toolchain accepts (negative shift immediates, a 48-bit form of selas): seen on DN2 units. The DT2's IMASK is the same, and 70b185's DT2 rules already forbid the same encodings. {dn2-dspstop} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: L1 block 2 holds the PM data cache, so it is not free even though the image leaves it empty (DN2). The cache configuration register is the same on the DT2. {dn2-dspstop} {digikit-f103}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: The IIR0 and FIR0 accelerators compute in a different order from the hardware reference (IIR0 output from stored word 5, FIR0 sums added in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round in ACM). Read on a DN2; neither stock engine uses them. {dn2-accel}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 2. Silicon-level, seen on one unit, expected on the other
facts.text: DM and PM data caches are not coherent on DDR (a DN2 finding, applied as a rule on the DT2 without a DT2 test). `[doc]` {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
facts.text: Reply record: on the DT2 the SHARC writes two copies (`0x266220`, `0x267220`, picked by a selector), words 1-6 are rewritten by firmware and words 670-676 arrive untouched. On the DN2, reply word 2 is free on 1.12 (elekloader). These allocation results have not been checked on the other device; the record addresses differ with the image. {own-dt2-notes} {elekloader-sharc-dn2}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
facts.text: Diagnostic reply publication: digikit's DT2 probe received 0 in 3,995 of 4,000 diagnostic word-25 records. `[hw]` Its own `core/fx` and `core/dsp-voice` clears overwrote the previous block's reply word; removing those clears restored delivery in the DN2 1.12 emulator. The replacement keeps a static word and publishes at block tail. `[emu]` Finding 101 leaves silicon DMA timing unmeasured and says the new design had not yet run on a real DT2; it does not attribute the clears to stock firmware. {digikit-f101}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
facts.text: Free L2: DT2 problems start past `0x200f5a74` on a unit, although the static map shows free space up to `0x200fa000`. DN2: usable `0x20088400-0x200b0000` per the DN2 skill, and one block in L2 stopped a unit from starting. The two stock images load different amounts into L2 (`0x2001ab7c` vs `0x2008823c`), so each device needs its own limit. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-firmware}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
facts.text: Code in L2 "dead" stock FX spots stopped a DN2 at random moments (Digiwerk SC01); no DT2 test of the same idea. {dn2-cfw-roadmap}

facts.text: Per-sample stores into a stock DDR output buffer crashed a DT2; render into L2 and copy once. No DN2 test. {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 3. Firmware-level, one device only: check before relying on it
facts.text: The FreeRTOS layout (idle task, unused priorities 2-4 and 6) was measured on the DT2. The DN2 image has the same FreeRTOS files, but the addresses must be re-found. {own-dt2-notes} {digikit-sharcmap}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
facts.text: DSP DDR: on the DN2, `0x80531000-0xa0000000` (~507 MB) was never written in a fill-and-scan test on a unit. On the DT2 that range is the sample pool: its window runs from `0x8422b9c8` to `0x9d22b9c8`. Do not carry the DN2's "free DDR" over to the DT2. The DT2's SHARC image also zero-fills 32 MiB at `0x80a00000` and a `0x1c4`-byte control block at `0x82a00000` that the DN2 image lacks, and the SHARC functions that use them have no DN2 twin. {dn2-ddr} {dt2-lab-flex-mem} {dn2-drive}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
facts.text: How stock spends the block: the DN2 engine renders every voice every block (~63-65 % flat by dnfw's idle-task method, a held voice adds ~8k cycles; elekloader reads ~80 %, conflict O15). The DT2 engine scales with what plays and governs its own load: with 8 heavy tracks it ran at 99-100 % for whole windows and missed no block. Budgets measured on one device say nothing about the other. {dn2-sharcload} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
facts.text: What an overrun does: on the DT2 a late block is exactly one missed block, and even 54 provoked misses did not leave lasting damage. dn2mk2 users saw custom-voice overruns on the DN2 cut all audio until a power cycle. These are not the same experiment (sustained overload by added voices vs. single late blocks), so they do not contradict each other. A test that settles it: provoke single late blocks on a DN2 the way the DT2 test did. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2mk2-reports}

facts.section: Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 4. Different on the two devices
facts.text: Reply word 0: on the DT2 it is a true load figure, about 6.5k cycles below an idle-task measure. On the DN2 the DN2 skill uses it as the DSP load, while dnfw reads the frame handler's own count (~416k cycles) from it. Compare both methods on one DN2 before using word 0 there. {own-dt2-notes} {dn2-skill-emulators} {dn2-sharcload}

facts.text: Agents scan thousands of decompiled functions, infer roles (MIDI parsing, voice allocation), label symbols and draft hooks; they struggle on older DSP chips with little training data (hallucination risk). Developers run the real firmware in desktop emulators and let agents compile, boot, check for crashes and iterate many times per hour without touching hardware. `[?]` {dubspot}

facts.text: Disclosure practices: Felucca credits agents for code, tests, docs and maintenance; Schwung describes its code as largely agent-written under human review, requires AI-usage disclosure from contributors and bans Grok-generated pull requests; DT-FM and DNX disclose LLM use. elk-herd rejects AI-generated issues/PRs outright. `[doc]` {dubspot} {dt-fm} {dnx-page} {elk-herd}

facts.text: Agent files as "trap registers": examples quoted - the OLED y-axis runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader's `ev_draw` doc also says y=0 is the bottom row), and compiling ColdFire code with `-O2` without `-fno-ipa-sra` corrupts interrupt pointers. The repo that carries the second one is not named in the article. Treat both as rules to copy into any ColdFire/OLED work. `[?]` {dubspot} {elekloader-adapting}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
facts.text: Bricking is usually recoverable when the bootloader is untouched; the danger is projects that modify boot code or lack a documented recovery path. Subtle DSP/bus timing bugs are more likely to ruin a session than bricking. One mod developer bricked an Akai MPC Sample in September (video). Verified bricks in the wave are described as rare. `[?]`

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Failure modes
facts.text: Version lock-in: each mod targets exactly one OS build; official updates break mods until ported. Abandoned solo repos leave users stuck on old builds. Web patchers and installers run with full privileges and are rarely audited. `[?]`

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
facts.text: Elektron's 16 Sep policy bans sharing/requesting/linking to firmware mods, tools, repos or guides on Elektronauts and its social channels; a next-day amendment extended it to discontinued legacy machines; general discussion stays allowed; development moved to Discord, independent forums and GitHub (see the policy page itself in AGENT-RULES B4). `[doc]` {elektronauts-policy}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Legal and policy points as the article describes them (not legal advice)
facts.text: Developers distribute patches or scripts, not firmware, and warn users not to share compiled `.syx`/`.bin` outputs. The article cites US DMCA section 1201 exemptions (research, repair, interoperability; active through October 2027, generally not distribution) and the EU Software Directive's narrow interoperability allowance; neither has been tested over a music-hardware mod. Paid firmware (Groove OS, $29) and unlocking paid features on current hardware raise legal risk; first takedowns are expected for commercial mods. Warranty: expect denial for faults caused by third-party firmware, depending on country. `[?]` {dubspot}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
facts.text: Tool: build `make`; Linux/macOS native, Windows via WSL (work in the Linux home directory, a filename in the tool repo contains `?`). Commands: `-i` summary + checksum check, `-v` detail, `-o dir` extract all, `-d ID` extract one section, `-c ID file -o new.syx` replace a section and repack, `-r` repack unchanged (self-test), `-V` version string, `-l 0..3` compression level, `--emit-container`. Sound/pattern/project dumps are `.syx` too but the tool rejects them as non-firmware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
facts.text: The Digitone II 1.11 example file has 18,668 SysEx messages, 8-in-7 encoding, per-packet checksums, a container with model/version/overall checksum and an HMAC-SHA256 signature the tool recomputes on repack. Section 3 (MAIN OS) is the usual target; leave 2 (bootstrap) and 4 (updater) alone because the bootloader holds the recovery menu; section 8 appears as `?` (no known name); section IDs differ on other devices, so `-i` is authoritative. `.raw` sections are copied as-is, `.bin` sections are decompressed. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

facts.section: Ecosystem lessons - how the 2026 custom-firmware wave is built, verified and what goes wrong / Safe byte-level editing rules (elektronmods tutorial by the forum admin, using elektron-firmware-tool)
facts.text: Editing rules: overwrite bytes only, the file size must not change (later addresses shift); replacement text must be the same length and use characters already present; keep the terminating zero byte; always edit a copy in `work/` and keep `extracted/` untouched; verify with `cmp -l` (exactly the intended number of changed bytes) and by re-extracting section 3 from the new file and comparing it byte-for-byte; `-V` must not exceed the original version string length (e.g. 4 characters like `1.11`). The repacked file is smaller than Elektron's because the tool compresses slightly better (level 3 took ~14 s, level 0 is ~18x faster and ~3 % larger). The author states the worked example (replacing "UNTITLED" with "ELEKMODS") was not tested on hardware. `[doc]` {em-tutorial}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
facts.text: Digitakt II: section 2 = bootstrap, section 4 = updater (never modify); the DSP program is an ADI boot stream in section 7; ElekLabs digikit's patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8.

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
facts.text: Section 7 is a stream of ADI boot records (the ADSP-2156x hardware reference, boot chapter). Each header is four little-endian uint32s: block code, target, byte count, argument. The block code's top byte is `0xad`; its byte at offset 2 makes the XOR of all 16 header bytes zero; its low 16 bits are flags: `0x0001` LOAD (copy `count` bytes to the target), `0x0101` FILL (fill with the argument), `0x5001` FIRST + IGNORE (starts a boot image; target = entry in PC16, argument = distance from the end of this header to the next FIRST), `0x0801` INIT and `0x8001` FINAL (end the image and the stream). Later loads overwrite earlier ones in order, and stock relies on that (15 overlapping loads and fills on DN2 1.12). To add code, insert records before FINAL and grow only the last FIRST's argument and XOR byte; dt2-machine-lab used FILL records to keep a decoded stream under the size limit below. `[doc]` {elekloader-sharc-boot} {dt2-lab-capicola}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections
facts.text: Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
facts.text: What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re}

Against that: the DN2, Rytm and A4 operating systems carry their own panel firmware inside MAIN and re-flash the panel from there.

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Preamble of the decoded byte stream: u32 container size + u32 content checksum, then the container (magic at offset 8). Container size: DN2 1,743,120, DN1 1,102,352 (the sizes of the file pair dnfw analysed). The content checksum is not a standard algorithm: a running 32-bit sum over big-endian words, each word XORed with its one-based index; trailing bytes that do not fill a word are excluded. Compressed sections carry a header with the stream length and a u32 sum of the stream bytes (padding excluded). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Trailer: the last 32 bytes of the declared container are an HMAC-SHA256 on the first 16-byte boundary at least 4 bytes past the last section (gap zeroed); it covers everything before it, padding included; the key is derived from material inside the image (a printable string in a decompressed section, found in the bootstrap, plus a fixed constant) - never edit that key material, the device likely verifies with its installed copy. DN1 1.42A is unsigned (trailer all zeros). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: Compression: each section is raw or aPLib-variant compressed (not flagged - inferred by whether the bytes depack): LZ77 with interlaced Elias-gamma codes, a biased offset, a last-offset reuse code and a length bonus for far matches, minimum match 2; Elektron's streams keep the furthest match within 1 MiB and the longest at 2,048 bytes. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: DN1 vs DN2: bootstrap load address DN2 `0x02000000` / DN1 `0x02000800`; blob (id 7) compressed on DN2, raw on DN1; boot (id 6) absent on DN2, present (raw) on DN1; section 5 (meta) is 15 bytes, stored raw, no destination address, identical size on both; section 8 appears in OS 1.11 compressed (it is the Outbox 8 accessory firmware). `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {dn2-cfw-handoff}

facts.section: Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
facts.text: After patching, recompute: re-encoded section data and its stream length/sum (+ padding to 4 bytes, table length includes the padding), section table offsets/lengths and 16-byte placement (and the count if sections change), the preamble (container size, content checksum), SysEx packet checksums/counters/packet count, and on DN2 the HMAC over everything before the trailer. The page does not say whether the product code, build string or version string must change, nor whether ids must be renumbered. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
facts.text: MIDI DIN runs at 31,250 baud, about 3,125 bytes/s; a 2,209,184-byte image needs at least ~12 minutes (derived, not timed). Do not interrupt. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / Numbers
facts.text: Nothing is written until reception completes. The receiver has no error recovery: a bad sequence number or checksum freezes the progress bar with no message and no retransmit. Checksums and sequence counters are content-independent, so the receiver cannot tell a modified image from stock. `[doc]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem
facts.text: Reported 2026-09-11: Transfer showed 100 % sent while the device bar froze near 80 %; stock 1.10E stalled over the same route, so the link was at fault, not the image. Root cause in that case: a Focusrite Scarlett 4i4's MIDI went idle mid-transfer and dropped packets; the stall point varied (30/70/80 %). `[hw]` {dn2-flashing}

facts.section: Flash procedure and link pitfalls (Digitone II, as practised by dn2mk2 and dnfw) / The "stalls at ~80 %" problem
facts.text: Fixes: prove the link with the stock firmware first; use a dedicated class-compliant USB-MIDI cable for long recovery transfers; disable Windows USB selective suspend and device power management; retry. `[hw]` {dn2-flashing} {dn2mk2-safety}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: CPU fingerprint: NXP MCF5441x (ColdFire V4m with EMAC) - UART8 `0xEC070000`, GPIO `0xEC094000`, eDMA `0xFC044000` (TCDs +0x1000), INTC0-2 `0xFC048000/0xFC04C000/0xFC050000`, DSPI0 `0xFC05C000`, PIT0-3 `0xFC080000-0xFC08C000`, EPORT `0xFC090000`. Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: DDR is 128 MiB (DDRMC writes in the bootstrap; earlier 64 MiB claims are wrong): `0x40000000-0x47FFFFFF` cached (ACR0), `0x48000000-0x4FFFFFFF` an uncached alias of the same DDR used for DMA buffers; reset SP `0x48000000`; 32 MiB C++ heap above `0x44000000`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: NOR flash 16 MiB, S25FL127S-class (RDID mfg 0x01, id 0x2018); the bootstrap's flash loop uses 512-byte pages and 256 KB erase blocks. The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: UART8 receive is done by eDMA (channel 34), not by reading the data register - an emulator must model eDMA, not just the UART. `[emu]` {digikit-f08}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: eMMC part table: DT2 1.16 (`0x402b4a24`) and DN2 1.10E/1.11 (`0x4029f554`) accept the same seven 32-byte entries: Kingston parts `TX2932` and `TS0A32`, both 32 GB, matching the Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 on a DN2 board photo. Shared ColdFire storage code: the block driver, the MmcFs slot store and the transfer routing; the sample filesystem, its request handler and the sample manager are DT2-only. `[doc]` {dn2-drive}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: eMMC card (both, about 32 GB part, 0x2E1A000 sectors assumed): sectors `0x0-0x457FFF` belong to the firmware (boot, tables, projects, pools, presets); MmcFs refuses writes at `0x457FFF` and above. DT2 1.17: factory sample table "MaGj" at `0x458000` and 1,265 factory samples to `0x5D7FFF` - never touch; +Drive (ekFS) `0x5D8000-0x2DF017F`; `0x2DF0180` to the end unused. DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. Unchecked bank ids in the Data API can reach every sector below `0x800000` over USB - put any private store above that line (digikit: DT2 `0x2DF1000+`, DN2 `0x800000+`). Not checked on a real card. `[doc]` {digikit-f59}

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
facts.text: Card pools inside the firmware area (MmcFs) `[emu]` {digikit-samples}: Fixed slots: projects 0-127 (16 MiB each on both), sounds 0-2047 (DT2 4 KiB, DN2 1 KiB), kits 0-1023 (DT2 64 KiB, DN2 32 KiB). The bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect padlocks, not occupancy. The boot project (magic "COKi") has two copies at sectors `0x40000` and `0x48000`. The working project is at `0x50000` and is rewritten from the boot copy at every start. The DT2 has a path filesystem (ekFS +Drive) for samples. The DN2 has none: only the MmcFs pools. Card layouts are device data (digikit `devices/<device>.toml`).

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: RAM aliases every `0x08000000`: a byte answers at nine addresses up to `0x8c000000`. ACR0 caches only the first window, and stock reaches its DMA buffers through the second (`0x4e......`). Scan all nine windows before you call RAM unreferenced. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Flashed bytes above the reset clear do not survive a reset (DT2 1.16 clears from `0x40312000`; on the DN2 about 3,200 B separate the end of MAIN OS from the clear). Code placed there must be copied up by a loader *after* the clear. digikit, dnfw and elekloader all do this. `[hw]` (bytes lost on a DT2)

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: The DN2's code region has no free run of even 24 bytes. Zero runs exist in the constants region, and code there does execute (a boot-path cave printed "CAVE RAN!!!" on a real DN2). One "free" run was an array the code fills at run time: patching it crashed the unit, and the emulator watch read zeros. Two static checks catch most cases: a fixed stride between equal gaps marks an array, and `lea`/`pea`/`move.l #` operands mark referenced space. On 1.11 only 13 runs (4,207 B) pass both, not the "~29 KB" first assumed. `[hw]` ([I19](../INCIDENTS.md#i19-patching-a-free-zero-run-crashed-the-unit))

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Displaced stock instructions are replayed at another address, so no PC-relative instructions in the displaced bytes. Pick hook sites whose first instructions are absolute. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / ColdFire code caves and mod RAM (dnfw `code-caves.md`, `mod-memory-regions.md`, DN2 1.11)
facts.text: dnfw's mods take fixed RAM chunks in `0x46700000-0x47fe0000` (waverider 436 KB at `0x4670c000`/`0x467f0000`/`0x46a00000`, lfo4 `0x46800000`/`0x46900000`, ...). The alternative is the stock 32 MiB buddy heap (`0x4464abf0`), where the allocator records the use but a 12.9 MB project load takes half. Mods that store settings in unused pattern bits must not claim the same bits. `[doc]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Stock does not touch `0x46710000-0x47ffffcc` in emulation. Three independent checks agree: dn2-cfw's write watches over `0x46800000-0x47f00000`, elekloader's canary over `0x46710000-0x48000000` (cold boot, two panel sessions), and digikit's reference scan (`0x4671a000-0x47fe0000` unreferenced, [`dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md)). All three ran in an emulator, so rule A43 (canary on a unit) still applies. `[emu]`

facts.section: Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Digitone II: who uses the RAM above the reset clear (compared across five projects, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The range from `0x46700000` up to `0x46710000` is not free. On 1.12 it holds the end of the DMA buffers; on 1.11 the MMC bounce buffer reaches `0x46701300`. dnfw's lfo4 state sat at `0x46700000` until 2026-10-11 and corrupted every project saved on an LFO4 unit (the bounce buffer carries each piece of a project on save and load); it now lives in the first block of stock's heap (`0x4464abf0`). dnfw's remaining `0x4670xxxx` chunks (from `0x46708000`) are above the 1.11 DMA section (`0x466b8000-0x46701340`) but inside the 1.12 one, so they must move for a 1.12 port. The "25.3 MB unclaimed above BSS" figure in dnfw's memory map missed these alias references. The skill's "`0x46700000..0x46900000` unused, hardware-confirmed" disagrees: see [CONFLICTS S17](../CONFLICTS.md). `[doc]`

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
facts.text: The menu route sends no SysEx reply at all; only the screen shows progress. Pace by time: digikit uses 128-byte messages every 2 ms (about 29 s DT2, 37 s DN2) - 12x slower than the emulated ceiling; not run on hardware.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Acknowledgement and buffering
facts.text: The whole container is staged in RAM; flash is untouched until the last message. A transfer cut before the footer leaves the screen on "Receiving" and nothing validated, erased or written. Power loss during the flash phase leaves the container area partly erased; the bootstrap (`0x40000`) is never written by this path, so FUNC boot menu and DIN OS UPGRADE stay usable (emulated).

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
facts.text: No "UPGRADE OS NOW?" on the menu route in the emulator: the delegate returns "do not ask", so after the last message the screen goes ERASING FLASH... -> SUCCESS! REBOOTING -> reset with no key pressed. Real hardware may differ (no derived delegate class was found). NO while receiving asks "CANCEL OS UPGRADE?".

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Validation (before any erase; run up to three times)
facts.text: The flash writer ignores erase/program return codes - "Success" is shown whatever the chips did. It erases sector by sector from flash `0x80000` (default sector 0x10000) and programs 0x100-byte pages, waits 3 s, soft-resets via `0x80 -> 0xec090000`.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Prefer the RPC route with explicit End; send End 0 on every abort. Do not resend Writes blindly; a failed run costs only a new Start.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: A "Success!" screen does not prove the flash was written correctly - verify by version string / behaviour after reboot.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Never rely on the in-OS path for recovery; it needs a working MAIN OS. The bootstrap route (DIN) is the recovery.

facts.section: How Digitakt II and Digitone II take an OS update from the running OS (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / Rules that follow
facts.text: Digitone II has no build floor in the validator - an older signed image is accepted; Digitakt II refuses builds below 0060.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Controller: MCF5441x USB OTG at `0xFC0B0000`, device mode, external ULPI PHY, high speed (480 Mb/s; descriptors have 512-byte bulk packets; DEVICE_QUALIFIER stalled = HS-only). Only endpoints EP0-EP3 exist. VID `0x1935`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Modes -> descriptors: USB MIDI PID `0x012b` (EP1 bulk pair, 2 cables); USB AUDIO/MIDI PID `0x102b` (UAC2 iso on EP2/EP3 + MIDI on EP1); OVERBRIDGE PID `0x0b2b` (vendor class 0xFF: interrupt EP3 in/out, EP2 OUT bulk 512 + EP2 IN interrupt 64, plus MIDI on EP1); a service mode PID `0xffff` with CDC-ACM. No MS-OS/BOS descriptors - Windows will not bind WinUSB on its own. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: In USB AUDIO/MIDI mode on the DT2/DN2 EP2 OUT is unused; digikit adds a bulk OUT interface there at boot. `[hw]` {digikit-f123-bulk}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: SysEx throughput is limited by the ColdFire's per-byte handling (about 32 instructions per wire byte just to split USB-MIDI events, two 512-byte receive buffers in flight); digikit estimates 0.8-1.4 MB/s at best for an own SysEx route. Transfer's file-write RPC: OpenFileForWrite `0x40`, WriteFileV1 `0x42` (handle, length, offset, data), CloseFileWriter `0x41`. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / USB device side of Digitakt II / Digitone II (digikit finding 42, static, DT2 1.16)
facts.text: Samples are not converted on the device: the native file is a 0x40-byte header (+1 stereo flag, +4 length, +8 rate 48000) + big-endian int16 PCM + 16-byte trailer; no WAV parser in the image. The host must resample to 48 kHz and convert. `[doc]` {digikit-f42}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
facts.text: The container's 4-byte version field (header `+0x14`, `1.12` on stock) is sent to the computer by the main OS. A build that writes its own name there (e.g. `CMP1`) makes the Overbridge plugin answer "Device is not running compatible OS Version" and fail to open. The engine itself connects; the refusal comes from the plugin. `[hw]`

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Fix: patch the two main-OS sites that send the version so they send a header copy with `1.12`. The flash and the power-on screen keep the build's name. Overbridge and Transfer work again on the unit (2026-10-22). `[hw]`

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Overbridge refuses a mod whose version field changed (Digiwerk OB01, DN2 1.12)
facts.text: Rule: keep the version field the device expects, or patch only what is sent out. Overbridge logs on macOS: `~/Library/Logs/Elektron Overbridge/`.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / What this means for development
facts.text: Overbridge works over a class-compliant-looking USB link with Elektron-specific framing; a firmware mod that changes audio routing, channel counts or the USB descriptor could break Overbridge. dn2-cfw's builds show "incompatible OS version" in Overbridge (open issue), so Overbridge compatibility is checked against the OS version/build - plan for it. `[doc]` {dn2-cfw-roadmap}

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / What this means for development
facts.text: Unknown: the USB class/endpoints, the control channel carrying parameters, and whether the Heat's internal DSP/CPU architecture resembles any other Elektron box. Reading Overwitch's source and `dtdump` would answer the first two.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1 with a Raspberry Pi as host (digitakt-sidecar-pi, OS 1.54)
facts.text: Alt setting 3: interrupt endpoint `0x83` IN, 368 bytes, and `0x03` OUT, 88 bytes. Seven frames per packet, a 32-byte header and big-endian int32 words, with input data 24-bit in 32-bit words. The measured cadence is 47,999.5 frames/s.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1 with a Raspberry Pi as host (digitakt-sidecar-pi, OS 1.54)
facts.text: A four-minute stream (1.6 M packets each way) ran with zero gaps, short packets or USB errors, on Linux and on a bare-metal (Circle) host.

facts.section: Overbridge over USB (what Overwitch's README reveals) - the only deep source on Analog Heat +FX so far / Confirmed on a Digitakt mk1 with a Raspberry Pi as host (digitakt-sidecar-pi, OS 1.54)
facts.text: Host-observed analog round trip: 5.3-6.0 ms (median 5.7 ms), including Linux scheduling and the analog loop. `[hw]`

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
facts.text: A mod can break the normal USB update path without anyone noticing until the next update. On Overtone 1.0 (Digitone II), an OS sent with Transfer stopped at "Receiving" or "PREPARING..." and wrote nothing. The only way off it was the STARTUP menu over DIN, about 15 minutes. Test "install the next build over USB" as part of every release (rule A36). `[hw]` {overtone} ([I22](../INCIDENTS.md#i22-a-mod-broke-the-normal-usb-update-path))

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Rules of thumb (all from the sources above)
facts.text: Test your DIN interface before you need it. On a DT2, a generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) delivered nothing, while a controller's DIN out worked. Cheap cable adapters are known to drop or mangle long SysEx; a stock-OS dry run with your exact cable is the only proof. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} ([I44](../INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing))

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research `RECOVERY.md`): keep an official stock `.syx`, a physical MIDI interface and cable ready; MIDI OUT of the interface to the Digitakt II's MIDI IN (USB MIDI cannot be used); hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; in Elektron Transfer open the SYSEX TRANSFER page and choose "OS upgrade via device startup menu"; select the stock file and keep power on until the unit reboots. No durations are given and the author states recovery is not guaranteed if the startup menu or bootloader cannot run, power is lost during a critical write, or storage/hardware is damaged; the page reports no hardware test of the procedure. `[doc]` {dt2-recovery}

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery}

facts.section: Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)
facts.text: Other Elektron devices, from elekloader's BUILDING.md (for reference): Analog Rytm MKII and Analog Four MKII - FUNC at power-on (STARTUP menu), TRIG 4, stock `.syx` over 5-pin DIN MIDI, USB does not work. Octatrack - hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 3 = MIDI UPGRADE, DIN MIDI; normal flashing from the card (PROJECT > SYSTEM > USB DISK MODE, copy the `.bin`, then PROJECT > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE, power-cycle once more before judging). Digitakt mk1 / Digitone mk1: FUNC, TRIG 4, legacy mode; the connection is not stated for these two. Per-device notes: [`analog-rytm.md`](../devices/analog-rytm.md), [`digitakt.md`](../devices/digitakt.md), [`digitone.md`](../devices/digitone.md). `[doc]` {elekloader-building}

Recovery from such a stall is a power cycle and the startup menu. `[hw]` {overtone} {dt2-install} ([I23](../INCIDENTS.md#i23-plaits-builds-failed-normal-transfer-updates-at-preparing))

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Digitone mk1 device ID is `0x0D`; its pattern format differs from Digitone II and SYXGRID rejects it. The DN2's is `0x15`. All known device bytes: [firmware-container.md](firmware-container.md#sysex-device-byte-per-device-merged-from-the-projects-that-decode-these-files). `[doc]` {syxgrid}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Two protocol generations: the Digitakt II / Digitone II speak "gen-2"; Analog Four speaks "gen-1" with a different pattern format and a slower wire. `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Digitone II library contains Digitone mk1 preset files, which use a second container format (refuse foreign formats by magic bytes). `[doc]` {digi-roll-studio}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Framing and encoding
facts.text: Container structure and checksums for older machines are best documented in libanalogrytm (Analog Rytm only; no Analog Heat); the frame, packing and checksum match the newer devices, the type bytes do not (section "Dump messages and device ids across generations" below). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: One dump frame for every generation compared: `F0 00 20 3C <device> <dev id> <type> 01 01 <index> <packed payload> <checksum hi lo> <count hi lo> F7`. The Rytm writes the same `01 01` version field ("OS 1.02c" in libanalogrytm), the same index byte and the same trailer. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The same 7-bit packing: groups of one header byte plus up to 7 data bytes; header bit 6 holds the MSB of the first data byte, bit 0 that of the seventh; a short last group keeps its header. syxgrid's DN2 field "control byte 101506, mask `0x40`, payload 101507" is exactly this rule (first byte of a group). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The same checksum and count: checksum = sum of the packed payload bytes (header bytes included) mod 2^14, sent as two 7-bit bytes, high first; count = packed length + 5 (checksum, count and `F7`), also mod 2^14. syxgrid recomputed the checksum over raw bytes `[10, 114113)` and matched the DN2's own on every fixture. A DN2 pattern message is 114,118 bytes, so its count field wraps; tools must not use it as a length. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Requests: an empty payload, trailer `00 00 00 05` (checksum 0, count 5) on both generations; the Rytm's request is 15 bytes, `F0 00 20 3C 07 00 <id> 01 01 <nr> 00 00 00 05 F7`. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: The index byte on receive: a DN2 stores a received pattern in the slot armed on the device, not in the index the message carries (syxgrid, on a unit). libanalogrytm does not say what a Rytm does with it. `[hw]` {syxgrid-map}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: Device byte in dumps: Rytm (libanalogrytm's era, MKI) `0x07`; Digitakt `0x0A`; Digitakt II `0x14`; Digitone II `0x15`. A DN2 answered only `0x15` in a sweep and ignored `0x0B-0x0E`, `0x14` and `0x16`. The same bytes appear in the OS files ([`firmware-container.md`](firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} Three different device ids. They are easy to mix up, and the same number means different devices in different namespaces:

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
facts.text: `0x14` is the Digitakt II's SysEx byte but the Digitone mk1's product id; `0x0A` is the Digitakt's SysEx byte but the Analog Heat's product id. Name the namespace whenever you write an id down.

facts.text: Elektroid reads the product id from byte 5 of the decoded `Device` (Ping) reply and looks it up in its device table; digi-roll captured 42 and 43 from a DT2 and a DN2 the same way. The FAQ table on elektron.se (Heat `000A`, Digitakt `000C`, Digitone `0014`, Heat MKII `0016`, Model:Samples `0019`, Model:Cycles `001B`, Digitone Keys `001C`) matches Elektroid's table entry for entry, so that table lists product ids. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {digi-roll-protocol} {elektron-faq}

Overwitch's Overbridge ids: Analog Four MKII `0x0B47`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x0B48`, Digitone Keys `0x0B35`, Syntakt `0x0B4A`. digikit read the DT2's USB ids from the image: `0x012B` (USB MIDI), `0x102B` (audio/MIDI), `0x0B2B` (Overbridge), so the low byte is shared across modes. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {overwitch-devices} {digikit-f42}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Message: product byte `0x15`, message type `0x50` (pattern). A pattern dump is 114,118 bytes. The body from raw byte 10 to 114113 is 7-bit packed (one control byte per 7 payload bytes); "decoded" offsets below are into the unpacked payload.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Slot: raw byte 9 is the slot the device dumped from (0 = A01 ... 127 = H16), not a destination. A received pattern is stored in the slot armed on the device, advancing by one per pattern.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Step states: at decoded `4 + 1187*(track-1) + 2*(step-1)`, two bytes per step, 16 tracks x 128 steps. Odd-step trig `03 81`, even-step trig `03 91`. `03 90` / `03 80` (bit 0 clear) is not an occupied step. First byte `0x78` = trigless trig (parameter automation, no note).

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Trigger records: at decoded `18996`, 6 bytes each, up to 8,192 records. Fields: track, step, note, velocity (`0xFF` = track default), length index (`0xFF` = inherit), and a signed micro-timing byte (1/384 note, -23..+23). A record is free when its track byte is `0xFF`; nothing terminates the table, so skip and keep scanning. Chords are stored as all primary notes first, then all chord extras.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II pattern dump: hardware-confirmed offsets (syxgrid's map v1.13.0, CC BY 4.0, facts restated)
facts.text: Track type bitmask at decoded `99348-99349`, big-endian, bit i = track i+1, 1 = MIDI track.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
facts.text: Remote control without touching the UART: the firmware's button decoder `f(channel, new_mask)` (DT2 1.17 `0x4011e318`, DN2 1.12 `0x4011fc8c`) and encoder decoder `f(encoder0, delta)` (`0x4011e598` / `0x4011ff0c`) can be called from a mod. Mask SR to `0x2700` around the call; the decoders do unprotected read-modify-write. Neither checks the channel (safe: buttons 0-6, encoders 0-8). An encoder turn is ignored for 40 ticks after its click key is released. `[emu]`

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
facts.text: DIN MIDI runs on UART9 (`0xec074000`, 31,250 baud, receive by eDMA channel 36). The front panel talks over UART8 (`0xec070000`). Panel key codes used by emulators: SETTINGS 8, FUNC 17, YES 10, NO 12, UP 11, DOWN 14, LEFT 13, RIGHT 15. `[emu]`

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
facts.text: Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio}

facts.text: NRPN groups (Digitakt II, MCP project): MSB 1 = track/trig/source/filter/amp, MSB 2 = FX, MSB 3 = trig note/velocity/length. Sample select is NRPN MSB 1 / LSB 3 per one forum user, who found that sample-slot control by NRPN looked broken and that a separate "sample slot" + "bank" CC pair may be the real route. `[?]` {digitakt-midi-mcp} {elektronauts-dt2-sample-slot}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Rules for agents
facts.text: Never write to a unit's storage with an unverified format: back up via Transfer first, work on throwaway projects, read back and compare.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Rules for agents
facts.text: Treat every "best-guess" request format as unsafe until you have captured the real traffic with a MIDI monitor.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Rules for agents
facts.text: Do not use libraries that parse a different device generation (Digitone mk1 vs II, Analog Four gen-1 vs gen-2) - the formats differ.

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Elektroid (dagargo) - a general sample/SysEx client
facts.text: Supported (README list): Analog Four MKI/MKII/Keys, Analog Heat MKI/MKII/+FX, Analog Rytm MKI/MKII, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Model:Cycles/Samples, Monomachine MKII, Syntakt, plus non-Elektron gear (Arturia, Casio CZ-101, Eventide, KORG, MFB, Moog, Novation, MIDI SDS samplers). No per-device capability table; `elektroid-cli info <device>` shows the compatible filesystems. `[doc]` {elektroid-readme}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Elektroid (dagargo) - a general sample/SysEx client
facts.text: Connectors: `system` (local computer, for format conversion), `elektron`, `cz`, `sds`, `efactor_preset`. Elektron filesystem families: raw/sample (`raw`, `preset-raw`, `sample`), data (`data`, `project`, `preset`, `preset-takt-ii`, `sound`), memory (`ram`, `track`). The Digitakt II "Preset" filesystem is implemented as `preset-takt-ii`. `raw` and `data` are for testing only and not compatible with Transfer formats. A firmware `upgrade` command exists in the CLI (which devices is not stated). Device definitions come from `~/.config/elektroid/elektron/devices.json` if present. Elektron samples cannot be swapped. `[doc]` {elektroid-readme}

facts.section: SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Elektroid (dagargo) - a general sample/SysEx client
facts.text: Backends: ALSA MIDI and PulseAudio by default on Linux, RtMidi/RtAudio elsewhere. 2,506 commits, 19 open issues; no version shown on the page (altstrument lists v3.4, 2026-08-22).

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: selache pitfalls that halt a real DSP but run in the emulator (elekloader ADAPTING.md, Nov 2026; the first matches 70b185's DT2 finding): A shift by a negative immediate (`LSHIFT R1 BY -16`) is encoded without sign extension. Put the count in a register (`R2 = -16; R1 = LSHIFT R1 BY R2;`). elekloader's lint flags candidates, but it cannot see instruction boundaries, so check each one in the listing. A C function whose locals sit more than ~63 words from the frame pointer is compiled wrongly. One large local array is enough. Keep large buffers static or in the voice state. `[hw]` {elekloader-adapting} {own-dt2-notes}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: Two projects compared selache's VISA decoder with digikit's table decoder on the DN2 stock program, and agree on where each is wrong. The test: walk instruction by instruction between known starts (branch targets, `cjump` sites, DO-loop ends) and see who lands exactly. `[doc]` {dn2-selache} {dn2-cfw-t31} selache's disassembler gives some 48-bit forms as 32-bit (Type 3a `59be`, Type 4a `6a3e`, Type 7a `043e`, Type 16a `9980`) and one 32-bit form as 48-bit (Type 3b `593e`); DO-loop ends land on the table decoder's starts 85 of 85 times, on selache's 64 of 85, and selache prints most DO offsets with bit 23 set. digikit's table had Type 2b wrong (the programming guide's `000000011`, not the reference's `110000000`; selache won 119 to 0) and wrongly ruled out `Type10a_rel` in VISA; both fixed in digikit#31. Its `undoc16/48` forms are still provisional. A two-byte-late start still lands 94.9 % of spans, because VISA resynchronises within a few instructions. A decoder's score means something only against that control.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Compilers and builders
facts.text: Disassembled text is not a patch format. 11,440 distinct encodings from the DN2's L2 program, each disassembled with selmap and reassembled alone with selas: 83.9 % came back identical; 1,265 kept their width but lost register fields the text does not show (`bitrev`, `modify`, `dm` moves); 216 changed width; 320 printed forms could not be parsed; 40 crashed the assembler. A 48-bit `nop` reassembles as the 16-bit one. Patch from source, and compare bytes (rule A41). `[doc]` {dn2-selache}

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Shift immediates only reach 8. A shift by 14 or 15 costs a `moveq` plus a register shift; a shift by 16 is `swap` (+ `ext.l`). Arrange fixed-point products to land on a 16-bit boundary (e.g. store tables as unsigned Q16 so that `(s*w16) >> 16` equals `(s*w15) >> 15` exactly).

facts.text: Prove the bounds once per block, then run a loop without checks, with state in locals. Keep the checked loop as the fallback near buffer ends.

facts.text: Mark hot loops `noinline`: an inlined, merged loop kept a branch inside and spilled to the stack (~45 instructions per sample). `do { } while (--n)` saves the count test.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Specialise on loop-invariant cases: unity-speed grains skip interpolation (13 vs ~26 instructions per sample); a cached per-voice window table replaces per-sample shape blending.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: EMAC in fractional mode (MACSR `0x20`: signed fractional, truncating, no saturation): save and restore MACSR, ACC0 and ACCEXT01, and clear ACC0 first. Bit-exact Python models must truncate each product as `floor(x*y/2^23)`, keeping 8 bits below the LSB.

facts.section: Toolchains and emulators / Writing fast ColdFire C (digigrain's measured notes, Digitakt mk1, gcc `-mcpu=54455 -O2`)
facts.text: Hooks must preserve every register the caller relies on. Real bugs: a chord hook missed a4-a6, a callee clobbered a0, and a restoring `movem` lost a decision kept in d7. Test hooks with a stub that junks all scratch registers.
